BiaD9zBnSY.one_liner: Derives optimal time complexities and matching methods (Grace SGD, Leon SGD) for nonconvex decentralized optimization under bandwidth constraints.
BiaD9zBnSY.problem: A realistic decentralized setup with bandwidth-constrained communication lacks optimal time complexities for non-convex stochastic parallel and asynchronous optimization.
BiaD9zBnSY.method: They derive optimal time complexities, up to logarithmic factors, for homogeneous and heterogeneous settings, characterized by min-cut/max-flow quantities, and develop the matching methods Grace SGD and Leon SGD. The analysis uses Gomory-Hu trees and Steiner Tree Packing.
BiaD9zBnSY.key_idea: Express the time complexity through min-cut/max-flow quantities of the network and use Gomory-Hu trees and Steiner tree packing to select workers and communication schemes.
BiaD9zBnSY.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds, where the lower bounds assume zero-respecting algorithms; no experiments are stated.
BiaD9zBnSY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives provably optimal algorithms under a realistic bandwidth-constrained model, with a protocol that unifies gossip and AllReduce communication and graph-theoretic tools that make the results practical.
BiaD9zBnSY.main_concern: One reviewer found errors in the lower-bound proofs (for example the probability computations for the sampled index subset), while the others asked only for added citations and proofreading.

1UMm9d7raH.one_liner: LLM-driven evolutionary search with a MAP-Elites archive produces domain-independent C++ planning heuristics
1UMm9d7raH.problem: Hand-engineered domain-independent planning heuristics took decades to build, and LLM-synthesized heuristics so far work only for a single domain.
1UMm9d7raH.method: LLMs propose code mutations to C++ heuristics, a MAP-Elites archive keyed by informedness and evaluation speed maintains diversity, and fitness blends coverage with solving time. The evolved programs are ordinary C++ that can be integrated into existing planners such as LAMA.
1UMm9d7raH.key_idea: Evolve C++ heuristic programs via LLM-proposed mutations, keeping a MAP-Elites archive keyed by informedness and evaluation speed, with fitness mixing coverage and solving time.
1UMm9d7raH.evidence: Benchmarked against nineteen hand-engineered heuristics on held-out domains, with blind versus FF seeding comparisons and integration of two evolved heuristics into LAMA.
1UMm9d7raH.claimed_gains: Combining two evolved heuristics inside LAMA solves 50 more held-out tasks and yields a 1.11× speedup to the first plan, and the best evolved heuristic outperforms all of the baselines on held-out domains.
1UMm9d7raH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it yields reusable domain-independent heuristics that transfer to held-out domains, integrate into existing planners, and are evaluated against 19 hand-engineered baselines.
1UMm9d7raH.main_concern: The contribution beyond optimizing FF is unclear because the evolutionary components (MAP-Elites, islands, LLM pool) are not ablated, and the heuristics carry no admissibility guarantees.

Gsk2rxmUh6.one_liner: Three-stage dynamical analysis of weight decay in two-layer ReLU networks: rapid fitting, amplitude compression, neuron condensation
Gsk2rxmUh6.problem: The role of weight decay in neuron condensation, meaning parameter direction alignment, remains unclear.
Gsk2rxmUh6.method: Starting from a neural tangent kernel regime initialization, the paper analyzes a residual correlation field that governs neuron amplitudes and directions in a two-layer ReLU network, and bounds the drift of its attracting extrema to show contraction of neuron directions around them.
Gsk2rxmUh6.key_idea: Weight decay keeps a residual correlation field nonzero and amplifies it as the kernel decays, so its few attracting extrema pull neuron directions together.
Gsk2rxmUh6.evidence: Theoretical derivations for a two-layer ReLU network from NTK-regime initialization (reviewers note one-dimensional inputs and gradient flow), with toy, synthetic and Transformer experiments.
Gsk2rxmUh6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the angular analysis interesting and coherent, showing weight decay affects neuron directions beyond shrinking parameter norms, with well-supported derivations and clear presentation.
Gsk2rxmUh6.main_concern: The theory covers only one-dimensional inputs, two-layer ReLU networks and gradient flow, and empirical evidence for realistic settings is limited to toy examples and a Transformer run with a very large weight decay.

6zIhJuWxmV.one_liner: Adds contact-force tokens and a temporal transformer to a human reconstruction model to jointly predict pose, contacts and forces
6zIhJuWxmV.problem: Existing approaches separate visual pose reconstruction from contact and force estimation, which limits joint reasoning and propagates errors between stages.
6zIhJuWxmV.method: PACT augments a human reconstruction foundation model with learnable contact-force tokens and a temporal transformer that fuses visual features with world-space motion, with joint prediction heads and physics-based supervision for consistency between motion and forces. Training labels come from an annotation pipeline that combines contact labeling with physics-based motion and force optimization on synthetic and real videos.
6zIhJuWxmV.key_idea: Jointly predict pose, contacts and forces in one model supervised by physics-optimized pseudo labels, rather than a staged reconstruction-then-force pipeline.
6zIhJuWxmV.evidence: Comparisons with staged reconstruction approaches on climbing datasets including the new ForceWall benchmark with force-sensor ground truth and on RICH, with ablations and tests of generalization beyond the training distribution.
6zIhJuWxmV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written with extensive experiments and see the ForceWall benchmark, which measures hand and foot loads, as a useful contribution.
6zIhJuWxmV.main_concern: Label quality and the end-to-end claim are weakly validated, since hand contact and force pseudo-labels are unverified and the staged baselines differ in training data, body model, contact source and mass.

RWcRiQ45vV.one_liner: Relightable Gaussian splatting that propagates light through the object interior with a differentiable finite-volume transport solver for subsurface scattering.
RWcRiQ45vV.problem: Relightable Gaussian splatting models appearance independently per primitive, so non-local effects such as subsurface scattering are hard to represent.
RWcRiQ45vV.method: Uses the spatial support of the Gaussian scene as the domain of a differentiable finite-volume transport solver; a small network predicts scattering and absorption coefficients per Gaussian and the solve redistributes incident light. A shadow term predicted from visibility, transmittance and scattering, plus a regularizer suppressing specular highlights in predicted unlit regions, keep other terms from taking over.
RWcRiQ45vV.key_idea: Spread per-Gaussian scattering coefficients onto a voxel grid derived from Gaussian occupancy (winding numbers per a review) and let light flow through it with a finite-volume solver.
RWcRiQ45vV.evidence: Relighting experiments on three OLAT benchmarks, plus a per-primitive dipole-model substitution that lowers PSNR in six of seven scenes (Appendix G per a review).
RWcRiQ45vV.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before its results, and reviews report improvement across three OLAT benchmarks.
RWcRiQ45vV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the volumetric formulation captures non-local subsurface scattering through spatial connectivity and improves results across three OLAT benchmarks.
RWcRiQ45vV.main_concern: Evaluation is missing pieces (no separate PBR novel-view results or intermediate-attribute accuracy, no ablation of voxel grid resolution), and the transport domain is filled from Gaussians fit for image reconstruction whose boundaries may be inaccurate.

Td87itrJu6.one_liner: GraFINS replaces absolute coordinates with frame-invariant geometry features and a graph embedding to avoid the coordinate shortcut in neural surrogates.
Td87itrJu6.problem: On aligned vehicle benchmarks, surrogates can predict fields from absolute coordinates (a coordinate shortcut), so low error does not show they learned how fields respond to geometry and boundary conditions.
Td87itrJu6.method: GraFINS (Graph-Encoded Frame-Invariant Neural Surrogate) drops coordinate inputs, uses frame-invariant features encoding local geometry and its relation to boundary conditions, and adds a graph embedding that encodes the spatial arrangement of points.
Td87itrJu6.key_idea: Remove coordinate inputs and encode local geometry relative to boundary conditions with frame-invariant features, recovering global spatial information through a graph embedding.
Td87itrJu6.evidence: Trained only on vehicles with frontal flow, evaluated on unseen inflow directions and unrelated shape families against equivariant and non-equivariant baselines, plus in-distribution automotive and blood-vessel benchmarks and rotation stability.
Td87itrJu6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coordinate-shortcut diagnosis is meaningful, the out-of-distribution experiments (unseen inflows, unrelated shapes) are convincing, and GraFINS improves over baselines.
Td87itrJu6.main_concern: Confounders are not controlled (extra parameters and multi-scale design versus Transolver baselines), and a simple alternative of coordinates expressed in the physical frame is not compared.

E8kCaahqbf.one_liner: Controlled study arguing long open-loop action chunking mainly helps short-context policies imitate non-Markovian demonstrations.
E8kCaahqbf.problem: Why long open-loop action chunking helps imitation learning is poorly understood, and it reduces reactivity and error correction.
E8kCaahqbf.method: Varies the expert type (human versus scripted Markovian, among others), context length, execution horizon and data scale across four simulation and two real-world tasks to separate expert non-Markovianity from compounding errors.
E8kCaahqbf.key_idea: Non-Markovian expert demonstrations, not compounding errors, drive the benefit of long open-loop horizons, which vanishes once policies have long context and enough data.
E8kCaahqbf.evidence: Four simulation and two real-world tasks, with experiments varying the expert, observation context length, execution horizon and data scale.
E8kCaahqbf.claimed_gains: not stated; the finding is that closed-loop, long-context policies perform best in the high-data regime.
E8kCaahqbf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is well controlled, isolates expert non-Markovianity from compounding error, and usefully questions a common design default in imitation learning.
E8kCaahqbf.main_concern: Computational cost and real responsiveness of long-context, frequently queried policies are not evaluated, and details such as whether ACT temporal ensembling is used are missing.

p2caASr8D3.one_liner: Benchmark of executable alien-world sandboxes with counter-intuitive rules, testing whether AI systems discover and apply rules through experiments.
p2caASr8D3.problem: Scientific exploration is hard to evaluate because new hypotheses are hard to verify and discovery is hard to separate from recall of pretraining knowledge.
p2caASr8D3.method: ExplorationBench provides two sandboxes, AlienCode (31 discovery targets, 70 tasks) and AlienLogic (24 discovery targets, 70 tasks), each with a flawed manual, task-specific environmental feedback and a tool-call schema. Systems explore, then solve held-out tasks that are exactly verifiable.
p2caASr8D3.key_idea: Executable worlds whose rules conflict with familiar knowledge make answers exactly checkable and recall-proof, so held-out task success measures knowledge acquired by exploration.
p2caASr8D3.evidence: Evaluation of 10 AI systems on both sandboxes, with trajectory analyses and hindsight, fixed-probe and no-tool baselines.
p2caASr8D3.claimed_gains: not stated (benchmark paper; reports that the strongest of 10 systems can acquire and apply unfamiliar rules, but performance varies across trajectories).
p2caASr8D3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and the benchmark is trustworthy, with exactly verifiable, contamination-resistant tasks and analysis that goes beyond final scores.
p2caASr8D3.main_concern: Weak statistical design: only three trajectories per system per sandbox, with a best-of-3 selection that biases the autonomous-versus-hindsight comparison, and the worlds are synthetic.

afc0DiW11W.one_liner: Shows finite Newton-Schulz smooths Muon's polar update into a Lipschitz spectral map, yielding nonsmooth nonconvex stationarity guarantees via online-to-nonconvex conversion.
afc0DiW11W.problem: Existing Muon theory replaces Newton-Schulz with the exact polar factor or treats it as approximation error, so the iteration Muon actually runs can only hurt the guarantees.
afc0DiW11W.method: Analyzes Muon through online-to-nonconvex conversion, viewing it as an online learner with a smoothed spectral potential. Proves that a Newton-Schulz depth growing only logarithmically in the target accuracy suffices for convergence to stationary points, whereas Muon with the exact-polar update may fail.
afc0DiW11W.key_idea: Finite Newton-Schulz turns the discontinuous polar map into a Lipschitz map of the singular values, so Muon becomes an online learner with a smoothed spectral potential.
afc0DiW11W.evidence: Theoretical analysis of stationarity and sample complexity for an algorithm inside a randomized online-to-nonconvex protocol; the visible abstract states no experiments.
afc0DiW11W.claimed_gains: Sample complexity bounds match the best-known guarantees for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization and are optimal for smooth nonconvex optimization up to problem-dependent factors.
afc0DiW11W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a new interpretation of finite Newton-Schulz as beneficial smoothing rather than error, and an analysis that extends to general Lipschitz spectral maps.
afc0DiW11W.main_concern: The analyzed algorithm differs from practical Muon (fixed normalization, classical Newton-Schulz coefficients, randomized gradient queries, averaged output), limiting how far the guarantee applies to real implementations.

NDlFU2MnU9.one_liner: SPARK learns input-dependent gates that scale FFN outputs in a frozen LLM to control parametric knowledge during RAG.
NDlFU2MnU9.problem: Conflicts between retrieved context and parametric knowledge make LLMs rely on inconsistent internal knowledge, and editing parameters to resolve them is hard and may damage the backbone.
NDlFU2MnU9.method: A lightweight participation policy modulates the contribution of FFN-mediated parametric knowledge while the backbone stays frozen, and it is optimized with a faithfulness-oriented reward. Reviews describe it as one scalar gate per FFN layer, initialized to identity, that can attenuate or amplify FFN outputs.
NDlFU2MnU9.key_idea: Train per-layer input-dependent scalar gates on FFN outputs with a faithfulness reward, so the model adaptively throttles parametric knowledge without editing weights.
NDlFU2MnU9.evidence: Experiments on six datasets across several model sizes and families, out-of-domain evaluation, and checks on general capabilities.
NDlFU2MnU9.claimed_gains: Introduces and optimizes only 0.01% additional trainable parameters while keeping the backbone fully frozen; accuracy numbers are not stated in the abstract.
NDlFU2MnU9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple and parameter-efficient, with identity initialization, no backbone updates and broad experimental coverage including out-of-domain tests.
NDlFU2MnU9.main_concern: The ablations do not separate the contribution of RL training from input-dependent gating, and the constructed 'conflicting' passages and exact-match reward may not measure real contextual faithfulness.

6Lk3xKg1Mh.one_liner: Self-supervised pretraining for 3D vessel segmentation using curvilinear masking, tubular implant localization, and wavelet-detail prediction.
6Lk3xKg1Mh.problem: Vessel annotations are costly, and it is unclear how pretraining can encourage learning of sparse, slender, branching vascular structure without manual labels.
6Lk3xKg1Mh.method: TAP combines cubic and curvilinear masking for contextual restoration, localizes intensity-matched donor content implanted into tubular masks for dense region discrimination, and predicts removed wavelet detail from coarse views for fine-scale supervision.
6Lk3xKg1Mh.key_idea: Build pretext tasks from vessel morphology priors: curvilinear masks to restore, tubular implants to localize, and wavelet details to predict.
6Lk3xKg1Mh.evidence: Four vessel datasets, with a controlled comparison using the same 1,066 pretraining volumes and Swin UNETR backbone (per reviews).
6Lk3xKg1Mh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is relevant and the motivation clear, and that controlled comparisons and ablations with matched pretraining data support the reported gain.
6Lk3xKg1Mh.main_concern: Methodological novelty over VasoMIM and wavelet-based masked modeling is unclear, the synthetic vessel generation is simple, and the controls do not isolate which vascular property drives the gain.

Ahc6GUSVu3.one_liner: Lightweight pairwise scorer that correlates per-position top-k candidates of a diffusion-style drafter, making parallel speculative drafts jointly coherent.
Ahc6GUSVu3.problem: Diffusion-style drafters such as DFlash are trained on per-position marginals, so drafted tokens are individually plausible but jointly incoherent.
Ahc6GUSVu3.method: LiLiCorr keeps the top-k tokens per position as candidates, processes them jointly to produce an in and an out vector for each, and scores consecutive-position pairs by cosine similarity between the earlier out vector and the later in vector. It is trained to rank correct pairings highest and co-trained with the DFlash drafter, leaving only a cheap greedy walk sequential.
Ahc6GUSVu3.key_idea: Score adjacent-token candidate pairs via cosine similarity of learned in/out vectors, so block coherence is computed with batched matrix operations without materializing the joint.
Ahc6GUSVu3.evidence: Reviews describe experiments on Qwen3 targets with a common SGLang backend on a single H100, reporting acceptance length, throughput, and speedup against DFlash, DFlash 2, Domino, and DSpark.
Ahc6GUSVu3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clear, the marginals-versus-joint motivation is sound, and the serving evaluation (acceptance length, absolute throughput, concurrency sweep) is consistent and meaningful.
Ahc6GUSVu3.main_concern: The DFlash2 baseline appears mis-described and its reimplementation is unverified, gains over DFlash2 are small, and the central architectural components are not isolated by ablation.

NudM6zc90a.one_liner: Proves constant-depth rational-weight GNNs with sigmoid or tanh match 1-WL if Schanuel's conjecture holds.
NudM6zc90a.problem: It is unknown whether a constant-depth GNN with only rational weights can match the expressive power of the 1-WL test.
NudM6zc90a.method: The authors construct a uniform constant-depth GNN with integer or broad-range rational weights and logistic sigmoid, tanh, or related activations that matches 1-WL assuming Schanuel's conjecture. They also prove a partial converse for exponentiation, sinh, or cosh activations in a setting with auxiliary vertices.
NudM6zc90a.key_idea: Conditional on Schanuel's conjecture, a fixed integer-weight GNN, uniform across graph sizes and using sigmoid or tanh activations, distinguishes everything that 1-WL distinguishes.
NudM6zc90a.evidence: Theorems (a forward construction and a partial converse) plus experiments showing the constructed GNNs match the 1-WL test.
NudM6zc90a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the connection to Schanuel's conjecture novel and mathematically interesting, with a simple explicit integer-weight construction that is uniform in graph size.
NudM6zc90a.main_concern: Reviewers say exact real arithmetic leaves the gap to finite-precision computation open, so the practical meaning of the rational-weight result is unclear, and the converse needs a modified architecture with restricted activations.

IfYDX3tDmp.one_liner: Linear model with Gene Ontology graph-constrained gene representations predicts transcriptomic responses to unseen gene perturbations.
IfYDX3tDmp.problem: Predicting responses to untested gene perturbations matters for single-cell genetic screens, while recent work emphasizes large pretrained models rather than using existing biological relationships.
IfYDX3tDmp.method: Scaffold uses a GO annotation-overlap graph to constrain gene representations while measured responses train a shared linear response map.
IfYDX3tDmp.key_idea: Constrain gene embeddings with a GO annotation-overlap graph and fit a single shared linear map from embedding to response.
IfYDX3tDmp.evidence: 17 methods compared across nine scPerturBench datasets under the benchmark's six-metric ranking, plus controlled comparisons of GO, STRING, control-cell coexpression, and GO neighborhood width.
IfYDX3tDmp.claimed_gains: Ranked first on seven of nine datasets and third on the remaining two, with the best mean dataset rank of 1.44 among 17 methods.
IfYDX3tDmp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value that a small linear model (8,192 parameters in the shared response map) tops a public benchmark whose published ranks were reproduced, and the useful GO, STRING, and neighborhood comparisons.
IfYDX3tDmp.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited and a simple GO neighbor-averaging baseline, which has lower mean MSE than scaffold, sits outside the headline 17-method comparison.

yelw2WYdJB.one_liner: Scores message persuasiveness by how it shifts likelihoods of balanced pro and con stance probes against a neutral reference.
yelw2WYdJB.problem: Human persuasion experiments are costly, and LLM evaluators based on simulated reactions or holistic judgments are sensitive to innocuous instruction changes, which confounds persuasiveness with measurement reactivity.
yelw2WYdJB.method: The Contrastive Stance Probe Estimator (CSPE) is a reaction-free readout that measures how a message shifts the conditional likelihood of balanced third-party pro and con stance probes relative to a claim-matched neutral reference, using aggregate human treatment effects as the external criterion.
yelw2WYdJB.key_idea: Read persuasiveness from the change in conditional likelihood of pro and con probe statements given the message versus a neutral reference, instead of eliciting ratings.
yelw2WYdJB.evidence: 720 messages across ten policy issues and three evaluator models against Likert and Rubric-score baselines, stability transfer on 5,052 messages, and a matched-quartet validation; CSPE is reported as more stable and best correlated with human effects.
yelw2WYdJB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach is simple and well motivated, offering a more transparent, instruction-robust alternative to rating-based persuasion measurement with human-grounded evaluation.
yelw2WYdJB.main_concern: It is unclear whether CSPE measures persuasion or mainly stance agreement, and it is insufficiently compared with related likelihood-shift persuasion metrics.

LqgBCd5zmO.one_liner: Mask-aware RoPE injects erase masks into a text-to-image model trained on 101M pairs with RL and TraceFusion inference.
LqgBCd5zmO.problem: Real-world erasing needs broad coverage of objects, visual text, watermarks, associated effects, multiple objects, and varied scales and resolutions in one general model.
LqgBCd5zmO.method: The authors build LensErase-100M with 101.07 million source-mask-target examples and pretrain from the text-to-image model Lens using Mask-Aware RoPE, a 3D rotary encoding that injects the mask into source-image tokens without a separate mask token sequence. SFT and RL with contract-guided, region-aware rewards refine it, and TraceFusion at inference preserves content outside the effective edit region.
LqgBCd5zmO.key_idea: Encode the erase mask directly in a 3D rotary positional encoding of source-image tokens, avoiding extra mask tokens, and fine-tune with region-aware verifiable rewards.
LqgBCd5zmO.evidence: Six public benchmarks and LensErase-Bench with reference-based metrics and reference-free VLM evaluation; reviewers cite 12 baselines and ablations.
LqgBCd5zmO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large, diverse dataset with clean supervision and the Mask-Aware RoPE, RL, and TraceFusion pipeline give strong results across six benchmarks with useful ablations.
LqgBCd5zmO.main_concern: The same proprietary VLM serves as RL reward and benchmark judge (risk of reward hacking), no human study is reported, and it is unclear how much gain comes from data scale rather than the method.

TnLtRd28Q1.one_liner: Training-free token pruning that releases ViT tokens already judged normal, ranked against a trimmed normality reference over layers.
TnLtRd28Q1.problem: Pruning rules inherited from image classification discard faint defects while keeping salient normal regions, which fails in dense anomaly detection that labels every location.
TnLtRd28Q1.method: ADoRe scores each token against a normality reference trimmed to resist anomalies and accumulates its rank over a band of intermediate layers. The most normal patches are released and enter the anomaly map as zero without interpolation.
TnLtRd28Q1.key_idea: Prune tokens whose normality is settled, scored by rank accumulation against a trimmed-mean normality reference, rather than tokens that cannot change a global prediction.
TnLtRd28Q1.evidence: CLIP- and DINOv2-based image anomaly detectors and video appearance encoders on industrial, medical, and video benchmarks with random-selection controls; a reviewer cites 4.3% anomalous tokens mis-pruned at 60% pruning on VisA versus 13.5% for EViT.
TnLtRd28Q1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task-specific pruning criterion for dense anomaly detection is well motivated, simple, training-free, and deployment-friendly, with broad evaluations.
TnLtRd28Q1.main_concern: Fixed keep-ratio pruning and a trimmed-mean normality reference can fail with large defects or non-homogeneous backgrounds (a drop of 8.79 pixel AUROC on MVTec-AD for large anomalies), and the tested detector paradigms are limited.

GWFfAJxlQh.one_liner: Coordinate-preserving embeddings, participant-mean aggregation, and curvature and proximal regularizers reduce partition-induced risk gap in vertical federated learning.
GWFfAJxlQh.problem: When each VFL client holds a finer feature block, aggregating local representations loses information and degrades predictive performance.
GWFfAJxlQh.method: The authors derive a worst-case population-risk bound identifying the factors behind partition-induced degradation, then reduce them with architectural designs (coordinate-preserving embedding, participant-mean aggregation) and optional objectives (extraction-curvature and proximal extraction-output regularization).
GWFfAJxlQh.key_idea: Map each term of a worst-case risk bound to a design component: coordinate-preserving embeddings, mean aggregation across participants, and regularizers on extraction curvature and output drift.
GWFfAJxlQh.evidence: Numerical experiments, particularly on image classification; reviewers cite comparisons with Vanilla VFL and LASER-VFL, runtime and aggregation ablations, and full participation only.
GWFfAJxlQh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory-to-design link is principled and interpretable, the issue matters for fine-grained partitions, and the simple method gives large gains at large K.
GWFfAJxlQh.main_concern: All experiments use full participation, leaving the partial-participation and scalability motivation untested, and it is not shown that the regularizers actually reduce the theoretical gap.

VfF8pxLQ8f.one_liner: ENCORE performs exact replica exchange for inference-time diffusion control by storing generation trajectories and replacing upward moves with truncation.
VfF8pxLQ8f.problem: Sequential SMC control needs large particle populations, and existing replica-exchange methods are biased because they approximate an intractable time reversal.
VfF8pxLQ8f.method: Each replica stores its generation trajectory, so the upward move is a truncation and the intractable time reversal is never simulated; the paper proves target invariance and shows the dynamics are non-equilibrium replica exchange with the exact time reversal as forward proposal. A diffusion analysis compares guided and unguided proposals under refinement of the time discretisation.
VfF8pxLQ8f.key_idea: Run replica exchange in trajectory space so upward moves are truncations of stored trajectories and the intractable time-reversal terms cancel in the acceptance ratio.
VfF8pxLQ8f.evidence: Proofs of target invariance and a diffusion stability analysis, plus experiments on synthetic targets, Boltzmann sampling of molecules, and SDXL-Turbo reward tilting (the abstract is truncated after synthetic targets and Boltzmann sampling).
VfF8pxLQ8f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the trajectory-based construction is conceptually clear, removes a real bias in the closest prior replica-exchange method, and gives a useful comparison between SMC and replica exchange.
VfF8pxLQ8f.main_concern: Novelty and evidence are questioned: path-space lifting is standard in SMC, the experiments use unguided proposals while the favourable theory covers guided ones, and plain self-normalised importance sampling beats ENCORE in Table 4.

BJw3PRAyUN.one_liner: CoCom jointly picks tokens to commit and pending-update strength in masked diffusion decoding via a total-correlation bound.
BJw3PRAyUN.problem: Masked diffusion decoders must choose which predictions to commit and how strongly to update provisional context, but the model gives only per-position marginals that do not determine their joint dependence.
BJw3PRAyUN.method: CoCom bounds total correlation between committed variables and randomly retained pending variables using only current marginals, valid for every compatible joint distribution. One dependence budget then constrains both the committed set and the pending-update strength, with no extra forward passes, no training, and no separately tuned update strength.
BJw3PRAyUN.key_idea: A single marginals-only total-correlation bound on a reference observation couples commitment selection with the strength of provisional-context updates.
BJw3PRAyUN.evidence: Four backbones and four benchmarks, budget transfer from LLaDA-1.5 to LLaDA-Ins and Dream, and ablations comparing the joint bound with a separable bound.
BJw3PRAyUN.claimed_gains: Improves the accuracy-computation tradeoff over the compared accelerated decoders across four backbones and four benchmarks, and achieves the highest accuracy among accelerated decoders in seven of eight settings on LLaDA-Ins and Dream.
BJw3PRAyUN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling commitment and context-update decisions under one dependence bound is the main contribution, is mathematically coherent, and gives a practical decoder with no extra training or forward passes.
BJw3PRAyUN.main_concern: Evidence for the joint bound is uneven (small gains over the separable bound on GSM8K and MATH500, ablations only on LLaDA-1.5), with an unclear Native baseline setup, budgets partly selected on evaluation data, and theory that links only indirectly to actual decoding.

UqJMUrB8gs.one_liner: Position paper: interaction state should be an explicit learning target beyond object-centric features, illustrated by a SAM4D pilot.
UqJMUrB8gs.problem: Systems can track object identities and classify interactions yet leave open how a particular relationship is developing, such as whether a grasp is forming or ending.
UqJMUrB8gs.method: The paper argues the state of the interaction between specific participants, and how it changes, should be an explicit learning target judged by transfer to new questions about the event. A pilot trains SAM4D, a small readout on frozen SAM 3 features told which two participants to attend to.
UqJMUrB8gs.key_idea: Treat the state of the interaction between named participants, and its change over time, as a learning target evaluated by transfer to unseen event questions.
UqJMUrB8gs.evidence: A pilot on 15 events from eight videos with matched temporal heads, nonvisual controls, a duration prior, video-level uncertainty, and two human annotators auditing the event labels.
UqJMUrB8gs.claimed_gains: Telling the readout both participants raises relation Recall@3 by 19.39 percentage points over an actor-only query, while on 15 events from eight videos the recognition-trained representation shows no reliable advantage in predicting time left in the current event.
UqJMUrB8gs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the position is useful and falsifiable and that the pilot is transparent, with matched random readouts, nonvisual controls, bootstrap intervals, and annotation audits.
UqJMUrB8gs.main_concern: The central hypothesis is untested: no interaction-state objective is trained or compared with existing objectives, and the temporal evaluation (8 videos, 15 events) has intervals crossing zero.

Dtt178l9kS.one_liner: A learned policy jointly proposes structural model edits and diagnostic experiments, revising the model class once anytime-valid evidence rejects it.
Dtt178l9kS.problem: Discovery systems that optimize experiments within a fixed hypothesis space fail when every candidate omits the same mechanism, because candidate disagreement collapses while the model class stays wrong.
Dtt178l9kS.method: The method pairs a class-level distinguishability objective, where one shared parameterization must explain all selected experiments, with anytime-valid sequential evidence that triggers structural revision only after the current class is rejected. Edits are drawn from a supplied typed grammar.
Dtt178l9kS.key_idea: Gate structural edits on an anytime-valid test of the current model class, and pick each edit together with the experiment that tests whether it is necessary.
Dtt178l9kS.evidence: 400 held-out controlled dynamical environments, transfer tests (unseen mechanism combinations, held-out primitives, parameter extrapolation, shifted experiment costs), and the ODEBench and ODEBase benchmarks per reviews.
Dtt178l9kS.claimed_gains: Reaches 89.5% structural recovery with a budget of 32 real experiments, improving a resource-matched trained baseline by 10.0 percentage points, and detects library insufficiency in 88% of cases with a 5.5% false-support rate.
Dtt178l9kS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clear and well motivated, that gating revision on an anytime-valid class test is principled, and that reporting library insufficiency instead of forcing a wrong-class fit is valuable.
Dtt178l9kS.main_concern: The learned policy that drives the gains is under-specified (architecture, teacher search, imitation and RL details), and novelty is bounded by a supplied edit grammar with missing false-insufficiency rates and sharper baseline comparisons.

v26QBs5xyw.one_liner: Diversity measure from scale-integrated doubly-nonnegative relaxation of maximum diversity, satisfying three axioms and computable in polynomial time.
v26QBs5xyw.problem: Known diversity measures satisfying monotonicity, uniqueness, and continuity are NP-hard to evaluate, leaving open whether any such measure is computable in practice.
v26QBs5xyw.method: They take maximum diversity (Leinster-Cobbold diversity maximized over abundance distributions), integrate it over the scale of exponential similarity matrices, and replace the NP-hard single-scale evaluation with its doubly nonnegative relaxation, a convex problem solvable to prescribed accuracy in polynomial time.
v26QBs5xyw.key_idea: Integrating over similarity scale restores the axioms and the doubly-nonnegative relaxation preserves them while making evaluation a convex problem.
v26QBs5xyw.evidence: Theorems proving the three axioms and polynomial-time additive-accuracy evaluation; experiments use synthetic Euclidean data where the relaxation is exact and reduces to a convex QP (per the reviews).
v26QBs5xyw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper resolves a precise open problem with a mathematically interesting construction that preserves all three axioms, with results general to non-Euclidean dissimilarities.
v26QBs5xyw.main_concern: Experiments use only Euclidean distances where the relaxation is exact, so the general SDP route and its cost are not evaluated, and some sections are hard to follow.

rTpoNzwXu1.one_liner: Relaxes temporal weight sharing in spiking networks with compact time-varying modulation and binary synaptic routing for event vision.
rTpoNzwXu1.problem: SNNs usually share synaptic weights across timesteps, but event distributions and neuronal states evolve over time, so timesteps have heterogeneous features and conflicting optimization demands that one fixed transformation must serve.
rTpoNzwXu1.method: Delta SNN augments a shared synaptic backbone with compact temporal modulation for adaptive per-timestep transformations, and uses binary synaptic routing so the modulation runs with sparse, addition-based inference.
rTpoNzwXu1.key_idea: Add a compact per-timestep modulation on top of shared SNN weights, realized through binary synaptic routing to keep inference addition-based.
rTpoNzwXu1.evidence: Three event-vision tasks, plus a theoretical argument on expressive capacity; reviews cite ablations on modulation width, temporal windows, and routing binarization, and comparisons with parameter-matched static modulation and LoRA-style variants.
rTpoNzwXu1.claimed_gains: Improves strong baselines on three event-vision tasks with only marginal overhead; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
rTpoNzwXu1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation for time-dependent synaptic adaptation is clear, the module fits different SNN architectures while preserving spike-driven computation, and improvements are consistent across tasks and backbones.
rTpoNzwXu1.main_concern: Novelty looks incremental (LoRA-style low-rank residuals), gains are not cleanly separated from added capacity, and practical energy savings over ANNs are unvalidated on hardware.

p6BcZFbiWd.one_liner: Stores optimizer momentum as a moving average of output-space prediction errors and reprojects it through the current network each step.
p6BcZFbiWd.problem: Momentum is stored as a parameter-sized moving average of past gradients, which is memory-costly and fixes each past signal in the coordinates where it was computed.
p6BcZFbiWd.method: BOM keeps a compact moving average of prediction errors at the model output and reprojects that history through the current network at every step, preserving the current supervised gradient. It can replace the first-moment component of several adaptive optimizers, including ones that already compress their state.
p6BcZFbiWd.key_idea: Replace the parameter-space first moment with an output-space moving average of prediction errors, reprojected by backpropagation through the current model at each step.
p6BcZFbiWd.evidence: Language and vision fine-tuning (a primary five-task comparison), language and vision pretraining studies across output spaces and model scales, three language backbones, and matched mechanism controls.
p6BcZFbiWd.claimed_gains: Reduces parameter-shaped optimizer state by 49.7 to 99.8% in three compositions and paired step time by 4.0% averaged over three language backbones, and improves mean validation performance by 1.42 points in the primary five-task comparison.
p6BcZFbiWd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find output-space momentum an interesting, memory-efficient idea that plugs into existing optimizers such as AdamW, with promising results and adequate experimental scope.
p6BcZFbiWd.main_concern: It is not explained why averaged output-space errors beat standard momentum, nor whether the validation gains come from extra output-error information or from other effects.

2VmhZG47IL.one_liner: Training-free vision-encoder token retirement that ranks tokens by analytically computed removal influence and confirms low rank across consecutive blocks.
2VmhZG47IL.problem: Deciding when a token can be safely retired inside the vision encoder is hard because its representation is still evolving, and existing criteria rank tokens by redundancy rather than by whether later computation depends on them.
2VmhZG47IL.method: ICTR progressively shortens the sequence to a fixed terminal budget, estimating each token's external influence without extra forward passes by analytically computing how removing it from the current key-value set changes other tokens' outputs. It recomputes influence as the active set evolves and retires candidates whose ranks stay low over consecutive blocks.
2VmhZG47IL.key_idea: Score each token by averaging the largest relative output changes it causes in other tokens when removed from the key-value set, recomputed per block and confirmed across consecutive blocks.
2VmhZG47IL.evidence: Controlled interventions showing a frozen key-value memory does not substitute for continued updating, plus evaluation across 10 benchmarks; reviews mention several architectures including LLaVA-based models and Qwen2.5-VL, varied token budgets, and ablations.
2VmhZG47IL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the intervention-based criterion well motivated and analytically grounded, with generally convincing results, controls, and ablations across architectures and budgets.
2VmhZG47IL.main_concern: Gains over prior token-pruning methods are limited, the contribution is incremental over FlowCut and EvoCut, and baselines such as AutoPrune and CDPruner are missing.

u8OFXbfqS1.one_liner: Controlled study of how far ahead frozen-encoder latent world models rank actions reliably during zero-shot goal-image planning.
u8OFXbfqS1.problem: Existing studies show what world models can do but not when their predictions stay useful for planning and where they fail.
u8OFXbfqS1.method: They train action-conditioned predictors on five frozen visual backbones (V-JEPA 2, V-JEPA 2.1, VideoMAEv2, VideoPrism, DINOv2), pick actions by latent distance to a goal image, and vary predictor size, rollout-length training, encoder and simulator accuracy.
u8OFXbfqS1.key_idea: A latent-distance planner ranks actions reliably only for goals within, or slightly beyond, the rollout horizon the predictor was trained on.
u8OFXbfqS1.evidence: Meta-World manipulation tasks and BridgeData V2 real-robot interactions, with controls including a perfect simulator, an untrained predictor, matched-budget sweeps, and VLA experiments per reviews.
u8OFXbfqS1.claimed_gains: Finding rather than gain: with five-step rollouts, actions are ranked reliably only for targets five to ten control steps ahead, while task goals lie 16 to 53 steps away, and an 81-fold larger predictor does not extend this.
u8OFXbfqS1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the scientific testing of widely used methods, the well-designed controls, and the comparison of five encoders under one shared predictor and planner.
u8OFXbfqS1.main_concern: Cosine-distance scoring and representation-level analysis may not reflect decision-making quality, and the headline finding is seen as expected from myopic MPC.

5ylJYMtX3n.one_liner: Cuts spiking-Transformer training memory by partitioning into gradient-isolated units trained with local STBP, coordinated by adaptive intrinsic plasticity.
5ylJYMtX3n.problem: Global STBP retains neuronal states across both depth and time, creating a large memory burden for training deep spiking neural networks.
5ylJYMtX3n.method: NeuroProp partitions a spiking Transformer into consecutive units, stops gradients at unit boundaries, and runs full surrogate-gradient STBP over blocks and time steps within each unit. AdaIP broadcasts a semantic condition and turns it into channel-wise synaptic gain and membrane bias, adjusting the effective firing threshold and equilibrium potential of LIF neurons.
5ylJYMtX3n.key_idea: Stop gradients at unit boundaries so activation memory scales with the largest unit, and coordinate units with a condition-driven channel-wise gain and bias on LIF neurons.
5ylJYMtX3n.evidence: Controlled CIFAR-100 experiments on SpikFormer and SDTv3 and ImageNet-1K results, with training memory and throughput comparisons.
5ylJYMtX3n.claimed_gains: Peak memory reduced by 48.29% on SpikFormer and 79.41% on SDTv3 in CIFAR-100 experiments, and 71.30% ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy without global-STBP fine-tuning.
5ylJYMtX3n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the memory savings are clear and meaningful, with competitive accuracy across several datasets and spiking Transformer architectures.
5ylJYMtX3n.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty and the role of AdaIP: stop-gradient local learning is already common, and AdaIP's mechanism and necessity are not isolated or well explained.

YOfJGZYmd0.one_liner: Shows LLM agents communicating via a shared directory at test time outperform independent parallel attempts on hard open-ended tasks.
YOfJGZYmd0.problem: Whether communicating agents help beyond adding independent parallel attempts is an open question with mixed prior results.
YOfJGZYmd0.method: Agents with no predefined roles communicate through a shared directory; a team of k agents (team@k) is compared with independent agents on ARC-AGI-3, then tested on polyomino packing and MNIST classifier compression.
YOfJGZYmd0.key_idea: Agents without predefined roles share breakthroughs through a shared directory so one agent's discovery can push the whole group forward, compared against independent best@k attempts.
YOfJGZYmd0.evidence: ARC-AGI-3 (all 25 public games per reviews), polyomino packing and MNIST classifier compression, noting that independent agents may win when compute is limited.
YOfJGZYmd0.claimed_gains: A team of k communicating agents matches the success rate of 4k independent agents on ARC-AGI-3, and on MNIST a team of four produced a 1,957-byte classifier with 99.4% test accuracy.
YOfJGZYmd0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is relevant and meaningful and that the team@k versus best@k comparison shows substantial gains on ARC-AGI-3, with polyomino and MNIST results suggesting transfer to research tasks.
YOfJGZYmd0.main_concern: Reviewers say the experiments do not isolate communication as the cause (prompts that push diverse exploration, action synchronization only for ARC teams) and are under-tested, with missing confidence intervals and single team trials on some tasks.

93WJUnP2GC.one_liner: Estimates prompt difficulty for RLVR by sharing rollout feedback across a semantic graph with Potts-prior latent difficulty states.
93WJUnP2GC.problem: Online difficulty estimates for RLVR scheduling are hard to get: dedicated probing adds generation overhead, and history-based estimators suffer cold start and stale feedback and ignore relations among samples.
93WJUnP2GC.method: A difficulty-aware sample graph is built from semantic and reasoning similarities, latent difficulty states are introduced with a Potts prior that encourages neighbors to share a state, and estimates are updated continuously from rollout feedback. The estimator plugs into existing sample-selection and rollout-allocation schedulers.
93WJUnP2GC.key_idea: Propagate rollout feedback between related problems over a similarity graph with a Potts prior on latent difficulty states, removing the need for dedicated probing.
93WJUnP2GC.evidence: Mathematical reasoning with two model families and three schedulers, plus batch-level correlation and overhead comparisons against low-cost estimators, per the reviews (abstract truncated).
93WJUnP2GC.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results).
93WJUnP2GC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sharing rollout feedback across related problems is a reasonable, low-overhead way to avoid probing, with consistent gains across model families and schedulers.
93WJUnP2GC.main_concern: Novelty and baselines are unclear because prior work already propagates success estimates across prompts and related adaptive schedulers are not compared, while a static graph and cumulative estimates may go stale as the policy changes.

Sn983rEl02.one_liner: Characterizes optimal secretary policies when a content-free stochastic signal arrives no later than the best item, including closed-form asymptotics.
Sn983rEl02.problem: Learning-augmented secretary algorithms use value estimates, rank predictions, or recommendations, leaving advice conveyed only through timing unstudied.
Sn983rEl02.method: Derives the exact finite-n optimal policy and success probability for arbitrary known signal distributions under random arrival order, then threshold policies and asymptotics for the alpha-power family, robustness to misspecified alpha, and worst-case guarantees under adversarial order.
Sn983rEl02.key_idea: Model the signal as a timing precursor to the best item and solve the resulting Bellman recursion exactly, yielding threshold policies for the alpha-power signal family.
Sn983rEl02.evidence: Theoretical proofs only: exact recursion, closed-form asymptotics, robustness to alpha misspecification, and adversarial-order worst-case guarantees.
Sn983rEl02.claimed_gains: The limiting success probability exceeds the classic 1/e for every alpha > 0, equals 1/2 for alpha = 1, and approaches 1 as alpha goes to infinity.
Sn983rEl02.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the model clean, the optimal policies explicit with matching success probabilities, the closed-form asymptotics elegant, and the paper well written.
Sn983rEl02.main_concern: Limited novelty and relevance: the random-order model is a special case of the framework of Dütting et al., and the signal assumption (perfectly reliable, known distribution) is very strong.

LtRhxZUsKa.one_liner: Adds a geometric attention kernel using 3D points and camera poses beside the semantic kernel in VLMs, plus reference-frame supervision.
LtRhxZUsKa.problem: VLMs struggle with 3D spatial relations across views, and fusing reconstruction features into visual tokens is hard to align with pretrained semantic representations under limited spatial supervision.
LtRhxZUsKa.method: Dual-Kernel Attention keeps the pretrained semantic kernel and adds a geometric kernel that uses estimated 3D points and camera poses to modulate attention through point displacements and relative view transformations, fused by a learned gate. Reference-Frame Composition (RC) supervision trains stepwise turn and heading updates.
LtRhxZUsKa.key_idea: Inject geometry into attention as position (point displacement and view transform) in a parallel gated kernel rather than as fused reconstruction features.
LtRhxZUsKa.evidence: Six spatial benchmarks including VSI-Bench and ReVSI-32, with Qwen3-VL as backbone and ablations on single-kernel, additive-position, and identity-transform controls.
LtRhxZUsKa.claimed_gains: DK-VLM-8B achieves the highest average across six spatial benchmarks and the top overall scores on VSI-Bench (74.33) and ReVSI-32 (58.28).
LtRhxZUsKa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the dual-kernel design a well-motivated way to add geometry while preserving pretrained attention, supported by controls and strong benchmark gains.
LtRhxZUsKa.main_concern: Novelty is incremental (the geometric operation is inherited from GTA), evidence is limited to Qwen3-VL, and RC gains are not fully isolated from extra supervision and compute.

D4RNKyIOJ5.one_liner: Recovers anisotropic diffusion coefficients from unpaired population snapshots by solving a weak Fokker-Planck linear system.
D4RNKyIOJ5.problem: Unpaired population snapshots reveal marginal evolution but do not determine an unrestricted stochastic generator.
D4RNKyIOJ5.method: SNAP-Diffusion converts snapshot statistics and occupation quadrature into a finite weak Fokker-Planck system over a uniformly elliptic coefficient class, giving identifiability within the class through restricted coercivity along with stability bounds. The recovered operator is frozen for downstream prediction.
D4RNKyIOJ5.key_idea: Weak-form Fokker-Planck constraints from snapshot statistics give a finite-dimensional linear estimation problem whose restricted coercivity yields identifiability and stability.
D4RNKyIOJ5.evidence: Theory (identifiability, stability, error control), controlled two-dimensional transport experiments, and a controlled FX experiment on state-dependent local correlation.
D4RNKyIOJ5.claimed_gains: In the FX experiment SNAP reduces mean pricing error by 68% and 71% relative to constant- and time-dependent-correlation models and by 19% relative to same-class forward calibration.
D4RNKyIOJ5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework coherent and practically motivated, with theory establishing identifiability and stability and validation that is rigorous and consistent with the narrative.
D4RNKyIOJ5.main_concern: Experiments are limited to controlled synthetic or low-dimensional settings with predefined coefficient families, and presentation, motivation, and novelty relative to weak-form estimation are weak.

E1sqClfF16.one_liner: Weights audio-visual matching evidence by entropy-based informativeness and integrates it over monotone temporal paths for deepfake detection.
E1sqClfF16.problem: Sustained or recurring visual states make local audio-visual correspondences ambiguous, so matching strength becomes unreliable evidence for deepfake detection.
E1sqClfF16.method: AATT estimates correspondence informativeness from the normalized entropy of local matching distributions, marginalizes the weighted evidence over monotone paths for soft cross-modal correspondences, and scores via transport compatibility, mean informativeness, and path surprisal. It trains only on authentic talking videos with a ranking objective.
E1sqClfF16.key_idea: Entropy-weighted correspondence evidence marginalized over monotone alignment paths, scoring deepfakes by transport compatibility, informativeness, and path surprisal learned only from real videos.
E1sqClfF16.evidence: Four benchmarks including SHDF (singing), with AVH-Align and T-AVFD retrained on the same authentic videos, reverse-transfer tests, and module ablations.
E1sqClfF16.claimed_gains: Outperforms retrained baselines on all four benchmarks, including a 7.9-point AUC gain over T-AVFD on SHDF per a reviewer; the visible abstract states no numbers.
E1sqClfF16.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the ambiguity motivation reasonable, the method clearly designed, and the detection and cross-scene transfer results strong when trained only on real talking videos.
E1sqClfF16.main_concern: Limited novelty and weak attribution: it combines entropy weighting, monotone dynamic-programming alignment, and feature aggregation, with little direct evidence that gains come from ambiguity handling or from path surprisal.

vgGbxzZCrV.one_liner: Trains few-step autoregressive video generators on adversarially perturbed self-generated histories chosen by distribution-matching gradients of future predictions.
vgGbxzZCrV.problem: Few-step autoregressive video models remain highly sensitive to errors in their generated history (the local history robustness gap), so small deviations amplify and errors accumulate over long horizons.
vgGbxzZCrV.method: AGF uses distribution matching gradients from future block predictions to select adversarial perturbations of self-generated histories, then trains the generator jointly on the original and perturbed histories.
vgGbxzZCrV.key_idea: Select history perturbations that maximize the future block's distribution-matching loss, and train the generator to stay robust on both original and perturbed histories.
vgGbxzZCrV.evidence: VBench Total score on 60-second video and visual quality on four-minute generation, trained on five-second rollouts, with Gaussian-perturbation and recovery-experiment comparisons.
vgGbxzZCrV.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest VBench Total score on 60-second generation and the best visual quality on four-minute generation after training on only five-second rollouts.
vgGbxzZCrV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the history-robustness framing useful, the use of future distribution-matching gradients to select perturbations a meaningful design, and the long-horizon results strong.
vgGbxzZCrV.main_concern: Controls are missing: no matched ablation without history perturbations (clean-only DMD with the same recipe), the Gaussian baseline is not separately tuned, and the robustness framing may be circular with error accumulation.

MdtIjEwpP6.one_liner: Dimension-free decentralized nonsmooth nonconvex optimization via a decentralized online-to-nonconvex conversion to online convex optimization.
MdtIjEwpP6.problem: The best existing decentralized algorithm for finding Goldstein stationary points has sample and communication complexity that depends polynomially on the dimension d.
MdtIjEwpP6.method: Reduces decentralized nonsmooth nonconvex stochastic optimization to a decentralized online convex optimization (D-OCO) problem through an online-to-nonconvex conversion whose consensus requirements are inherited from the D-OCO decisions, linking dimension dependence to consensus error.
MdtIjEwpP6.key_idea: A decentralized online-to-nonconvex conversion with a shared random interpolation weight inherits consensus from D-OCO, trading dimension dependence for only logarithmic extra communication.
MdtIjEwpP6.evidence: Theoretical analysis only: complexity theorems and a general reduction; reviewers note there are no numerical experiments.
MdtIjEwpP6.claimed_gains: Achieves O(δ^{-1}ε^{-3}) sample complexity and Õ(γ^{-1/2}δ^{-1}ε^{-3}) communication complexity, with no polynomial dependence on the dimension d.
MdtIjEwpP6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives the first decentralized first-order result without polynomial dimension dependence, matching the centralized sample-complexity lower bound, through a general and clearly explained reduction.
MdtIjEwpP6.main_concern: There are no numerical experiments or communication lower bound, and practicality is questioned because Algorithm 1 outputs a global average that individual nodes do not hold and the shared-weight scheme leaves most nodes idle.

p1Zxt5QWZe.one_liner: Adds a regularizer that spreads causal contribution across attack tokens to make optimization-based jailbreaks transfer better.
p1Zxt5QWZe.problem: Optimization-based jailbreaks work on the source model but fail to transfer, because their success depends on a small subset of attack representations whose contribution shrinks in target models.
p1Zxt5QWZe.method: Uses causal interventions to show localized dependence, then introduces Causal Resilience (CR), a plug-in regularization term that evenly distributes contributions to attack effectiveness across the attack space and applies to GCG, AutoDAN, and variants without changing their search.
p1Zxt5QWZe.key_idea: Penalize uneven causal contribution across attack positions (via mean and standard-deviation terms) so attack success is not tied to a few localized representations.
p1Zxt5QWZe.evidence: Causal-tracing analysis of source versus target models and transfer experiments on GCG, AutoDAN, and variants across two benchmarks, two source models, and diverse target model families.
p1Zxt5QWZe.claimed_gains: Consistently improves the transferability of GCG, AutoDAN, and their variants to diverse model families; no numbers stated, and one reviewer calls the gains marginal.
p1Zxt5QWZe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the causal-intervention diagnosis intuitive and convincing and CR a plug-and-play regularizer that works across several attack methods.
p1Zxt5QWZe.main_concern: Gains are marginal and the evaluation has flaws: hyperparameters appear tuned on a target model despite a claimed target-isolation, novelty over importance-spreading methods like PiF is unclear, and overhead is unreported.

1cR9KNtNeJ.one_liner: Generates ligands while denoising full-protein conformations, using coordinate-perturbation training on holo complexes to cover apo inputs.
1cR9KNtNeJ.problem: Structure-based ligand generation assumes a fixed protein, ignoring conformational change on binding, and paired apo-holo data are scarce.
1cR9KNtNeJ.method: FlexiDD models full-protein conformational adaptation at atomic resolution during ligand generation. A transferable coordinate-denoising strategy perturbs coordinates so apo and holo conformations overlap in noisy distributions, allowing training solely on holo complexes while accepting apo or holo inputs at inference.
1cR9KNtNeJ.key_idea: Add coordinate noise so apo and holo structures share overlapping noisy distributions, letting a model trained only on holo complexes handle apo inputs.
1cR9KNtNeJ.evidence: A leakage-audited benchmark with predicted binding affinity and PoseBusters validity for both holo and apo inputs; reviewers note computational experiments only.
1cR9KNtNeJ.claimed_gains: Under apo conditioning, FlexiDD reaches 91.6% PoseBusters validity versus less than 46.1% for the evaluated methods (abstract truncated).
1cR9KNtNeJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and the full-protein flexibility modeling with apo-holo transfer interesting, with extensive comparisons against existing work.
1cR9KNtNeJ.main_concern: The noise-based apo-holo bridging is insufficiently validated (8 Å noise scale, no noise-scale or pure-noise-initialization ablations) and the advantage over existing methods is not significant.

sC6TvswKIS.one_liner: Pretrains a world-action model from scratch with a control-oriented autoencoder, one-step visual planner, and inverse dynamics model.
sC6TvswKIS.problem: World-action models usually adapt natural-video generators, leaving open how manipulation capability scales when pretrained from scratch on manipulation data.
sC6TvswKIS.method: GE-Act 2.0 combines a control-oriented autoencoder (CoAE), a single-step visual planner (SVP), and an inverse dynamics model (IDM), with SVP and IDM pretrained separately and trained jointly by knowledge-aligned selective optimization (KASO) on generated futures compatible with recorded actions.
sC6TvswKIS.key_idea: Co-train the visual planner and inverse dynamics model only on predicted futures compatible with recorded actions, using one-step generation for real-time control.
sC6TvswKIS.evidence: Zero-shot OOD evaluation on 100 real-robot tasks across 20 skill groups and two embodiments (G1-OP and G2-90D), with data scaling from 300 to 30,000 hours and a skill-coverage analysis.
sC6TvswKIS.claimed_gains: Generates a 52-action chunk in 104 ms on one RTX 5090 for 30 Hz control, scaling co-training data from 300 to 30,000 hours substantially improves success rates, and fine-grained instruction following reaches at least 90% Follow Score (abstract truncated).
sC6TvswKIS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the scale and breadth of real-robot zero-shot evaluation (100 tasks, two embodiments, up to 30,000 hours) and the coherent from-scratch architecture notable.
sC6TvswKIS.main_concern: Comparisons and attribution are weak: no matched real-robot comparison against other WAMs or VLAs, scaling gains confound data volume with diversity, and contact-rich tasks such as Zip stay at 0.0% success.

rB5EnFgmGI.one_liner: Jointly estimates sub-frame view time offsets and 2D/3D point tracks from unsynchronized multi-view videos using epipolar geometry and attention.
rB5EnFgmGI.problem: Multi-view 3D point tracking assumes temporally aligned videos, and even small time offsets break the epipolar geometry and degrade cross-view feature aggregation.
rB5EnFgmGI.method: EpiInit analytically initializes offsets from an epipolar constraint with a second-order Taylor approximation. A transformer stage then alternates EpiRef (updates offsets via Sampson error landscapes) and STCV attention (refines 2D/3D trajectories under temporal misalignment).
rB5EnFgmGI.key_idea: Alternate geometry-based offset refinement (Sampson error) with spatio-temporal cross-view attention so synchronization and tracking improve each other.
rB5EnFgmGI.evidence: Five datasets (e.g., MV-Kubric2 and Panoptic Studio) compared with VisualSync, plus component ablations and multi-seed results per reviewers.
rB5EnFgmGI.claimed_gains: Achieves sub-frame synchronization accuracy and significantly outperforms the visual synchronization baseline; a reviewer cites 30 vs. 94 ms on MV-Kubric2 and 87 vs. 269 ms on Panoptic Studio against VisualSync.
rB5EnFgmGI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, EpiInit gives a geometrically grounded start, and synchronization and tracking improvements over baselines are large across datasets.
rB5EnFgmGI.main_concern: The contribution looks like a combination of existing techniques, and experiments do not isolate synchronization's effect from the backbone or show that alternating refinement beats simple geometry-based alternatives.

ujz5K8Ie4B.one_liner: Hierarchical Minecraft agent pairing a capability-aware harness (planner, memory, completion detector) with a single native keyboard-mouse VLA.
ujz5K8Ie4B.problem: Existing game agents give either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy, or high-level planning executed through APIs or predefined skills.
ujz5K8Ie4B.method: A VLM planner picks subtasks within the VLA's capabilities using structured memory and a policy-coupled completion detector, while one VLA executes with vision-only perception and native keyboard and mouse. Regime-specific RMSNorm branches and separate mouse-movement token embeddings reduce GUI and non-GUI interference, and training combines world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and RL.
ujz5K8Ie4B.key_idea: Close the planning-execution loop with a completion detector conditioned on VLA policy context, and isolate GUI versus non-GUI regimes with regime-specific RMSNorm branches.
ujz5K8Ie4B.evidence: Minecraft benchmarks (LongBench with 14 tasks and MineStudio per reviewers), a fixed-policy harness ablation, and training-stage ablations.
ujz5K8Ie4B.claimed_gains: The visible abstract gives no numbers; reviewers cite LongBench goal success rising from 10.7% to 25.0% with the harness and MineStudio from 65.1% to 80.7% with RL.
ujz5K8Ie4B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the integration of native-interface execution with long-horizon coordination compelling, with the frozen-policy harness ablation showing that orchestration drives the gain.
ujz5K8Ie4B.main_concern: Evaluation is narrow and weakly controlled: all experiments are Minecraft-only, LongBench has only 14 tasks without confidence intervals, planning relies on GPT-4o without a weaker-planner ablation, and long-horizon success remains low.

vHb6pIycg3.one_liner: Samples cyclic peptides jointly in sequence and structure while preserving compiled covalent ring constraints and applying receptor-guided potentials.
vHb6pIycg3.problem: Existing cyclic-peptide generators leave ring constraints unenforced during sampling, which can compromise physical validity and receptor compatibility.
vHb6pIycg3.method: HyBridge is a hybrid sampler: a receptor-free reference model supplies peptide diversity, then after geometric placement a shared receptor potential guides backbone motion and residue substitutions, with accepted updates preserving the compiled constraints. Pairing preferences are learned from crossed peptide-receptor panels with chemical supervision.
vHb6pIycg3.key_idea: Enforce covalent ring constraints throughout joint sequence-structure sampling while a learned receptor potential guides each accepted update.
vHb6pIycg3.evidence: Held-out receptor targets under a head-to-tail (H2T) benchmark, with guidance ablations and an AF3 analysis on seven reciprocal receptor pairs per reviewers.
vHb6pIycg3.claimed_gains: Achieves 61.2% structural delivery under a common closure, contact, and severe-overlap criterion; suffix guidance adds 15.1 percentage points over no learned potential and 5.6 over terminal-only use.
vHb6pIycg3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving covalent constraints throughout sampling rather than post-processing is a useful design, with controlled evidence that guidance during sampling improves structural delivery.
vHb6pIycg3.main_concern: The metric measures geometric feasibility rather than binding affinity or specificity, and baseline comparisons are not compute-matched given HyBridge's internal candidate screening and search.

0izVG6pysU.one_liner: Uses the policy's own length-normalized log-likelihood of correct trajectories as a difficulty signal for RL curriculum and reward shaping.
0izVG6pysU.problem: Sparse outcome rewards limit RL guidance for reasoning, and pass-rate difficulty cannot separate correct trajectories for the same problem.
0izVG6pysU.method: Self-Curriculum scores verified trajectories by negative length-normalized log-likelihood under the current policy, orders them from easy to hard, periodically updates difficulty as the policy changes, and incorporates the signal into reward shaping within GRPO.
0izVG6pysU.key_idea: Use the current policy's likelihood of a correct trajectory as a learner-relative, periodically re-estimated difficulty score that drives ordering and reward shaping.
0izVG6pysU.evidence: Multiple math reasoning benchmarks and model families (Qwen3-8B, plus 14B per reviewers) against GRPO and external difficulty baselines at problem and trajectory levels.
0izVG6pysU.claimed_gains: A reviewer reports Qwen3-8B MATH accuracy rising from 65.59% with GRPO to 71.29%; the abstract states consistent gains over GRPO without numbers.
0izVG6pysU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the trajectory-level likelihood curriculum well motivated, with controls (shared student-generated pools; separate filtering, ordering, reranking, and shaping) and gains across model families, seeds, and 14B models.
0izVG6pysU.main_concern: Novelty and attribution are limited: easy-to-hard curricula and rewarding low-probability correct responses already exist, extra gains may come from signal in all-correct groups, and benchmarks are dated with a 42-question AMC/AIME subset.

9eaH7FWdY7.one_liner: Training-free attention bias on identity-critical facial keypoint tokens to strengthen identity preservation in image-conditioned text-to-image models.
9eaH7FWdY7.problem: Image-conditioned T2I models know which reference tokens to attend to but under-weight identity-critical facial features relative to peripheral ones, failing on cross-view or small-scale subjects.
9eaH7FWdY7.method: FreeID uses the model's own attention responses to match reference facial keypoint tokens to generation tokens, then injects sparse attention biases that amplify those links, with magnitudes set by a closed-form expression.
9eaH7FWdY7.key_idea: Match reference facial keypoint tokens to generation tokens through the model's own attention, then add sparse attention biases whose magnitudes come from a closed-form rule.
9eaH7FWdY7.evidence: FLUX.2-klein and LongCat-Image-Edit-Turbo on a 50-sample test set (25 Unsplash and 25 CelebA per a reviewer), with ablations and add-ons to PuLID, DreamO, and image-to-video models.
9eaH7FWdY7.claimed_gains: Improves identity preservation without training, at +15.5% latency and no extra memory per a reviewer; the visible abstract gives no numbers.
9eaH7FWdY7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the attention-allocation analysis insightful and the training-free, plug-and-play method simple and effective, with modest overhead and some generality across T2I and I2V.
9eaH7FWdY7.main_concern: Evaluation is small and narrow: two models and a 50-sample test set, few comparisons with other editing models or adapters, and the identity-versus-editability trade-off is under-evaluated.

TE2XR1JsY3.one_liner: Consults a clinical casebook for a frozen LLM via a patient graph and greedy search by marginal utility.
TE2XR1JsY3.problem: Retrieving prior patients for EHR reasoning suffers from perspective limitation, instance-level retrieval that ignores cohort structure, and overlapping cases that give diminishing marginal gains.
TE2XR1JsY3.method: GraphWalker organizes historical patients into a clinically structured graph, localizes relevant groups with cohort prototypes, and runs Context-Conditioned Greedy Search with Frontier Expansion that re-evaluates candidate patients by marginal utility, measured by the reduction in target-input cross-entropy.
TE2XR1JsY3.key_idea: Score each candidate patient by how much it lowers the target input's cross-entropy under the current working context, searching a cohort-structured patient graph greedily.
TE2XR1JsY3.evidence: EHR clinical prediction tasks (mortality and readmission) with several LLM backbones and encoders, supervised comparisons, a held-out institution, and a factorial search ablation.
TE2XR1JsY3.claimed_gains: A reviewer cites mortality AUPRC rising from 32.23 to 59.46 and AUROC from 75.37 to 84.19 with Qwen3-14B; the visible abstract gives no numbers.
TE2XR1JsY3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the hierarchical retrieval plus context-conditioned search reduces duplicate and irrelevant cases, with improvements surviving strong controls and substantial gains across tasks and backbones.
TE2XR1JsY3.main_concern: The prediction timeline is unclear (last-visit target versus ICU readmission labeling, with possible future-information leakage), and the graph-specific benefit is not isolated at equal scoring cost.

x7hhRx7tNO.one_liner: Replaces candidate slots of a frozen trajectory predictor with retrieved, causally eligible past trajectories, with no training.
x7hhRx7tNO.problem: Deployed trajectory predictors accumulate realized futures of earlier predictions, but existing ways to use such feedback need model updates, gradients, or auxiliary training that black-box settings forbid.
x7hhRx7tNO.method: TCMA is an output-level adapter that retrieves trajectories whose futures have fully elapsed and replaces the last q candidate slots, combining a scene-invariant egocentric channel and a scene-aware world-frame channel tuned online from elapsed labels, with finite-sample risk bounds.
x7hhRx7tNO.key_idea: Only trajectories whose futures have fully elapsed are causally admissible memory, retrieved through egocentric and world-frame channels to swap into the predictor's candidate set.
x7hhRx7tNO.evidence: ETH-UCY prospective evaluation across seven predictors, with an analysis decomposing retrieval benefit and displacement harm.
x7hhRx7tNO.claimed_gains: Mean relative reductions of 6.52% in minADE@20 across seven predictors on ETH-UCY (a second reduction is cut off in the abstract).
x7hhRx7tNO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-free black-box setting practical and the method simple and applicable across predictors, with consistent gains and low latency.
x7hhRx7tNO.main_concern: Limited novelty and evidence: memory retrieval was explored in MANTRA and MemoNet, there are no direct comparisons with online-adaptation methods or simple replacement baselines, and the theoretical guarantee is not operational at inference.

DAScAUX9CT.one_liner: Builds shorter valid confidence intervals using LLM-generated texts, with content-style representations and density-ratio calibration against distribution shift.
DAScAUX9CT.problem: With few text-outcome pairs, precise inference is hard, and naive use of LLM-generated texts is biased and overconfident because of distribution shift and within-source dependence.
DAScAUX9CT.method: MaSI generates texts that preserve source content while varying style, learns outcome-relevant content and complementary style coordinates, builds a calibrated auxiliary statistic on a separate evaluation set with density-ratio calibration, corrects with real-label residuals, and estimates uncertainty across original sources.
DAScAUX9CT.key_idea: Treat generated texts as dependent within source, calibrate their shift with density ratios, and correct with real-label residuals in a prediction-powered-inference style.
DAScAUX9CT.evidence: Theory (representation learning, asymptotics, interval validity) and experiments including a controlled text experiment, negative controls, and variance sensitivity analysis.
DAScAUX9CT.claimed_gains: Shorter confidence intervals with valid coverage when real text-outcome pairs are scarce; a reviewer notes interval-width ratios of about 0.93 rising to 0.96-0.98 once dependence is accounted for.
DAScAUX9CT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the treatment of dependence among texts from the same source, the honest negative controls (the independent-text control covers only 0.782 instead of 0.90), and the theoretical analysis.
DAScAUX9CT.main_concern: The guarantees rest on hard-to-verify assumptions, and gains are small and inconsistent (simpler methods sometimes match it, and widths shrink only to 0.96-0.98 after accounting for dependence).

DTXigl9Qsf.one_liner: Maintains a query-independent active state through verified state transactions committed at interaction time, not reconstructed at read time.
DTXigl9Qsf.problem: Retaining history through long context, summaries, retrieval, or recurrent memory does not guarantee a coherent current state: single-state recovery can be accurate while whole-state consistency fails.
DTXigl9Qsf.method: StateCommit converts interaction evidence into explicit state transactions verified before a deterministic runtime commits persistent updates, and for visual prediction grounds the state with slot-indexed Visual Bindings. It also introduces the StateReturn benchmark for whole-state maintenance and state-consistent future prediction.
DTXigl9Qsf.key_idea: Shift state resolution from read time to interaction time via verified, versioned state transactions committed by a deterministic runtime into an Active State.
DTXigl9Qsf.evidence: The StateReturn benchmark comparing against Full-History baselines after varying numbers of intervening interactions, with target-state and full-state exact-match metrics.
DTXigl9Qsf.claimed_gains: On StateReturn, StateCommit achieves 98.67-100.00% full-state exact match, whereas Full-History retains 98.61% target-state accuracy but only 13.89% full-state exact match after 16 intervening interactions.
DTXigl9Qsf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it identifies a real failure mode (history retention versus whole-state consistency), with a clear and thoughtful benchmark design separating target-state from whole-state correctness.
DTXigl9Qsf.main_concern: Results may be easy by construction: predefined slot schemas make maintenance near-deterministic and saturate the benchmark, and baselines such as Mem0 and A-MEM and end-to-end agent task success are missing.

l7Eyl0npKQ.one_liner: Trains multimodal reward models with visual-gain and evidence-flip margin supervision to reduce reliance on text-only shortcuts.
l7Eyl0npKQ.problem: Multimodal reward models rely on text-only shortcuts, and the Bradley-Terry objective amplifies textual preference signals while leaving visual evidence's contribution to the margin unsupervised.
l7Eyl0npKQ.method: Visual-conditional margin learning (VCM) adds visual-gain supervision from text-only to multimodal conditioning, plus evidence-flip (EF) supervision that enforces preference-margin changes under local reversals of decisive visual evidence with question and responses fixed, cancelling the shared text-only component.
