l7Eyl0npKQ.key_idea: Require the preference margin to change when decisive visual evidence is edited while the text is held fixed, so the text-only component cancels.
l7Eyl0npKQ.evidence: Multiple MM-RM backbones and multimodal preference benchmarks, a preliminary frozen-probe and BT-dynamics analysis, and Best-of-N downstream selection.
l7Eyl0npKQ.claimed_gains: Improved reward-model performance, reduced text-only shortcut dependence, and better Best-of-N response selection; no numbers stated.
l7Eyl0npKQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the preliminary analysis a clear motivation and the evidence-flip objective a well-targeted fix, with analyses that go beyond benchmark accuracy.
l7Eyl0npKQ.main_concern: Novelty and data reliability are questioned: the work combines prior shortcut analysis with prior image-editing methods, gains are inconsistent once EF data exposure is matched, and EF samples flip preference only 88% of the time.

K41ebvrKaw.one_liner: Propagates gated memory across rollout steps so a shallow constructive policy learns dynamic embeddings for combinatorial optimization without labels.
K41ebvrKaw.problem: Dynamic-embedding NCO methods rebuild subproblem representations from scratch at each step with deep attention stacks, and the strong ones need solution labels or aggressive search-space pruning.
K41ebvrKaw.method: MiLoop is purely RL-based: it fuses current embeddings with historical memory before the attention layers and applies adaptive gated updates afterward, so updated representations serve both current decisions and stepwise reuse.
K41ebvrKaw.key_idea: Reuse the multi-step computation of a rollout by fusing prior memory before attention and gating updates after, so a shallow policy approximates dynamic embeddings.
K41ebvrKaw.evidence: Four COPs including TSP and CVRP, trained on 100-node instances and applied up to 10K nodes, with greedy and 100-start decoding and memory-component ablations.
K41ebvrKaw.claimed_gains: Produces high-quality solutions across four COPs; a reviewer cites the CVRP gap falling from 2.87% at 100 nodes to 1.09% at 10K nodes, and a TSP10K gap of 2.56% versus 5.63% without memory.
K41ebvrKaw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing computation across construction steps is well motivated and that label-free training with generalization to much larger instances is a strength, supported by memory ablations.
K41ebvrKaw.main_concern: Comparisons are not matched: MiLoop with 100-start decoding is compared with greedy or augmented baselines, and a candidate-set limit at inference may help it avoid out-of-memory failures that other baselines hit.

BiXNlDOdP1.one_liner: Benchmark that traces each procedural requirement from experience to retention to execution for self-evolving LLM agents.
BiXNlDOdP1.problem: Existing benchmarks show aggregate performance changes or retained-knowledge quality but not which procedural requirements are learned or where the experience-to-behavior pathway breaks.
BiXNlDOdP1.method: EvoTrace uses Agent-Executable Standard Operating Procedures (AE-SOPs) as a common reference to track each requirement across actual experience, explicit retention, and held-out execution, with 115 AE-SOPs across seven professional domains and 10,792 executable instances.
BiXNlDOdP1.key_idea: Align every procedural requirement to a shared AE-SOP reference so failures can be attributed to exposure, retention, or realization.
BiXNlDOdP1.evidence: Eleven representative self-evolution methods evaluated on 115 AE-SOPs, with a human audit and intervention experiments; reviewers note theorems on the non-identifiability of aggregate metrics.
BiXNlDOdP1.claimed_gains: No method gain claimed; the benchmark finds that similar forms of retained knowledge can yield substantially different gains, and broader coverage does not necessarily mean more reliable execution.
BiXNlDOdP1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the requirement-level view of experience, retention, and execution more informative than a single success score, with a broad method comparison and an explicit human audit.
BiXNlDOdP1.main_concern: Measurement noise undermines the diagnostic claims: 74.2% extraction recall for skill artifacts, a 34.5% false-acceptance rate on dependency judgments, and no sensitivity analysis or direct evidence that existing benchmarks mislead.

yK1Eeu3BzU.one_liner: Prompt-Invariant RLVR combines a trinary format-versus-content reward with an embedding-space adversarial consistency regularizer for multimodal LLMs.
yK1Eeu3BzU.problem: RLVR gains in MLLMs are brittle to rewording or answer-template changes because the binary verifier conflates format with content and training prompts cover few equivalent prompts.
yK1Eeu3BzU.method: PIRL uses a dynamic trinary reward that separates format from semantics, plus a consistency regularizer driven by an adversary in instruction-embedding space that enforces answer invariance across semantically equivalent prompts.
yK1Eeu3BzU.key_idea: Separate format from correctness in the reward and penalize answer changes under worst-case embedding-space prompt perturbations.
yK1Eeu3BzU.evidence: Exam, medical, and legal/document VQA with two Qwen-VL backbones, template stress tests, dynamic evaluation, and a GRPO-MT baseline using the same template pool.
yK1Eeu3BzU.claimed_gains: Under template stress testing PIRL's mean accuracy drops by only 0.1-0.4%, whereas GRPO drops 1.3-2.9.
yK1Eeu3BzU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the robustness gap is practically relevant and well diagnosed, the evaluation is diverse, and the GRPO-MT control separates PIRL's benefit from template augmentation.
yK1Eeu3BzU.main_concern: Novelty and mechanism are questioned: the components resemble existing reward-normalization and latent-adversarial consistency methods, the consistency penalty does not clearly disentangle format from semantics, and embedding perturbations may not mimic real prompt shifts.

imsHQJ18k8.one_liner: Represents the auxiliary modality in RGB-X detection as lightweight task factors that guide and refine RGB features.
imsHQJ18k8.problem: RGB-X detectors use parallel feature streams and focus on fusion, though the added task utility of X varies by sensing modality and detection task given a strong RGB representation.
imsHQJ18k8.method: TF-DETR keeps RGB as the primary semantic stream and encodes the auxiliary modality as Task Factors (explicit detection-oriented states plus sensor-dependent latent evidence), aligns them with global-anchored multi-scale task alignment, and feeds them into the RGB encoder through reliability-aware query guidance and bounded low-rank feature refinement.
imsHQJ18k8.key_idea: Encode X as task factors with reliability estimates, then inject aligned evidence into the RGB encoder via query guidance and low-rank refinement rather than a second semantic stream.
imsHQJ18k8.evidence: RGB-Thermal and RGB-Event object detection benchmarks; reviewers note six benchmarks covering event, thermal, and depth modalities.
imsHQJ18k8.claimed_gains: Claims leading detection performance on RGB-Thermal and RGB-Event benchmarks with a lightweight auxiliary pathway; no numbers stated.
imsHQJ18k8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the observation that the task utility of X varies by modality insightful, with experiments across many benchmarks showing fewer parameters and faster inference.
imsHQJ18k8.main_concern: Novelty is questioned: the RGB-primary asymmetric design and the component techniques (alignment, reliability gating, low-rank refinement) resemble prior multimodal detection work, with component-level analysis and RGB-D evidence lacking.

d2r5mgJnyr.one_liner: Trains object-centric encoders from masks using LeJEPA alignment in a semantic space and contrastive instance separation with copy-paste views.
d2r5mgJnyr.problem: Self-supervised image encoders need many images, and existing mask-supervised methods rely on reconstruction or contrastive losses with negative objects that require category definitions.
d2r5mgJnyr.method: Two projection spaces are used: a semantic space aligns per-object representations across views with an extended negative-free LeJEPA anti-collapse regularizer for variable-sized object sets, and an instance space uses a contrastive loss separating objects from their context and co-occurring instances. Copy-pasting objects into other contexts creates extra views.
d2r5mgJnyr.key_idea: Port LeJEPA's distributional anti-collapse regularizer to variable-size object sets for semantic alignment, plus a separate instance-space contrastive loss with copy-paste views.
d2r5mgJnyr.evidence: Pretraining on COCO with ground-truth masks, evaluated on downstream tasks across ten settings, dataset sizes down to 256 images, backbone capacities, and mask sources (e.g., ADE20k object classification and NAVI).
d2r5mgJnyr.claimed_gains: Outperforms image-level and mask-guided baselines when trained on COCO with ground-truth masks; the numbers are cut off in the abstract.
d2r5mgJnyr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the semantic/instance decomposition coherent, the data-efficiency gains and downstream results promising, and the evaluation broad across dataset sizes, backbones, and mask sources.
d2r5mgJnyr.main_concern: Limited novelty (it combines mask-level alignment, instance contrastive learning, and copy-paste), unclear why LeJEPA is needed when masks are available, and claims lack variance across independent pretraining runs.

fFS3TceVln.one_liner: Asymmetric two-sided test with entropy-weighted statistics detects LLM text whose watermark reverses detector score ordering.
fFS3TceVln.problem: Watermarked LLM text can reverse the score ordering used by logits-based detectors such as Fast-DetectGPT, causing detection to fail.
fFS3TceVln.method: Builds a two-sided test with separate upper and lower branches using a pair of asymmetric statistical measures. The upper reference mean and variance are adjusted by temperature scaling and nucleus truncation, and context entropy weights each token position.
fFS3TceVln.key_idea: Test both tails of the detection score separately with asymmetric statistics, reshaping the upper reference by temperature and nucleus truncation and weighting tokens by context entropy.
fFS3TceVln.evidence: Evaluated on 660 configuration settings (LLMs x watermarking methods x datasets) against Fast-DetectGPT and AdaDetectGPT using AUROC.
fFS3TceVln.claimed_gains: Mean AUROC exceeds Fast-DetectGPT by 0.1911 and AdaDetectGPT by 0.1968 across 660 settings.
fFS3TceVln.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the analysis of how watermarking breaks detectors is thorough and the detector performs well on watermarked text without extra training.
fFS3TceVln.main_concern: Limited novelty: the watermark-detector interaction was reported before and the method combines established techniques, with only 0.04 to 0.05 AUROC gain over a symmetric two-sided baseline.

sJVJEISFBZ.one_liner: Online tuning of discount factor and trace decay by comparing shared-network value heads with a central critic proxy.
sJVJEISFBZ.problem: Tuning discount factor and trace decay over many runs is costly, and existing dynamic adaptation methods are brittle, algorithm-specific, computationally heavy, or need costly policy evaluations.
sJVJEISFBZ.method: DOODAT adapts the discount factor and trace decay within a single run for value-based algorithms and is integrated into PQN and PPO. Per the reviews, auxiliary value heads with different hyperparameters share a network and a central critic is used as a proxy to judge which head performs best.
sJVJEISFBZ.key_idea: Use a central critic as a proxy to compare value heads with different discount and trace-decay values, shifting the hyperparameters toward the best head without differentiating through training.
sJVJEISFBZ.evidence: Compared against meta-gradient methods and non-adaptive baselines on PQN and PPO across multiple environment suites, with component ablations and appendix analyses.
sJVJEISFBZ.claimed_gains: Recovers high performance from suboptimal initial hyperparameters, reaching an IQM of 1.0; the baseline figure is cut off in the abstract.
sJVJEISFBZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) find the paper easy to follow, with solid empirical results, helpful ablations, low computational overhead, and gains especially when starting from poor initial hyperparameters.
sJVJEISFBZ.main_concern: The central critic is a weaker proxy than claimed (Kendall tau about 0.2), so the method may work mainly because wrong-direction updates are rare, and missing baselines such as random search, grid search, PBT and PB2 limit judgment of adaptation quality.

FZkUWYev4T.one_liner: Contrastive augmentation and a margin loss calibrate classifier guidance to steer autoregressive single-step retrosynthesis.
FZkUWYev4T.problem: Cross-entropy-trained classifiers are not confident enough on rare substructural token combinations such as reaction type to change an overconfident generator's ranking, so guidance fails to steer retrosynthesis.
FZkUWYev4T.method: Calibration for Autoregressive Guidance (CAG) trains the guidance classifier with contrastive augmentation and a margin-based loss so it can discriminate between continuations during decoding. It is applied at inference to a pretrained single-step model without retraining.
FZkUWYev4T.key_idea: Train the guidance classifier with contrastive augmentation and a margin loss so its prefix-level property estimates are confident enough to re-rank an overconfident autoregressive generator.
FZkUWYev4T.evidence: Experiments on USPTO-190 with chemist-specified reaction-type targets at every node; reviews also mention USPTO-50k and Schneider reaction classes.
FZkUWYev4T.claimed_gains: Routes meeting all specified reaction types for 27.4% of targets versus 9.5% for an unguided model and 23.7% for a cross-entropy classifier, and distinct routes per target rise from 2.1 for the unguided baseline (rest of abstract cut off).
FZkUWYev4T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) value the practical plug-and-play guidance of chemist preferences and the theoretically grounded diagnosis of why standard classifier guidance fails to rank paths.
FZkUWYev4T.main_concern: Gains over the authors' own cross-entropy classifier are modest and lack error bars, and a simple baseline of sampling more reactions and filtering by constraint appears strongest in Table 3.

509ozbvjTG.one_liner: Probes frozen visual encoders via nearest-neighbor demonstration retrieval and light action predictors for robot manipulation.
509ozbvjTG.problem: Robot visual representations are usually evaluated inside full visuomotor policies, so representation quality cannot be separated from downstream control.
509ozbvjTG.method: FakeVLA runs nearest-neighbor retrieval over demonstrations to test whether visual neighborhoods preserve end-effector state retrieval consistency, then trains lightweight action predictors to test what remains decodable. It compares generic, vision-language and VLA-derived encoders under controlled state and visual shifts against full VLA policies with frozen vision modules.
509ozbvjTG.key_idea: Measure Drift, the gap between visually retrieved and state-retrieved demonstration states, as a policy-free predictor of manipulation success for a frozen encoder.
509ozbvjTG.evidence: Compares generic, vision-language and VLA-derived encoders under state and visual shifts, with probe trends checked against full-VLA policies; reviews note only apple/banana pick-and-place tasks with 100 episodes each.
509ozbvjTG.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports only qualitative associations (lower Drift with higher manipulation success, texture shifts degrading most).
509ozbvjTG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) find the question of isolating the vision encoder from policy learning interesting and the encoder comparison broad, with useful diagnostic findings such as NN versus MLP behavior under visual shift.
509ozbvjTG.main_concern: The evaluation is narrow (only apple/banana pick-and-place with fixed placement locations) and the Drift and StateNN references are insufficiently justified, so findings may not generalize.

Avflih35YC.one_liner: Open pretraining recipe using FP8 on RTX 5090 GPUs, hyperball optimization and model averaging to train 2B models cheaply.
Avflih35YC.problem: Language model pretraining is prohibitively costly for academic and open-source groups, and no cost-efficient, hardware-accessible, fully open pretraining recipe exists.
Avflih35YC.method: Trains the Puro-2B collection from scratch on up to 1.4 trillion tokens with FP8 precision on consumer-grade RTX 5090 GPUs, combining hardware selection, low-precision training, hyperball optimization, curriculum model averaging and a data recipe. It also fits a Puro Cost Scaling Law relating training cost to average performance.
Avflih35YC.key_idea: Cut cost by combining consumer-GPU FP8 training, hyperball optimization, curriculum model averaging and a tuned data recipe, then fit a cost-to-performance scaling law.
Avflih35YC.evidence: Trains multiple Puro-2B models and evaluates them under the authors' protocol against Qwen-family models; reviews mention a 15-benchmark average and a scaling law fitted over the model collection.
Avflih35YC.claimed_gains: Best model trained for less than $6.9K and approaches Qwen2.5-1.5B performance; the fitted law says about $4.4K, less than $5,090, suffices to reach Qwen2-1.5B performance.
Avflih35YC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) value the unusually detailed open engineering documentation (data mixtures, checkpoints, code) and the demonstrated consumer-hardware FP8 training, including driver-level interconnect fixes.
Avflih35YC.main_concern: The cost comparison is not like-for-like (owned-hardware pricing, only the final run counted) and the 0.4-point margin over Qwen2-1.5B has no error bars, with possible benchmark contamination behind the model-averaging gain.

hmVlDPE9BE.one_liner: Benchmark of sequential part-level 3D edits with deterministic assembly-engine ground truth after every edit.
hmVlDPE9BE.problem: 3D editing methods are evaluated one edit at a time, so the ability to follow new instructions while preserving earlier edits and untouched regions is not measured.
hmVlDPE9BE.method: EditHero is a long-horizon 3D editing benchmark from image and natural-language instructions covering geometry and texture; a deterministic assembly engine produces the target after every edit and manual review verifies each sequence. It evaluates four 3D editing methods and six LLMs.
hmVlDPE9BE.key_idea: Generate ground truth for every intermediate edit state with a deterministic part-assembly engine so error accumulation and preservation of untouched regions can be measured.
hmVlDPE9BE.evidence: Evaluates four 3D editing methods and six LLMs that edit through code; reviews note the LLMs are tested on only 55 manually selected sequences and conventional methods build on TRELLIS latents.
hmVlDPE9BE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the part-assembly ground truth with every intermediate state enables reliable evaluation, with thorough experiments and metrics that separate instruction following from preservation.
hmVlDPE9BE.main_concern: Scale and analysis are limited: LLM methods are tested on only 55 hand-selected sequences, conventional editors and code-editing agents are compared unevenly, and the findings add little insight beyond documenting performance gaps.

S2FVm50WjS.one_liner: EEG foundation model with volume-conduction-aware channel encoding and neurodynamics statistics prediction pretraining.
S2FVm50WjS.problem: Most EEG foundation models transfer well only under end-to-end fine-tuning and degrade markedly under frozen probing, which the authors attribute to generic sequence architectures that ignore neural biophysics.
S2FVm50WjS.method: DeeperBrain adds a volume-conduction-aware channel encoding based on 3D electrode geometry and a neurodynamics-aware temporal encoding for slow oscillations and adaptive decay. Pretraining combines Masked EEG Reconstruction with Neurodynamics Statistics Prediction, which predicts spectral power, phase synchronization, cross-frequency coupling and signal complexity computed from the signal.
S2FVm50WjS.key_idea: Inject neurophysiological priors in the architecture (distance-decay spatial mixing, oscillatory and decay temporal encoding) and add an auxiliary objective predicting signal-derived neurodynamics statistics.
S2FVm50WjS.evidence: Pretrained on over 17,200 hours of heterogeneous EEG and evaluated on 12 downstream datasets spanning emotion, motor, sleep, seizure, speech, disorder, vigilance and workload tasks, under frozen probing and end-to-end fine-tuning.
S2FVm50WjS.claimed_gains: Pretrained on over 17,200 hours of EEG and evaluated on 12 downstream datasets; the result claim is cut off in the abstract after 'state-of-the-art or'.
S2FVm50WjS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the frozen-probing results are strong (wins on all twelve datasets in Table 4) and the neurophysiological priors in architecture and pretraining are a coherent, well-motivated design.
S2FVm50WjS.main_concern: The physiological interpretations of the spatial and temporal encodings are not validated beyond ablations, and the fine-tuning state-of-the-art claims lack significance tests with margins within about one standard deviation.

rkFNS5mirV.one_liner: Empirical study showing narrow multimodal fine-tuning induces broad emergent misalignment in vision-language models.
rkFNS5mirV.problem: Emergent misalignment has been studied almost entirely in text-only models, leaving its manifestation in multimodal models unclear.
rkFNS5mirV.method: Fine-tunes models on narrow multimodal tasks (vulnerable code, careless household-object use, conspiratorial readings of ordinary scenes) and measures transfer to unrelated tasks including misaligned opinions, visual dishonesty, unsafe image generation, visual jailbreaks and risky agentic actions. It also tests SFT versus preference optimization, reasoning propagation, and mitigations such as prompt inoculation, benign continued training and activation-level interventions.
rkFNS5mirV.key_idea: Fine-tune on narrow multimodal misbehavior and evaluate out-of-distribution misaligned dispositions, varying training-evaluation modality alignment to show EM depends on modality match rather than apparent data harmfulness.
rkFNS5mirV.evidence: Tested across fifteen commercial and open-source models of different scales under SFT and preference optimization; ablations and mitigations are mostly on Qwen3-VL-32B with the careless-object-use task.
rkFNS5mirV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the paper is well written and the evaluation is comprehensive across many models, datasets and downstream behaviors.
rkFNS5mirV.main_concern: The paper does not explain why EM arises or why factors such as image training, SFT versus DPO and consistent CoT matter, and it is unclear how EM differs from ordinary behavioral generalization.

Y0Ww5DnHS4.one_liner: Mixed-precision KV cache quantization restores higher precision in layers whose heads are most sensitive to agentic-coding failures.
Y0Ww5DnHS4.problem: Low-bit KV cache quantization in multi-turn agentic coding amplifies repetitive action loops, improper tool use and insufficient debugging, increasing the actions and tokens needed per task.
Y0Ww5DnHS4.method: Measures changes in attention distributions and head outputs under controlled KV cache perturbations to find the heads most sensitive to quantization around these failures (about 5% of heads, clustered in a few layers). It then keeps higher precision in the selected layers and low precision elsewhere.
Y0Ww5DnHS4.key_idea: Localize quantization-sensitive attention heads from attention-distribution shifts on failure segments and restore higher precision only in the layers containing them.
Y0Ww5DnHS4.evidence: SWE-bench Verified with Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, plus a Devstral-24B comparison and ablations across languages, model sizes and architectures per the reviews.
Y0Ww5DnHS4.claimed_gains: Raising average precision from 3.0 to 3.35 bits substantially reduces the three failures and brings task resolution close to BF16, while observed KV cache usage per case falls 12% versus uniform 3-bit quantization.
Y0Ww5DnHS4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree that evaluating KV quantization at trajectory level rather than per-token bits is a useful lens, and the failure-pattern analysis and ablations are informative.
Y0Ww5DnHS4.main_concern: Outcome deltas are small and no seeds, repeated runs or confidence intervals are reported, and baselines built for agentic KV compression and the behavior-category annotation are not validated.

kVWTeDawcD.one_liner: Three-stage physics-guided cascade uses multispectral images as a camera-agnostic bridge for cross-camera white balance and color correction.
kVWTeDawcD.problem: With only three RGB channels, separating illumination from reflectance is ill-posed, and color restoration is tied to a camera-specific raw space that must be recalibrated for each new sensor.
kVWTeDawcD.method: A single fixed multispectral camera feeds a three-stage framework that predicts camera spectral sensitivity (CSS) and white-balance gains, then applies per-image color correction. CSS is optimized in the sensor-response domain with CSS projection, so the model is trained once and transfers to a new RGB camera using its DNG ColorMatrices and a small set of MSI-RGB pairs.
kVWTeDawcD.key_idea: Project multispectral input through the target camera's recovered spectral sensitivity to separate sensor dependence from illumination learning, then derive an illuminant-dependent color correction matrix.
kVWTeDawcD.evidence: Experiments on 14 target camera models in a synthetic benchmark with ablations, plus a real-data check on one smartphone in an appendix.
kVWTeDawcD.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any results.
kVWTeDawcD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the physics-grounded decomposition into CSS, illuminant and dynamic CCM stages is interpretable and the ablations, especially CSS projection, support each component.
kVWTeDawcD.main_concern: Cross-camera generalization is weakly demonstrated (the main benchmark is synthetic and real data shows a visible domain gap), a new camera still needs paired MSI-RAW captures, and RGB baselines lack MSI-aware counterparts.

vxYwBdngJR.one_liner: Order-stable analytic anchor, bounded adaptation and class-view prototype mixing for ego-exo continual action recognition.
vxYwBdngJR.problem: Continual video learning is evaluated as sequences of new classes and ignores viewpoint shifts between first- and third-person views, where models may lose cross-view transfer or overwrite pretrained structure.
vxYwBdngJR.method: Introduces EgoExo-ViewCL, a view-labeled continual action benchmark built from EgoMe, Assembly101 and Charades-Ego with three protocols (view shift under a fixed label space, joint class-and-view expansion, sequential paired-view arrival). Proposes VFCT, which combines an order-stable analytic anchor, bounded semantic adaptation and cumulative class-view prototype score mixing.
vxYwBdngJR.key_idea: Keep shared action evidence in an order-stable analytic anchor while adapting only view-dependent cues in a bounded way, and mix class-view prototype scores cumulatively.
vxYwBdngJR.evidence: Three datasets, nine baselines, five class orders, single- and multi-label recognition, with view-order and true-versus-pseudo pairing controls.
vxYwBdngJR.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says VFCT consistently improves recognition under view switches, joint class-view expansion and paired-view transitions without giving numbers.
vxYwBdngJR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the benchmark is well motivated, with controlled protocols and broad evaluation beyond final accuracy, and that VFCT beats the baselines across datasets.
vxYwBdngJR.main_concern: Task construction entangles class arrival with viewpoint change, and VFCT's extra analytic statistics and prototypes are not matched across baselines (it loses to RanPAC at 16 MiB), so the source of the gains is unclear.

PBlM0SkzIK.one_liner: Training-free long-video frame acquisition conditioned on a compressed context via residual covariance and sequential query-weighted selection.
PBlM0SkzIK.problem: Frame selection and visual compression for long-video understanding ignore what the compressed view already preserves, although an added frame's value depends on both the question and the visible evidence.
PBlM0SkzIK.method: CoFi builds a query-independent compressed context, then conditions a state-trajectory relational prior on it to estimate residual covariance over candidate frames. It sequentially acquires full-resolution frames with a query-weighted acquisition score and updates the residual covariance after each selection.
PBlM0SkzIK.key_idea: Estimate a residual covariance over candidate frames conditioned on the compressed view, and greedily pick query-relevant full-resolution frames while updating that covariance after each pick.
PBlM0SkzIK.evidence: Matched 32-visual-unit budget on LLaVA-Video-7B across MLVU, LongVideoBench and Video-MME; Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL2.5-8B are compared only with uniform sampling.
PBlM0SkzIK.claimed_gains: Highest accuracy among evaluated methods on MLVU and LongVideoBench and competitive on Video-MME under a matched 32-visual-unit budget on LLaVA-Video-7B; no accuracy numbers are stated.
PBlM0SkzIK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree that conditioning frame selection on the compressed context already provided is a sensible idea, supported by extensive experiments over three benchmarks and several backbones.
PBlM0SkzIK.main_concern: The gain from context-conditioned residual modeling is small (0.78% and 0.45% over an unconditioned variant on MLVU and LongVideoBench, slightly worse on Video-MME), and the motivation and cross-backbone comparisons against strong selectors are limited.

Ayys9uid4U.one_liner: Per-patch scene tokens decoded to free Gaussians, merged to an inference-set budget, with cone and GeoCE losses.
Ayys9uid4U.problem: Pixel-aligned feed-forward Gaussian splatting yields redundant, possibly misaligned Gaussians across views, while token-based methods lack observation support and use a fixed reconstruction budget.
Ayys9uid4U.method: ZipSplat derives each scene token from an image patch, decodes it into freely placed 3D Gaussians, and merges tokens across views into a compact set whose size is adjustable at inference. A cone loss ties each token's Gaussians to its source patch, GeoCE aligns token similarity with 3D proximity, and TokenBA refines tokens and camera poses in a few seconds.
Ayys9uid4U.key_idea: Initialize scene tokens from image patches rather than learned queries, and use cone and GeoCE losses so merging groups tokens observing the same surface.
Ayys9uid4U.evidence: Feed-forward reconstruction from unposed images compared with pixel-aligned and token-based methods (abstract cut off); reviews cite ablations such as clustering by 3D position in Table 11.
Ayys9uid4U.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract and TL;DR say it outperforms pixel-aligned and token-based methods with far fewer Gaussians and needs neither camera poses nor intrinsics.
Ayys9uid4U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) find the observation-grounded tokens with an adjustable budget a well-motivated, effective design that outperforms competing methods with significantly fewer Gaussians.
Ayys9uid4U.main_concern: Novelty is incremental over TokenSplat, TokenGS and scaffold-GS (clustering by 3D position performs about the same), and one reviewer found the token terminology unclear.

iC8Bmj9kiY.one_liner: Heading-depth hierarchy poisoning (NDS) implants a backdoor in long-document LLM evaluators triggered by document structure.
iC8Bmj9kiY.problem: Document structure is usually treated as behaviorally neutral for long-document LLMs, but it may be exploitable as a learned behavioral signal.
iC8Bmj9kiY.method: Natural Document Structure poisoning (NDS) is a training-time intervention that associates a target heading-depth hierarchy with model behavior while preserving content and heading vocabulary. Controlled interventions swap heading text or heading depths, and an AutoResearch-style workflow tests whether generated manuscripts with an outline constraint activate a poisoned evaluator.
iC8Bmj9kiY.key_idea: Associate a target heading-depth configuration, independent of heading wording, with a target behavior during fine-tuning so that depth alone triggers it.
iC8Bmj9kiY.evidence: Tests across target hierarchies, model families, document distributions, parsers and a full-document QA task, with controlled interventions that change only heading text or only heading depths.
iC8Bmj9kiY.claimed_gains: With a 5% poisoning budget NDS reaches 92.45 +/- 0.63% target activation; replacing heading text keeps 91.82% activation, changing only heading depths drops it to 6.92%, and 72.50% of constrained generations comply (cut off).
iC8Bmj9kiY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) find the heading-depth trigger an interesting, well-motivated threat model with strong controlled experiments showing structure alone drives the effect.
iC8Bmj9kiY.main_concern: The attack needs fine-tuning (white-box) access to the evaluator, limiting realism for deployed systems, and the success metric depends on an LLM auditor that lacks independent validation.

yc20sODEjA.one_liner: Three-stage RGB-to-RAW reconstruction guided by squared vector-Jacobian-product sensitivity of a learned forward ISP.
yc20sODEjA.problem: ISP processing is lossy, so the RAW measurements behind an RGB image are hard to recover.
yc20sODEjA.method: FiberR2R first learns a differentiable forward ISP from paired RAW-RGB data, then predicts an RGB-conditioned RAW Anchor and trains a residual refiner around it. Squared VJP responses estimate local RGB response energy and parameterize Anchor-centered perturbation sampling and residual supervision; inference uses the Anchor plus one bounded residual refinement without evaluating the forward ISP.
yc20sODEjA.key_idea: Use squared vector-Jacobian-product responses of a learned forward ISP as sensitivity scores that set both perturbation sampling and residual loss weights around the RAW Anchor.
yc20sODEjA.evidence: Five camera-specific datasets, with ablations of VJP sampling-only, loss-only and uniform variants.
yc20sODEjA.claimed_gains: Highest SSIM on all five datasets and highest PSNR on four, with 11.49M inference parameters and 10.63 GFLOPs per 64x64 RGB window.
yc20sODEjA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the method gives strong reconstruction results with compact inference, supported by careful ablations of the VJP guidance and clear presentation.
yc20sODEjA.main_concern: Implementation details of the guidance (sensitivity smoothing, perturbation scale, probe count) and runtime or training cost are under-reported, and the sensitivity hypothesis is not statistically validated.

IwHpqA35Db.one_liner: LLM proposes one utility term at a time; greedy selection builds interpretable random utility models of human strategic behavior.
IwHpqA35Db.problem: Specifying the systematic utility in random utility models of human strategic behavior needs substantial domain expertise and manual refinement.
IwHpqA35Db.method: GreedyBM builds the systematic utility one term at a time; at each stage an LLM proposes candidate terms given the current utility and previously evaluated candidates, and the highest-scoring one is added. The authors derive a computable lower bound on single-stage training NLL reduction and a multi-stage bound relating candidate quality to attainable training NLL.
IwHpqA35Db.key_idea: Add one LLM-proposed behavioral term per stage to an additive utility, selecting by a score tied to a provable lower bound on training NLL reduction.
IwHpqA35Db.evidence: Three strategic scenarios (Ultimatum Game, repeated rock-paper-scissors, continuous double auctions), compared with expert-designed models and existing LLM-based model discovery methods such as AutoBM.
IwHpqA35Db.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports lower mean test NLL than expert-designed and existing LLM-discovered models with substantially fewer tokens.
IwHpqA35Db.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the term-by-term construction is a sensible, inspectable way to structure LLM-based model discovery, with a statistical selection score, a training-loss guarantee and large token savings.
IwHpqA35Db.main_concern: Empirical margins are thin (GreedyBM and AutoBM overlap within confidence bounds and efficiency is shown on one run), and the benefit of the proposed score is not isolated from term-by-term construction.

anOjWFxmTA.one_liner: Benchmark evaluating what transfers when universal interatomic potentials are fine-tuned on ensemble-derived experimental observables.
anOjWFxmTA.problem: Existing uMLIP benchmarks score pretrained models against DFT or experiment, although practitioners fine-tune to experiments and nobody has measured what that does off-target.
anOjWFxmTA.method: ExFiT-Bench fine-tunes six uMLIPs under a shared protocol on five tasks (elastic constants, a phase transition and a liquid structure factor in titanium, diamond and MgO) using experimental ensemble properties as labels. It evaluates the target observable and transfer to held-out temperatures, another polymorph, other observables and compositions.
anOjWFxmTA.key_idea: Fine-tune on ensemble-level experimental observables without per-configuration labels, then test transfer across temperature, polymorph, observable and composition.
anOjWFxmTA.evidence: Six uMLIPs on five tasks over titanium, diamond and MgO, with three seeds per the reviews, and held-out temperatures, a polymorph, observables and compositions.
anOjWFxmTA.claimed_gains: not stated; findings are qualitative (on-target error falls for every model on every task, pretrained ranking does not carry over, transfer across observables and compositions is less reliable).
anOjWFxmTA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the question of off-target effects after experimental fine-tuning is important and well motivated, with careful physics and a reproducible shared protocol.
anOjWFxmTA.main_concern: Scope is narrow (three materials, three of five tasks are elastic constants, some tasks reproduce earlier work), so conclusions about transfer across compositions are thinly supported and unexplained.

PbdsrmhaI3.one_liner: Looped Transformer trained to complete and correct partially wrong candidate solutions via masking and token-replacement discrete denoising.
PbdsrmhaI3.problem: Learning to refine intermediate answers is hard when supervision provides only completed solutions without intermediate reasoning trajectories.
PbdsrmhaI3.method: The Discrete Reasoning Diffusion Model (DRDM) trains a looped Transformer to reconstruct solutions from partially correct candidates, using masking and token replacement to create completion and correction tasks. A shared core performs several latent updates before predicting tokens, and progressive decoding adds assignments, allows revision and carries latent memory between steps.
PbdsrmhaI3.key_idea: Build refinement training problems by masking and replacing tokens in completed solutions, then solve them with a shared recurrent core using progressive decoding with revisable assignments.
PbdsrmhaI3.evidence: Three training seeds on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard and ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 with an approximately 7M-parameter model, compared with self-attention TRM.
PbdsrmhaI3.claimed_gains: 85.2% exact accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme, 87.3% on Maze-Hard and 50.5% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1, exceeding self-attention TRM by 9.7, 2.7 and 7.3 percentage points, with 4.8% fewer forward FLOPs at matched inference budgets.
PbdsrmhaI3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (2/3/4) agree that training on corrupted solution candidates without intermediate-step annotations is a natural approach and that DRDM improves over TRM on several reasoning tasks.
PbdsrmhaI3.main_concern: Contributions of the components are not isolated and the novelty over TRM, GIDD and Loopholing is unclear, with gains varying by task.

OnWCwEgfV4.one_liner: Benchmark of 400 reference-guided video editing cases with checklist-based five-dimension evaluation (RVE-Eval).
OnWCwEgfV4.problem: Existing benchmarks for reference-guided video editing do not build challenge-specific cases, so capability-specific failures go undetected.
OnWCwEgfV4.method: RVEBench has 400 human-calibrated cases and 5,672 fine-grained checklist questions across six scenarios in Spatial Perception, Temporal Modeling, Semantic Reasoning and Symbolic Fidelity. RVE-Eval combines sample-specific checklists and rubrics to separate edit execution, reference grounding, source preservation, perceptual quality, and physical or logical plausibility.
OnWCwEgfV4.key_idea: Score each edit with sample-specific checklists and rubrics along five separate dimensions so that edit execution is not masked by source preservation or visual polish.
OnWCwEgfV4.evidence: Experiments on ten configurations spanning seven models, with human validation on 60 cases (rank correlation over five configurations per case, per a review).
OnWCwEgfV4.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports qualitative findings only (polished but implausible videos, capability-specific failures, growing unintended changes as edits accumulate).
OnWCwEgfV4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the six challenge scenarios and the five-dimension evaluation give good diagnostic value for reference-guided video editing.
OnWCwEgfV4.main_concern: Validation of the evaluation is thin: human agreement covers only five configurations per 60 cases, sparse checklists may miss errors, and the unweighted Overall Avg is not justified.

GFsNe4TKc1.one_liner: Training-free expert skipping for MoE multimodal LLMs using layer- and modality-specific sensitivity-derived routing-mass thresholds.
GFsNe4TKc1.problem: Fixed Top-K routing activates the same number of experts per token, creating large overhead for visual-token-heavy inputs, and existing training-free skipping uses coarse or layer-shared criteria that ignore varying skipping tolerance.
GFsNe4TKc1.method: SLaMES calibrates sensitivity across layers, modalities and skipping ratios, uses offline lookup to search layer- and modality-specific thresholds with a few full-model forward passes, and skips experts by cumulative routing probability mass with conditional Top-1 protection for the dominant expert.
GFsNe4TKc1.key_idea: Calibrate per-layer, per-modality skipping sensitivity and search thresholds on cumulative routing probability mass so tolerant layers and visual tokens skip more experts.
GFsNe4TKc1.evidence: Three MoE MLLMs (16B to 122B per the reviews) on nine image and video benchmarks, integrated into vLLM with prefill speedup measured from 720p to 4K inputs.
GFsNe4TKc1.claimed_gains: Retains at least 99.25% of original performance at a 50% expert-skipping ratio and 96.39%-98.14% at 83.4%-87.5% skipping, consistently outperforming existing expert-skipping methods; vLLM gains are cut off in the abstract.
GFsNe4TKc1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the method is training-free, applies directly to existing models and maintains performance across multiple models and tasks, with real vLLM speedups.
GFsNe4TKc1.main_concern: Per-layer sensitivity is measured with other layers intact although multi-layer skipping interacts, and realized skipping ratios deviate from targets (71.4% realized versus an 83.4% target on Kimi-VL), so main-table comparisons are not compute-matched.

Dand0GuG3b.one_liner: Adversarial training on local molecular similarity graphs jointly trains predictor and risk head for accept-or-defer decisions.
Dand0GuG3b.problem: Post-hoc rejection rules attached to independently trained predictors still accept risky molecular analogues or reject reliable ones.
Dand0GuG3b.method: Reject-to-Protect (R2P) builds a frozen structure-only candidate graph from molecular similarity and, within local neighborhoods, runs a discrete inner maximization that finds unsafe-acceptance and over-rejection failures. An outer minimization trains a risk head, and optionally the predictor, under an explicit target-coverage constraint, with the risk head supervised by scaffold out-of-fold prediction harm.
Dand0GuG3b.key_idea: Mine unsafe-acceptance and over-rejection cases among structurally similar molecules as adversarial endpoints and train the risk head and predictor on them under a coverage constraint.
Dand0GuG3b.evidence: Nine MoleculeNet benchmarks at 80% coverage, with ablations and risk-coverage curves.
Dand0GuG3b.claimed_gains: On nine MoleculeNet benchmarks at 80% coverage it achieves the lowest mean selective risk on five of six (rest of the sentence cut off).
Dand0GuG3b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (4/3/2) agree the decision-aware formulation of unsafe acceptance and over-rejection addresses a practical problem, with leakage-aware design and benefits across nine datasets.
Dand0GuG3b.main_concern: The contribution of adversarial training is not isolated from extra training (R2P(Base) gets no further optimization), and strong ensemble and learned-selector baselines plus cost analysis are missing.

GYm4mg9yGQ.one_liner: Mechanistic analysis of input-level improvements from low-bit quantization, with rank-eight subspace adaptation built from them.
GYm4mg9yGQ.problem: Low-bit quantization lowers average performance yet improves some individual predictions, and it is unclear which activation changes give lower loss than the high-precision model or whether they share structure across inputs.
GYm4mg9yGQ.method: Analyzes quantization-induced activation changes in Llama and Qwen models (GPTQ, AWQ, NF4, OmniQuant at 3 and 4 bits) through per-unit loss-reducing contributions and interventions that replace, strengthen or suppress quantized activations. Builds local adjustments from these changes and a low-rank subspace for mechanism-guided adaptation (abstract cut off).
GYm4mg9yGQ.key_idea: Decompose per-input loss change into first-order contributions of quantization-induced activation displacements, then reuse the favorable displacements as a shared low-rank adaptation subspace.
GYm4mg9yGQ.evidence: Llama and Qwen models, several quantizers at 3 and 4 bits, causal activation interventions, on HANS and MMLU; per the reviews most mechanistic and adaptation experiments use a single 4-bit GPTQ model.
GYm4mg9yGQ.claimed_gains: A rank-eight subspace retains 96.06% and 88.21% of the cross-entropy improvement on HANS for Llama and Qwen, versus 24.77% and 18.89% on MMLU.
GYm4mg9yGQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree this is an interesting, first-of-its-kind input-level study of quantization-induced improvements, with consistent evidence that the improvements are structured rather than random.
GYm4mg9yGQ.main_concern: Null controls are missing (for example noise-injected layers or full-precision activation edits), so it is not established that the structure comes from quantization, and validation covers only two models and few tasks.

iYPGjL79Qx.one_liner: Generative model for molecular crystal structure prediction with flexible conditioning and cacheable pairwise refinement.
iYPGjL79Qx.problem: Molecular crystal structure prediction is hard because subtle conformation and packing differences change material properties, and existing generative approaches have limited conditioning flexibility and inconsistent evaluation.
iYPGjL79Qx.method: Packora jointly predicts atomic coordinates and lattice from molecular graphs and accepts any subset of conformers, stereochemical labels and space-group information, supporting multi-component and organometallic crystals. It combines cacheable pairwise refinement, training objectives and solvers chosen by systematic studies, conditioning dropout and balanced scaling of pairwise and single representations, plus an evaluation suite that separates generation from ranking following the CCDC blind test.
iYPGjL79Qx.key_idea: Jointly generate coordinates and lattice with optional conditioning on conformers, stereochemistry and space group, using cacheable pairwise refinement chosen through controlled design studies.
iYPGjL79Qx.evidence: Systematic studies of architecture, training, conditioning, inference and scaling, evaluated on six generation benchmarks and a new generation-versus-ranking suite.
iYPGjL79Qx.claimed_gains: Highest coverage across all six generation benchmarks and better results than baselines in both generation and ranking settings; the remaining numbers are cut off in the abstract.
iYPGjL79Qx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the systematic, controlled design studies are the main contribution and give useful guidance, and the generation/ranking protocol improves on prior evaluation.
iYPGjL79Qx.main_concern: Close design decisions rest on small margins without training-seed variance, conditioning accuracy for stereo and space-group labels is not directly evaluated, and methodological novelty is limited.

IVUfsgjVmc.one_liner: On-policy distillation that transfers teacher pairwise token preferences with adaptive margins and candidate-set mass control.
IVUfsgjVmc.problem: Standard on-policy distillation matches numerical token probabilities and does not make explicit which candidates compete and how strongly the teacher prefers one over another.
IVUfsgjVmc.method: Rank-OPD selects decision-relevant candidate relations, sets their required separation by teacher preference strength, and adds candidate-set mass control. Rank-OPD-T converts relation violations into bounded probability transport and combines the ranking-refined dense target with candidate-set mass matching.
IVUfsgjVmc.key_idea: Supervise the student with selected pairwise teacher preference relations whose margins scale with preference strength, and fix violations by bounded probability transport.
IVUfsgjVmc.evidence: Eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks compared with standard OPD, SFT, GRPO, EOPD and AOPD, plus mechanistic analyses and ablations.
IVUfsgjVmc.claimed_gains: Average scores of 42.01% for Rank-OPD and 43.69% for Rank-OPD-T versus 41.19% for standard OPD, with Rank-OPD-T best on six benchmarks.
IVUfsgjVmc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree that transferring the teacher's local preference structure is a reasonable, clearly specified idea with consistent gains over OPD baselines and informative component ablations.
IVUfsgjVmc.main_concern: The headline gain stacks sparse-to-dense matching with ranking correction (standalone Rank-OPD is only +0.28 over EOPD), and the contribution over existing ranking distillation such as TSD-KD is not established.

xiedU1TaN3.one_liner: Active inverse RL in Stackelberg games where the leader picks policies by Fisher-information experimental design.
xiedU1TaN3.problem: Rewards that explain behavior observed from a fixed policy pair may not induce optimal strategies when used for decision-making in strategic multi-agent settings.
xiedU1TaN3.method: Proposes an active IRL algorithm for Stackelberg games with an entropy-regularized follower and linear reward, where the leader adaptively selects policies to elicit informative responses. It combines maximum-likelihood estimation with experimental design to derive finite-sample guarantees on Stackelberg sub-optimality.
xiedU1TaN3.key_idea: Choose leader policies by experimental design on Fisher information so follower responses identify the reward directions that matter for Stackelberg decisions.
xiedU1TaN3.evidence: Theory: a fixed-policy impossibility result and finite-sample sub-optimality guarantees matching a new minimax lower bound of order K^(-1/2) up to polylogarithmic factors; the abstract is cut off before the experiments.
xiedU1TaN3.claimed_gains: Finite-sample guarantees on Stackelberg sub-optimality matching, up to polylogarithmic factors, a new minimax learning rate of K^(-1/2).
xiedU1TaN3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/2/4) agree that targeting strategically effective rather than exact reward recovery is meaningful, the fixed-policy impossibility result motivates active exploration, and the theoretical analysis is substantial.
xiedU1TaN3.main_concern: Novelty over prior active Stackelberg learning work needs sharper delineation, and the bounds leave gaps (dimension d, exponential warm-up samples) while exploration costs to the leader are ignored.

9mWB7cxhKy.one_liner: Prefix-autoregressive routing solver caching key-value states with a cache-compatible pointer decoder, cutting per-step decoding to O(N).
9mWB7cxhKy.problem: Scaling autoregressive neural combinatorial optimization solvers to larger instances is hard under RL because of long horizons, sparse rewards and expensive decoding.
9mWB7cxhKy.method: PrefixCO encodes instance attributes into reusable prefix representations and generates solutions causally with cached key-value states, computing static instance information once. A cache-compatible pointer decoder matches prefix-derived node keys with a trajectory-conditioned query, and training adds a new scheme that is cut off in the abstract (a reviewer identifies reward shaping).
9mWB7cxhKy.key_idea: Encode static instance information once as a reusable prefix and decode with cached key-value states so each step conditions on the evolving partial solution at O(N) cost.
9mWB7cxhKy.evidence: TSP and CVRP across several instance sizes (up to TSP-1000 per the reviews), with ablations and baselines tuned over multiple hyperparameter settings.
9mWB7cxhKy.claimed_gains: Reduces average per-step decoding complexity to O(N) from O(N^2); no benchmark numbers are visible in the cut-off abstract.
9mWB7cxhKy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the paper is clearly written and shows a practical efficiency gain on large routing instances, with evaluation on TSP and CVRP and ablations of each module.
9mWB7cxhKy.main_concern: Scalability evidence is limited (at most TSP-1000 versus TSP-10000 in other work) and novelty is limited as a combination of existing ideas, with ablations that do not cleanly isolate components.

xahPQOQYAe.one_liner: Global and local latent visual memories with an RL access policy re-inject visual evidence during multimodal reasoning.
xahPQOQYAe.problem: As multimodal LLMs reason for longer, attention to the initial visual input diminishes, weakening visual grounding.
xahPQOQYAe.method: ReMAP couples a static, question-conditioned Global memory preserving scene and cross-image context with a dynamic Local memory that selects and re-encodes region-level evidence using the current reasoning state. Both return compact latent tokens inserted into the reasoning sequence, and an RL access policy trained with branched rollouts decides when to continue reasoning or invoke Global or Local memory.
xahPQOQYAe.key_idea: Insert compact latent tokens from a global and an anchored local memory into the reasoning stream, with an RL policy deciding when to call each.
xahPQOQYAe.evidence: Ten benchmark families and four backbones, with a controlled analysis of memory curation, organization and access.
xahPQOQYAe.claimed_gains: Outperforms prior visual-memory methods on all four multi-image benchmarks, exceeding the strongest prior results on MuirBench and MIMIC by 8.38 and 14.84 percentage points.
xahPQOQYAe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the combination of question-conditioned global context and state-dependent local re-inspection is well motivated and targets the visual forgetting problem.
xahPQOQYAe.main_concern: Efficiency claims rest on reduced decoder visual tokens without end-to-end latency or memory measurements, and the VisMem baseline score on MuirBench (57.00%) differs from its original report (69.8%).

EKnbudzM6C.one_liner: Self-distillation that weights teacher guidance by retained exploration, a middle-layer signal of persistent semantically diverse alternatives.
EKnbudzM6C.problem: On-policy self-distillation with a privileged-information teacher contracts latent exploration, which coincides with late-stage reasoning degradation.
EKnbudzM6C.method: RESD defines retained exploration, a token-level signal of whether semantically diverse exploration persists across layers, and uses it to preserve exploration-supported teacher guidance while counteracting over-concentrated preferences at low-retained-exploration positions.
EKnbudzM6C.key_idea: Compute per-token retained exploration from middle-layer distributions decoded with the final unembedding matrix and use it to route teacher guidance, correcting over-concentrated preferences where exploration is low.
EKnbudzM6C.evidence: Three models (Qwen and SmolLM families) on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks against RLVR and self-distillation baselines, with layer-wise tracing of GRPO versus OPSD.
EKnbudzM6C.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says it consistently outperforms strong RLVR and self-distillation baselines across three models and five mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
EKnbudzM6C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the internal-state perspective is well motivated and RESD gives consistent gains over baselines across models and benchmarks, supported by ablations of the routing signal.
EKnbudzM6C.main_concern: The contribution relative to the closely related DASD is not fully established (no comparison with the complete method), and significance tests and full compute cost (about 1.6x GRPO per step) are not reported.

MHORiHecMd.one_liner: Zero-shot anomaly detection that contrasts normal and anomalous memory-bank retrieval via differential similarity on CLIP features.
MHORiHecMd.problem: Existing zero-shot anomaly detection methods generalize poorly under large cross-domain visual distribution shifts.
MHORiHecMd.method: DeltaAD amplifies anomaly-related differences and suppresses variations shared by normal and anomalous responses through differential similarity. DeltaAD-TF freezes the CLIP image encoder and contrasts retrieval from separate normal and anomalous region-feature memory banks, while DeltaAD-LE learns a residual relation of anomalies relative to retrieved normal visual explanations.
MHORiHecMd.key_idea: Score anomalies by the difference between normal-bank and anomalous-bank retrieval evidence under shared visual context, cancelling variation common to both responses.
MHORiHecMd.evidence: 15 industrial and medical benchmarks at image and pixel level, with train-free and training-based variants compared against CLIP-based methods such as MRAD.
MHORiHecMd.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports strong zero-shot generalization on 15 industrial and medical benchmarks at image and pixel level.
MHORiHecMd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the reasoning is clear and well supported by variance analysis and ablations, with meaningful improvements for both the train-free and training-based variants.
MHORiHecMd.main_concern: Comparisons are limited to CLIP-based baselines (missing AnomalyVFM, DiAD and MambaAD), and the difference from MRAD and the fit of the motivation to the DeltaAD-LE variant need clarification.

q8ZcQWezHQ.one_liner: Minimax regret characterization of shadow evaluation under imperfect request pairing via a posterior-contamination spectrum.
q8ZcQWezHQ.problem: Same-request comparisons in shadow evaluation cancel shared variation, but imperfect pairing leaves comparison quality uncertain, and aggregate provenance metrics can hide large differences in learning performance.
q8ZcQWezHQ.method: Studies bounded i.i.d. losses with a gap-dependent second-moment bound on same-request loss differences and marginal-preserving independent resampling, and derives matching minimax regret bounds governed by the posterior-contamination spectrum H(s)=E[1/(s+Z)]. It gives a calibrated inverse-variance weighting method and an order-only method that retains polynomial regret rates without calibration.
q8ZcQWezHQ.key_idea: Quantify provenance value by the spectrum H(s)=E[1/(s+Z)] of the posterior independent-resampling probability, which controls comparison precision and the lower bound for adaptive policies.
q8ZcQWezHQ.evidence: Matching upper and lower minimax regret bounds up to logarithmic factors, plus a pre-specified replication at T=2^18 with full budget and a near-clean tail exponent of 1/4 (abstract cut off).
q8ZcQWezHQ.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract gives minimax regret bounds matching up to logarithmic factors rather than empirical gains.
q8ZcQWezHQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the matching upper and lower bounds and the equal-accuracy, equal-mutual-information separation make a compelling theoretical characterization of provenance value.
q8ZcQWezHQ.main_concern: The observation model is restrictive and its practical relevance is weakly justified (supplied mismatch probabilities, fragile fast-rate regime, no clear service gains in experiments), and the paper is hard to read.

bSH82qjvtO.one_liner: One-million-image benchmark with edit-consistent filtered forgeries and technical and simplified explanations for explainable deepfake detection.
bSH82qjvtO.problem: Deepfake detectors that produce natural-language explanations are often weakly grounded in visual artifacts, and existing benchmarks mainly measure classification accuracy.
bSH82qjvtO.method: XPlainVerse pairs real images from five sources with forgeries from twelve editing and synthesis models, filtered by the Edit-Check multi-stage pipeline that verifies manipulations satisfy their intended edits. It provides technical and simplified explanations and proposes EntityScore and EvidenceScore metrics for whether explanations capture the manipulated entities and supporting evidence.
bSH82qjvtO.key_idea: Filter generated forgeries with Edit-Check for edit consistency and score explanations by whether they mention the manipulated entities and supporting evidence from reference explanations.
bSH82qjvtO.evidence: One million real and manipulated images (500K base images plus perturbed counterparts per a reviewer), human annotation of the metrics (abstract cut off), and cross-generator and region-swap experiments.
bSH82qjvtO.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before any results.
bSH82qjvtO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the large-scale benchmark with edit-consistency filtering and dual-style explanations addresses a worthwhile gap beyond binary deepfake detection.
bSH82qjvtO.main_concern: Reference explanations were generated using original images and edit instructions, so they may not reflect artifacts visible in the edited image alone, and metric validity against human judgment is unclear.

Fp52PZWzTg.one_liner: Policy-value-guided Monte Carlo tree search running inside Lean 4, trained with search-based reinforcement learning on a 1.7B model.
Fp52PZWzTg.problem: Formal proof search lacks an open framework that shares proof-state transitions between training and inference and exposes how neural predictions and tactic execution interact.
Fp52PZWzTg.method: Reap implements policy-value-guided MCTS with AND-OR search and replay verification directly in Lean, shared between inference and training rollouts, with structured action logs. Reaper-1, a 1.7B policy-value model, is trained by continued pre-training, supervised tactic learning and iterative search-based RL, and used with a separate premise selector.
Fp52PZWzTg.key_idea: Run the semantics-critical MCTS loop natively in Lean, shared by inference and RL training rollouts, so proof-state transitions and replay verification are identical in both.
Fp52PZWzTg.evidence: miniF2F-test at pass@32 against open provers, with ablations of the value head and premise selection (Section 4.4 per the reviews).
Fp52PZWzTg.claimed_gains: Solves 79.9% of miniF2F-test at pass@32, stated as state-of-the-art among open provers of comparable size and competitive with substantially larger models.
Fp52PZWzTg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the Lean-native search infrastructure is well motivated, the miniF2F result is at or near the state of the art for its size, and the ablations and behavioral analysis are informative.
Fp52PZWzTg.main_concern: The benefit of value-guided MCTS is unclear (193 versus 195 solved problems without value guidance, no compute-matched simpler-search baselines), and pass@32 comparisons across whole-proof and step-level systems are not budget-equal.

jpSRTgPRnR.one_liner: Training-free inference-time restoration of fact-rule value channels at layers located by an unlabeled collapse proxy.
jpSRTgPRnR.problem: LLMs are brittle on logical reasoning as proofs deepen or distractors accumulate, with representations losing selectivity toward proof-relevant evidence.
jpSRTgPRnR.method: Introduces Inferential Information Flow (IIF), a layer-wise diagnostic of whether a model preserves selectivity toward proof-relevant evidence over distractors, which reveals 'cascade IIF collapse'. FRGI (Fact-Rule Grouped Intervention) uses query-conditioned saliency to select candidate fact and rule spans and an Unlabeled Collapse Proxy to locate intervention layers, then restores fact-rule and value-channel representations without retraining.
jpSRTgPRnR.key_idea: Select fact and rule spans by query-conditioned saliency and edit their value-channel representations at layers where an unlabeled proxy indicates collapse.
jpSRTgPRnR.evidence: Three model families and three logical reasoning benchmarks (including ProverQA), with causal interventions and ablations such as Table 17.
jpSRTgPRnR.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract is cut off before any accuracy results.
jpSRTgPRnR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the layer-wise diagnostic gives useful insight into how proof-relevant information evolves and that FRGI is a practical training-free intervention with consistent gains across models and benchmarks.
jpSRTgPRnR.main_concern: Most of the gain may come from generic activation suppression rather than collapse repair (zeroing the selected value vectors lifts LLaMA from 44.20% to 70.20% versus 75.52% for full FRGI), and the IIF proxies do not directly establish collapse.

7ngGo6C7sB.one_liner: Causal per-frame perturbations that follow moving content protect streamed video against unauthorized 4D reconstruction.
7ngGo6C7sB.problem: Existing protection perturbs images or complete videos before release, but live streams are released causally frame by frame, and recorded viewers can reconstruct them as 4D assets.
7ngGo6C7sB.method: Safe4D generates each frame's protection without future frames or revisions, addressing temporal detachment (perturbations drifting off moving content and averaged out by motion-aligned purification), purification uncertainty (raw versus purified input) and irrevocable release (8-bit rounding). Per the reviews, it optimizes each perturbation with multiple surrogate evaluations per frame (64 calls by default).
7ngGo6C7sB.key_idea: Make each frame's perturbation follow object motion so motion-aligned averaging cannot cancel it, while accounting for purified inputs and 8-bit rounding.
7ngGo6C7sB.evidence: Depth-error evaluation on Sintel, Bonn, KITTI and TUM sequences against feed-forward 4D models, with transfer to VGGT and STream3R, temporal-filtering robustness and a 4DGS experiment per the reviews (abstract cut off).
7ngGo6C7sB.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before results.
7ngGo6C7sB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the causal-release protection problem is important and new, and that the idea that the perturbation must follow the object is correct and clearly explained.
7ngGo6C7sB.main_concern: In the main white-box setting it is barely better than copying the previous frame's noise (Sintel 0.476 versus 0.478) and it is too slow for real-time streaming (about 9.35 hours for 300 frames).

dNgakQfZ3M.one_liner: Training-free mask-guided image-to-3D fusion that routes each sparse query to one condition source via a 3D ownership field.
dNgakQfZ3M.problem: Image-conditioned 3D generators cannot assign an independent reference image to a user-masked region; treating multiple images as global conditions leaks reference appearance outside the region and weakens preservation elsewhere.
dNgakQfZ3M.method: A Mask-Conditioned Ownership Estimator lifts the 2D mask to a sparse 3D owner field by contrasting frozen cross-attention responses to selected and competing foreground patches. Owner-Exclusive Hierarchical Routing restricts every sparse query to its assigned condition source throughout the generator hierarchy, and Categorical Ownership Resolution resolves competing part assignments for multi-part fusion.
dNgakQfZ3M.key_idea: Estimate a sparse 3D ownership field from contrasted cross-attention and hard-route each query to its owning condition source throughout the generator hierarchy.
dNgakQfZ3M.evidence: Single-mask and multi-part benchmarks scored by CLIP-I and DINO-I, ablations of ownership and routing components, and comparisons with Fuse3D and image-editing models; the generator is TRELLIS.2 per the reviews.
dNgakQfZ3M.claimed_gains: not stated; the cut-off abstract reports accurate local reference transfer across diverse object categories and visual styles without numbers.
dNgakQfZ3M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree the training-free sparse-ownership formulation is intuitive and the qualitative results show useful local appearance transfer while preserving unselected regions.
dNgakQfZ3M.main_concern: Novelty over Fuse3D is narrower than claimed and that comparison changes the generator (TRELLIS versus TRELLIS.2), with weak image-based metrics and few hard or failure cases shown.

iF7LH6FiTU.one_liner: Diffusion peptide design guided by flexibility-conditioned out-of-distribution exploration and hotspot-driven hierarchical affinity guidance.
iF7LH6FiTU.problem: Generative peptide models rely on static structural representations and stay close to training-data patterns, limiting functionally diverse conformations and generalization to unseen scenarios.
iF7LH6FiTU.method: PhyDiff adds Flexibility-Conditioned Out-of-Distribution Exploration, which conditions generation on structural flexibility to explore the conformational landscape, and Hotspot-Driven Hierarchical Affinity Guidance, which steers exploration toward high-affinity binding modes by prioritizing hotspot interactions. A flexibility predictor trained on molecular dynamics data supplies the flexibility signal.
iF7LH6FiTU.key_idea: Condition diffusion on predicted structural flexibility to push samples out of distribution, and add classifier-style affinity guidance weighted toward hotspot residues.
iF7LH6FiTU.evidence: Multiple peptide design benchmarks with ablations of the two modules (the abstract is cut off before results).
iF7LH6FiTU.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract is cut off before any results.
iF7LH6FiTU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (2/3/4) agree that incorporating peptide flexibility and hotspot interactions into generation is a relevant, underexplored direction and that the method shows improvements across several benchmarks.
iF7LH6FiTU.main_concern: The guidance components are not well justified or isolated (why flexibility should drive out-of-distribution exploration, separate effects of the hotspot and affinity terms) and methodological novelty is limited.

WO8vBGLZ2C.one_liner: Quality-labeled imitation policy fine-tuned by iterative hindsight relabeling of online rollouts by measured speed and smoothness.
WO8vBGLZ2C.problem: Robot policies are judged by binary success, but deployment also needs controllable execution quality such as speed and motion smoothness.
WO8vBGLZ2C.method: The Quality-Controllable Policy (QCP) is conditioned on quality labels so individual attributes and their combinations can be controlled at inference. An iterative loop collects rollouts under target quality labels, adds successful trajectories, relabels them in hindsight by measured quality and fine-tunes the policy to extend the controllable range beyond the demonstrations.
WO8vBGLZ2C.key_idea: Condition the policy on quality labels computed from analytic metrics, and iteratively relabel successful rollouts by their measured quality to extend the quality range beyond the demonstrations.
WO8vBGLZ2C.evidence: Robomimic and RoboEval simulations plus real-world conveyor-speed and wine-glass transport tasks.
WO8vBGLZ2C.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports consistent improvements in execution quality and success rate across iterations, with rollouts exceeding the quality of the initial demonstrations.
WO8vBGLZ2C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree that execution quality beyond success is a practically relevant problem and the method is simple and easy to integrate, with broad simulation and real-world experiments.
WO8vBGLZ2C.main_concern: The relabel-and-retrain recipe closely follows prior work such as Quark and relies on pre-specified analytic quality metrics, with unresolved trade-offs between success rate and quality.

0tRbH9VK6A.one_liner: Single-bitstream generative video codec decoded by a bidirectional diffusion transformer or a distilled windowed autoregressive one.
0tRbH9VK6A.problem: Video diffusion codecs force a trade-off: bidirectional models give high quality but need the whole sequence and add latency, while autoregressive models stream with low delay but compress less efficiently.
0tRbH9VK6A.method: UniGVC shares a hierarchical latent codec that recurrently produces ultra-low-bitrate conditions for two decoders: UniGVC-BI, a dense-attention BI-DiT for random-access quality decoding, and UniGVC-AR, a windowed AR-DiT for streaming. UniGVC-BI serves as a conditional teacher for single-step distillation of UniGVC-AR, and a tiny conditional video decoder further cuts streaming latency.
0tRbH9VK6A.key_idea: Decode one codec bitstream with either a bidirectional teacher or an autoregressive student distilled from that teacher in a single step.
0tRbH9VK6A.evidence: Standard 1080p benchmarks with rate-quality curves, temporal measures, qualitative examples and human preference; AR evaluation uses captions generated from complete 96-frame videos.
0tRbH9VK6A.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract only says UniGVC-BI achieves the best overall result on standard 1080p benchmarks before it is cut off.
0tRbH9VK6A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/3/3) agree that supporting both quality-oriented and low-latency decoding from a single bitstream is practically useful and the codec design and generative decoding are coherently integrated.
0tRbH9VK6A.main_concern: The live-streaming claim is not validated: AR results use captions generated from the complete 96-frame video and the 1080p encoder runs at about 11.6 FPS, so decoder throughput does not establish end-to-end real-time operation.

BkRX0uRivL.one_liner: Flow-matching DiT on a high-dimensional semantic-acoustic latent, conditioned on structured multi-view captions, generates mixed audio scenes.
BkRX0uRivL.problem: Speech, music and sound effects come from separate models that cannot jointly generate coherent audio scenes, because of weak fine-grained supervision for real mixed audio and limited acoustic representations for concurrent components.
BkRX0uRivL.method: Structured multi-view captions split a complex scene into complementary description views for fine-grained control over audio layers, and a high-dimensional unified semantic-acoustic representation serves as the shared latent space. A simple flow-matching DiT then generates audio scenes end to end.
BkRX0uRivL.key_idea: Decouple scene descriptions into multi-view captions and model mixed audio in a high-dimensional semantic-acoustic latent (DashengTokenizer) with a plain flow-matching DiT.
BkRX0uRivL.evidence: A new evaluation pipeline for audio scene generation; per the reviews, comparisons with WavJourney and an expert pipeline, human evaluation by 20 audio professionals, and ablations of caption structure and latent representation.
BkRX0uRivL.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims performance approaching real-world recordings on mixed-audio categories and competitiveness with specialized models on single-type generation.
BkRX0uRivL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers (3/4/2) agree the unified mixed-audio framework is simple and effective, supported by extensive evaluations, ablations and human evaluation.
BkRX0uRivL.main_concern: Positioning against prior unified and joint speech-music-sound systems (UALM, Audio-Omni, Fugatto, VoiceLDM, Audiobox) is unclear, and the 128D VAE versus 1280D tokenizer ablation does not separate semantic content from latent capacity.

OihfOj2bYc.one_liner: Hybrid CNN/GNN backbone trained with a CRPS objective gives single-pass ensemble regional weather forecasts.
OihfOj2bYc.problem: Existing machine-learning limited-area weather models are not scalable because they rely on costly diffusion models or inefficient graph neural networks.
OihfOj2bYc.method: A hybrid CNN/GNN architecture forms the deterministic DET-LAM model and serves as the backbone of the generative CRPS-LAM, which is trained with a Continuous Ranked Probability Score objective so training and sampling need a single forward pass.
OihfOj2bYc.key_idea: Train an ensemble generator directly with a CRPS objective on a hybrid CNN/GNN backbone, so each ensemble member needs one forward pass instead of iterative diffusion sampling.
OihfOj2bYc.evidence: Regional domains in northern Europe (MEPS and DANRA per reviews), with ERA5 and IFS boundary inputs, comparisons to graph-based and diffusion-based baselines, and checks against station observations.
OihfOj2bYc.claimed_gains: About 39x speedup over diffusion-based baselines, with skillful and well-calibrated forecasts across atmospheric variables, and DET-LAM is both more efficient and more accurate than its graph-based competitor.
OihfOj2bYc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad and realistic, with a clear efficiency gain over Diffusion-LAM and consistent gains over graph-based baselines such as Graph-FM and Graph-EFM.
OihfOj2bYc.main_concern: The proposed models have far more parameters (233-251M) than the baselines (14.5-23.4M), so the accuracy gain cannot be attributed to the architecture without equal-capacity comparisons.

8JcBfsTfUc.one_liner: Self-distills a privileged object-cue teacher only at tokens whose distributions change most between real and weak images, reducing VLM hallucination.
8JcBfsTfUc.problem: VLMs hallucinate objects, attributes and relations in open-ended generation, while preference methods such as DPO are costly and entangle faithfulness with style and length, and hard pseudo captions from object cues can amplify teacher bias.
8JcBfsTfUc.method: Builds a non-verifying privileged visual teacher from training-time object cues and distills its soft token distributions on responses sampled by the student itself. Contrasting the teacher under the real image and a weak-image condition (Visual-KL) identifies visually sensitive tokens, and distillation is applied only at those positions.
8JcBfsTfUc.key_idea: Select tokens for on-policy self-distillation by the divergence between the privileged teacher's predictions under the real image and a degraded weak image.
