8JcBfsTfUc.evidence: Experiments on two model families and two LLaVA scales with ablations on token selection and weighting; reviewers cite AMBER hallucination rates over three backbones and three seeds on LLaVA-7B.
8JcBfsTfUc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find concentrating distillation on visually sensitive tokens well motivated, with consistent hallucination-metric gains, preserved general multimodal performance and comprehensive ablations.
8JcBfsTfUc.main_concern: Novelty and scope are limited: the token selection overlaps with VA-OPD's use of original versus degraded image predictions, and training and evaluation cover only COCO object-level hallucination.

rgimPbYcW6.one_liner: Proves W[1]-hardness of maximizing Lp norm over zonotopes by parameterized reduction, implying hard exact Lp-Lipschitz constants for two-layer ICNNs.
rgimPbYcW6.problem: The parameterized complexity of Lp-norm maximization over zonotopes, equivalent to the Lp-Lipschitz constant of two-layer ICNNs, was open for p in (1, infinity), unlike the tractable L1 and L-infinity cases.
rgimPbYcW6.method: Proves that for every fixed rational p in (1, infinity), maximizing the Lp norm over a zonotope in R^d is W[1]-hard in the dimension d, via a reduction from Multicolored Clique. By duality the same hardness holds for the Lp-Lipschitz constant of a two-layer ReLU ICNN.
rgimPbYcW6.key_idea: Geometric parameterized reduction from Multicolored Clique to Lp-norm maximization over zonotopes, so brute-force vertex enumeration is essentially optimal under ETH.
rgimPbYcW6.evidence: Theoretical proofs only: W[1]-hardness for every fixed rational p in (1, infinity) and, per reviewers, an ETH-based lower bound ruling out rho(d) N^{o(d)} algorithms; no experiments.
rgimPbYcW6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper settles a clearly posed open problem from COLT 2025 with a tight hardness result and presents the geometric intuition clearly.
rgimPbYcW6.main_concern: Overlap with concurrent work: Cao et al. (2026) and others prove the same W[1]-hardness result, so the contribution beyond them is narrow, and one reviewer also cites limited significance and no experiments.

cEXl4ymR0T.one_liner: LLM coarse variable-importance judgments initialize a competitive relevance prior in high-dimensional BO, adapted by reflection and posterior inference.
cEXl4ymR0T.problem: High-dimensional Bayesian optimization methods struggle to uncover useful structural biases from sparse observations under tight experimental budgets.
cEXl4ymR0T.method: CoRe-BO uses coarse LLM judgments of variable importance to set a relevance prior in which variables compete for a shared sensitivity budget, then adapts the structure through bounded LLM reflection and posterior inference as experiments accumulate. A regret analysis relates LLM guidance quality to search complexity.
cEXl4ymR0T.key_idea: Coarse LLM importance judgments become a Dirichlet-style prior over GP sensitivities with a shared budget so variables compete, then are revised from observations.
cEXl4ymR0T.evidence: Experiments on six scientific optimization tasks with 29-150 variables against high-dimensional and LLM-assisted BO baselines, plus a regret analysis.
cEXl4ymR0T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method principled and well written, with the competitive budget and LLM-derived semantic prior well motivated for scientific variables that have physical or chemical meaning.
cEXl4ymR0T.main_concern: Novelty and validation gaps: similar LLM-prior approaches exist (BORA and a high-entropy-alloy nanozyme study) and BORA is not a baseline, LLM-choice ablations do not cover all tasks, and Theorem 1 is not linked to the experiments.

9nHGUUfMQ7.one_liner: MLLM agent makes multi-turn tool calls for narrative video, trained on reflection-augmented trajectories and RL with a reflection-anchored process reward.
9nHGUUfMQ7.problem: Narrative video generation pipelines are fixed or one-shot plans that fail when intermediate outputs deviate from expectations and lack autonomous recovery.
9nHGUUfMQ7.method: ReFactor formulates generation as a Markov decision process where the agent picks a tool call from the narrative prompt, execution history, and generated artifacts. It is trained with SFT on 21K reflection-augmented trajectories with evaluator-accepted repair demonstrations, then agentic RL with a reflection-anchored process reward measuring improvement from intermediate repairs.
9nHGUUfMQ7.key_idea: A process reward measures the relative quality gain from intermediate repairs, giving denser signal for learning when and how to reflect on generated artifacts.
9nHGUUfMQ7.evidence: Evaluated on StoryEval with a human preference study, prompt-level paired bootstrap intervals, a separate test-time narrative judge, and architecture ablations.
9nHGUUfMQ7.claimed_gains: 18.9% relative improvement in narrative completion on StoryEval over the strongest (truncated in the abstract) baseline.
9nHGUUfMQ7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical, conditioning tool decisions on actual generated outputs is sensible, and the experiments, human study, and ablations are solid and clearly presented.
9nHGUUfMQ7.main_concern: Novelty is moderate (known components: multimodal tool use, trajectory collection, GRPO) and the ablations do not separate learned reflection from other changes, with weak process-level credit assignment.

yPkWPf4xRz.one_liner: Feature prediction on frozen ViT features separates dominant temporal change from residual motion, trained on real video plus Kubric.
yPkWPf4xRz.problem: Frame-to-frame change entangles camera and object motion, and this decomposition is underexplored in representation learning because the factors are tightly coupled and hard to supervise separately.
yPkWPf4xRz.method: The Structured Motion Model (SMM) separates the dominant source of temporal change from residual motion through feature prediction on frozen features of a pretrained image ViT, rather than a single entangled latent or dense transition tokens. Training combines self-supervision on real video with weak scene-motion supervision on synthetic Kubric data.
yPkWPf4xRz.key_idea: Feature prediction splits temporal change into a dominant component and a residual motion component, rather than one entangled latent or dense transition tokens.
yPkWPf4xRz.evidence: ProbeMotion, a new suite of synthetic and real video probes for camera, object, and combined motion, compared with CLS and average-pooled backbone features and VGGT, plus ablations on context and motion-token specialization.
yPkWPf4xRz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating camera from object motion is an important problem and that the ablations, probes, and qualitative analyses (including motion extrapolation and swapping) are informative.
yPkWPf4xRz.main_concern: Evidence for camera-object decomposition on real videos with both motions is missing, comparisons omit latent-action models (LAPA, Midway Network, Moto) and are unfair to single-image backbones, and gains may come from multi-layer features rather than the architecture.

Psl8GgO2we.one_liner: Decentralized LLM fine-tuning that floods seed-reconstructible zeroth-order updates to all clients, giving near-zero-size messages and global consensus.
Psl8GgO2we.problem: Decentralized fine-tuning has communication cost that grows with model size, and information decays over network hops, making global consensus inefficient.
Psl8GgO2we.method: SeedFlood exploits the seed-reconstructible structure of zeroth-order gradients so each message is near-zero in size and can be flooded to every client. A convergence analysis shows it avoids topology-dependent consensus terms.
Psl8GgO2we.key_idea: Transmit zeroth-order updates as seed-reconstructible near-zero-size messages and flood them to all clients, instead of gossip-averaging model weights.
Psl8GgO2we.evidence: Experiments with billion-parameter models and up to hundreds of clients against first-order gossip baselines, plus a convergence bound without topology-dependent consensus terms.
Psl8GgO2we.claimed_gains: Matches or surpasses first-order gossip baselines at larger collaboration scales with orders-of-magnitude less communication; no exact figures in the abstract.
Psl8GgO2we.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is well motivated and shows a communication advantage of several orders of magnitude while retaining competitive task performance, with clear presentation.
Psl8GgO2we.main_concern: Evidence of practical training speed and robustness is limited: scalability runs are small and simulated, and flooding assumes reliable delivery with little treatment of lost messages, stragglers, or latency.

tcrtrIVi2i.one_liner: Two-stage post-training that emphasizes early denoising states and learns recovery from self-generated rollouts for audio-editing source selection.
tcrtrIVi2i.problem: Unified audio editors often modify the wrong source or alter non-target content, and early denoising errors persist through later steps.
tcrtrIVi2i.method: STEER-Emphasis trains on task-relevant early-trajectory states and STEER-Recovery learns corrective denoising from self-generated rollout states; applied to build SteerSound for six editing tasks, with a new Selective Audio Editing Benchmark.
tcrtrIVi2i.key_idea: Prefix interventions show early denoising steps causally set the edited source, so training upweights early-trajectory states and learns to correct deviations from self-generated rollouts.
tcrtrIVi2i.evidence: Intermediate-state observation and bidirectional prefix interventions, experiments on the Selective Audio Editing Benchmark and realistic multi-source scenes, and tests across other models and selective-control tasks.
tcrtrIVi2i.claimed_gains: Consistently reduces source-selection errors and improves overall editing performance; no numbers stated.
tcrtrIVi2i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnostic prefix-intervention analysis, showing that early denoising steps determine source selection, convincing and the method simple and cheap.
tcrtrIVi2i.main_concern: Novelty is limited because early-timestep reweighting and training on self-generated states resemble known image and video generation techniques, and evaluation thresholds such as CLAP > 0.08 are unvalidated.

6WATgwTWK8.one_liner: Rectifies quantized ViT outputs by fitting a componentwise affine map from full-precision to quantized logits and analytically inverting it.
6WATgwTWK8.problem: Low-bit post-training quantization leaves systematic output distortions in vision transformers, and direct regression from quantized to full-precision outputs suffers class-dependent slope attenuation that distorts cross-class rankings.
6WATgwTWK8.method: InvAR uses paired outputs (such as class logits) from the full-precision and quantized models on a small unlabeled calibration set, fits a componentwise affine FP-to-Q mapping, and analytically inverts it. It runs post hoc without rerunning quantization.
6WATgwTWK8.key_idea: Fit the affine map from full-precision to quantized outputs and invert it, avoiding the slope attenuation of regressing quantized outputs onto full-precision ones.
6WATgwTWK8.evidence: ImageNet-1K Top-1 across PTQ methods, ViT architectures, and low-bit settings, with a controlled comparison against direct regression using identical models, calibration images, and affine forms.
6WATgwTWK8.claimed_gains: Vanilla InvAR and direct regression give mean ImageNet-1K Top-1 accuracy changes of +1.33 and -1.07 percentage points, respectively.
6WATgwTWK8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is lightweight, combines with existing PTQ methods, and that the controlled comparison of fitting directions is insightful.
6WATgwTWK8.main_concern: It lacks comparisons with simple per-class corrections and existing rectification or calibration methods, its theory does not justify the FP-to-Q advantage, and gains shrink at higher bit widths.

wgH9JT2xI7.one_liner: Replaces self-attention in embodied policies with learned shared state centers that aggregate tokens into compact states before query retrieval.
wgH9JT2xI7.problem: Alternatives to self-attention in embodied policies mostly address quadratic cost and not how source information should be organized before retrieval.
wgH9JT2xI7.method: Structured State Representation (SSR) uses learned per-head state centers shared across samples; source tokens are competitively assigned and aggregated into input-dependent states, and queries then retrieve from this compact state bank. It is swapped in for attention inside ACT and Diffusion Policy.
wgH9JT2xI7.key_idea: Organize first, then read: competitively assign source tokens to learned shared centers to form a compact state bank, then let queries retrieve from it.
wgH9JT2xI7.evidence: Controlled operator-replacement experiments in ACT and Diffusion Policy, plus linear probes of episode progress and linear CKA comparing Transformer and SSR denoisers.
wgH9JT2xI7.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract gives no figures: SSR stays competitive with standard attention, improves in selected settings, and has linear token-mixing cost for a fixed number of states).
wgH9JT2xI7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the organize-then-read formulation clear and compatible with the standard attention interface, with ablations and efficiency measurements supporting it.
wgH9JT2xI7.main_concern: SSR resembles Perceiver, Slot Attention, Set Transformer, and Agent Attention without matched comparisons, and its gains are task-dependent (for example worse on Bimanual Insertion and Robomimic Square).

4fo2kFaDQT.one_liner: Unlearns targeted content in multimodal LLMs by weighting tokens via counterfactual inputs and distilling on-policy self-generated responses.
4fo2kFaDQT.problem: Existing MLLM unlearning applies uniform forgetting objectives to whole responses with fixed off-policy supervision, giving coarse token control and misalignment with the model's current behavior.
4fo2kFaDQT.method: CUSE builds counterfactual inputs by removing target-related evidence and uses the resulting token-probability changes to find tokens needing stronger forgetting. It then distills token-level forgetting and retention targets on responses sampled from the current policy, with a frozen copy of the original model as teacher given forgetting- and retention-oriented privileged contexts.
4fo2kFaDQT.key_idea: Token-level forgetting strength comes from probability shifts under counterfactual evidence removal, and on-policy self-distillation from a frozen privileged-context teacher supplies forget and retain targets.
4fo2kFaDQT.evidence: Evaluated on MLLMU-Bench with several MLLM backbones, ablations, and robustness tests against random prefixes, paraphrasing, and jailbreak prompts.
4fo2kFaDQT.claimed_gains: On MLLMU-Bench, CUSE reduces forget-set ROUGE-L by 58.7% while achieving 4.6% higher retain-set ROUGE-L than the strongest baseline.
4fo2kFaDQT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree CUSE gives large forgetting gains while largely keeping retained utility, backed by extensive experiments, ablations, and multiple backbones.
4fo2kFaDQT.main_concern: The quality of the counterfactual data and sensitivity score is not systematically evaluated, the forgetting branch may amount to distilling a refusal template, and the remaining components build on existing techniques.

vvGUuiLUtF.one_liner: ProtGround grounds functional phrases in local protein 3D regions via a new region-function dataset and hierarchical multimodal pretraining.
vvGUuiLUtF.problem: Existing protein-text pretraining works at the whole-protein level and leaves the correspondence between functional descriptions and supporting local 3D structural regions unresolved.
vvGUuiLUtF.method: They build ProtGround-Align, a large-scale dataset of local region-function pairs, and train ProtGround-Hier, which models protein-region-phrase relationships with multi-positive region-phrase alignment, residue-token optimal transport, and multi-level masked modeling.
vvGUuiLUtF.key_idea: Jointly model protein, local region, and phrase relationships with multi-positive region-phrase alignment, residue-token optimal transport, and multi-level masked modeling.
vvGUuiLUtF.evidence: Experiments on fine-grained grounding (retrieval, candidate grounding, blind grounding) and downstream protein understanding tasks, with ablations of the optimal-transport and grounding losses.
vvGUuiLUtF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is meaningful and the large local region-function dataset (about 3M pairs over 376,866 proteins per one review) is the strongest contribution, with substantial grounding gains.
vvGUuiLUtF.main_concern: The comparison may be unfair because the new model trains on fine-grained region annotations while baselines use global ones, so gains may come from data rather than method, and the blind-grounding procedure and related work are thinly described.

KjHrTL5pzx.one_liner: GRACE-Bench scores coding agents on Godot game tasks with gate, behavior, and integration checks, exposing cross-system failures.
KjHrTL5pzx.problem: Game requirements span input, physics, rules, object lifecycles, and visuals through shared runtime state, and local functionality checks miss cross-system behavior failures in coding-agent outputs.
KjHrTL5pzx.method: A benchmark of 60 extension and repair tasks in existing Godot 2D projects with 1,270 executable checks in three layers (gate, behavior, integration), so each answer is judged against its complete requirement and each failure is located in a layer.
KjHrTL5pzx.key_idea: Layer executable checks into gate, designated-mechanism behavior, and cross-system integration for the same task, so failures that pass local checks are located.
KjHrTL5pzx.evidence: Twelve models evaluated on the 60 tasks, with task-resampling confidence intervals and leave-one-model-out, leave-one-task-out, and top-failed-check-removal robustness checks.
KjHrTL5pzx.claimed_gains: Benchmark finding: of 180 answers passing every gate and behavior check across 12 models, only 68 pass all integration checks, and the other 112 (62.2%; 95% interval 50.8-72.6%) fail.
KjHrTL5pzx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is carefully validated with reference and deliberately faulty implementations and that the integration failures it reveals across all 12 models are real and useful.
KjHrTL5pzx.main_concern: The added value of the behavior/integration split over existing runtime and integration testing is unclear, and reproducibility details (an inaccessible link, screening parameters) are missing.

nrqsrq8Oux.one_liner: Contextual Shift Attribution traces which attention heads and FFN neurons resist evidence-driven answer revision, then patches them.
nrqsrq8Oux.problem: Language models resist external correction despite explicit supporting evidence, and the internal mechanisms are poorly understood, with unclear separation between resistant behavior and the underlying contextual-parametric conflict.
nrqsrq8Oux.method: CSA decomposes evidence-induced answer shifts into signed component contributions along a controlled evidence-strength trajectory, separating components that resist revision from those that support it. Targeted intervention on the identified components is then tested.
nrqsrq8Oux.key_idea: Score each component by the direction of its contextual displacement times the downstream sensitivity of the answer-preference margin, tracked along increasing evidence strength.
nrqsrq8Oux.evidence: Six language models and three knowledge-conflict benchmarks, comparing targeted patching with random patching and PASTA, plus overlap and cross-benchmark transfer experiments.
nrqsrq8Oux.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (cut off at 'improves the average'); one review reports about 87.4% versus 77.9% for PASTA, leading in 16 of 18 model-dataset settings.
nrqsrq8Oux.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the signed attribution separates components that resist revision from those that support it, and that targeted patching clearly beats random patching with the same budget across six models and three benchmarks.
nrqsrq8Oux.main_concern: Component scoring, budget selection, and testing use the same three benchmarks, so calibration and evaluation are not separated and cross-benchmark transfer is not a clean test.

BN718ryQB8.one_liner: Trains VLAs progressively, first predicting future video then future depth through world embeddings, shaping representations with zero inference overhead.
BN718ryQB8.problem: Parallel joint training of future 2D video and 3D geometry prediction ignores their order, imposing 3D grounding before 2D scene evolution has been sufficiently learned.
BN718ryQB8.method: The Dream phase uses world embeddings to condition a pretrained video diffusion model for future-video generation; the Lift phase then conditions a pretrained depth diffusion model on the world embeddings for future-depth generation to add 3D spatial awareness.
BN718ryQB8.key_idea: Use a 2D-then-3D curriculum of auxiliary generative supervision, with world embeddings conditioning pretrained video then depth diffusion models to shape VLA representations.
BN718ryQB8.evidence: Multiple simulation benchmarks (MetaWorld and LIBERO-Plus per reviews) and real-world in- and out-of-distribution tasks, with ablations on training order, duration, and generative backbones.
BN718ryQB8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the curriculum ablations directly support the 2D-to-3D ordering and that evaluation across simulation and real-robot settings shows consistent gains with no inference-time overhead.
BN718ryQB8.main_concern: Alternative explanations for the ordering effect are not ruled out (no action-only to depth control, loss weighting, teacher-generated pseudo-depth), and the gain over DreamVLA is not controlled for backbone differences.

KiOVWFjQOA.one_liner: Dynamic knowledge tracing with frequency-aware recurrent aggregators and a context modulator using structural priors for cold start.
KiOVWFjQOA.problem: Dynamic KT methods struggle to separate transient cognitive fluctuations from stable knowledge acquisition and give unreliable predictions in cold-start cases with limited interaction history.
KiOVWFjQOA.method: Context-aware recurrent aggregators capture high-frequency cognitive variations while preserving long-term trends, and a context modulator generates student- and question-specific contextual representations that incorporate prior structural knowledge to alleviate cold start.
KiOVWFjQOA.key_idea: Counteract RNN low-pass oversmoothing with a frequency-domain enhancer on recurrent aggregation, and inject prerequisite-graph priors through a context modulator.
KiOVWFjQOA.evidence: Five public datasets and 12 baselines under transductive and inductive settings, with ablations, per reviews.
KiOVWFjQOA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of modeling transient fluctuations and cold-start prediction is worthwhile and that the evaluation is comprehensive across datasets, baselines, and settings.
KiOVWFjQOA.main_concern: Novelty is limited because components are largely existing techniques and prior fluctuation-aware KT such as FlucKT is not engaged, and the frequency-gate mechanism is unclear.

8lsLkIm1Kt.one_liner: Unifies teacher-guided diffusion distillation and reward RL with a sample-wise reward weight that interpolates DiffusionOPD and DiffusionNFT targets.
8lsLkIm1Kt.problem: Sequential distill-then-RL post-training of diffusion models suffers post-switch degradation, late-stage collapse, and sensitivity to the handoff schedule, especially under limited prompt diversity.
8lsLkIm1Kt.method: URF decides where to optimize and which velocity target to follow for each generated sample from one reward-adaptive objective controlled by a sample-wise weight p in [0, 1]. Negative reward feedback constrains the teacher-guided correction, and as reward rises p moves the update from DiffusionOPD to DiffusionNFT without an explicit stage switch.
8lsLkIm1Kt.key_idea: A per-sample reward-preference weight smoothly blends the distillation velocity target and the RL (NFT) update, replacing the explicit stage-wise switch.
8lsLkIm1Kt.evidence: Multi-reward training, single-reward optimization, four-step distillation, and component ablations in the DiffusionOPD/DiffusionNFT setting, with reviews citing GenEval and OCR scores and training speedups.
8lsLkIm1Kt.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract is cut off and gives no numbers)
8lsLkIm1Kt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear (switching times cause score drops or collapse) and that combining dense teacher supervision with reward optimization addresses a practical bottleneck, with faster training reported.
8lsLkIm1Kt.main_concern: Gains are slim and not averaged over seeds, the objective is a simple linear blend with ad hoc weighting, and claims go beyond the DiffusionOPD/DiffusionNFT pair tested.

Z8cMQAxLJN.one_liner: Speculative decoding with on-policy reverse-KL distilled diffusion drafters and an adaptive length head that sets candidate length on the fly.
Z8cMQAxLJN.problem: Diffusion drafters' global dependency (bidirectional attention and KV injection) causes high variance in acceptance rates across domains and across draft positions.
Z8cMQAxLJN.method: AdaFlash combines an on-policy distillation algorithm with reverse-KL divergence tailored to diffusion drafters, which adapts the drafter to the deployment distribution, with an adaptive length head that adjusts the candidate length dynamically to lower verification cost.
Z8cMQAxLJN.key_idea: Distill the diffusion drafter on-policy with reverse KL on the deployment distribution, and predict the draft length per step with a learned head.
Z8cMQAxLJN.evidence: Multiple target models, eight benchmarks spanning math, code, dialogue, and mixed domains, and high-concurrency serving settings against DFlash and OSD per reviews.
Z8cMQAxLJN.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract is cut off before the results)
Z8cMQAxLJN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diffusion-drafter variance problem is meaningful, the high-concurrency serving setting is practical, and the evaluation spans several targets and benchmarks.
Z8cMQAxLJN.main_concern: Gains are limited (small ablation improvements, sometimes slower than autoregressive decoding), and deployment complexity and online-training cost are not reported.

3qdu7phmri.one_liner: Policy-optimization algorithm achieving best-of-both-worlds regret in tabular MDPs with heavy-tailed losses, avoiding global occupancy-measure optimization.
3qdu7phmri.problem: Best-of-both-worlds guarantees for finite-horizon MDPs with heavy-tailed losses (bounded epsilon-th raw moment, epsilon in (1,2]) were only achieved by an occupancy-measure-based algorithm that requires solving a global optimization problem.
3qdu7phmri.method: They develop a policy optimization approach that updates the policy locally at each state, covering known and unknown transitions and adversarial and stochastic regimes. For unknown transitions it drops the truncated non-negativity assumption imposed by Chen et al. (2026).
3qdu7phmri.key_idea: Update the policy locally at each state with heavy-tail-robust policy optimization instead of solving a global occupancy-measure problem.
3qdu7phmri.evidence: Regret-bound analysis against Chen et al. (2026) for known and unknown transitions in adversarial and stochastic regimes; a reviewer notes there are no numerical experiments.
3qdu7phmri.claimed_gains: For known transitions, heavy-tail terms improve on Chen et al. (2026) by factors O(S^{2-2/eps}A^{2-3/eps+1/eps^2}) (adversarial) and O(S^2 A^{2-1/eps}) (stochastic); for unknown transitions, by O(S^{3-2/eps}A^{3-3/eps+1/eps^2}) (adversarial) and O(H S^3 A^{3-1/eps} log T) (stochastic).
3qdu7phmri.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit improved regret bounds across known and unknown transitions and stochastic and adversarial losses, and the removal of the truncated non-negativity assumption.
3qdu7phmri.main_concern: Presentation of the analysis: key insights are not distilled and informative details are deferred to the appendix; another reviewer also notes the lack of numerical evidence and of full minimax optimality.

wyiGeEcJW3.one_liner: Organizes LLM-mined alpha factors in a multi-relational graph, propagates search utilities over it, and selects parents by Pareto trade-offs.
wyiGeEcJW3.problem: Generation-centric and tree-based LLM alpha mining organizes factors only by lineage, so information stays local to parent-child trajectories, exploration can stay in redundant regions, and multiple objectives are not captured by one criterion.
wyiGeEcJW3.method: Discovered factors form a graph with edges for generation lineage, expression-structure similarity, and cross-sectional exposure correlation. A Graph Flow mechanism propagates search utilities across the graph, and Pareto-guided selection balances quality, fertility, and diversity.
wyiGeEcJW3.key_idea: Score each candidate factor with utilities propagated across lineage, structure, and exposure-correlation edges, then pick parents by Pareto trade-off among quality, fertility, and diversity.
wyiGeEcJW3.evidence: Experiments on CSI 300 (text cut off) and a second A-share universe with a chronological train/validation/test split and ablations of propagation and selection, per reviews.
wyiGeEcJW3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-relational graph, especially exposure correlation alongside structure and lineage, is a well-motivated search representation, with ablations probing what drives the gains.
wyiGeEcJW3.main_concern: The search comparison is not shown to be fair or isolating: methods are matched by output factor count rather than LLM or evaluation budget, and the Graph and MCTS variants differ in prompts and feedback.

fOYZ2tLlhe.one_liner: Drag editing resolved in FLAME geometry-condition space: Jacobian-weighted expression and jaw optimization for deformation, camera optimization for rotation.
fOYZ2tLlhe.problem: Diffusion-based drag methods track learned intermediate features where geometry is only implicit, so feature correspondence becomes unreliable under large facial deformation or rotation.
fOYZ2tLlhe.method: On a geometry-conditioned diffusion model (MMDM with FLAME), user 2D handles are tied to persistent 3D surface points. Deformation edits optimize FLAME expression and jaw parameters with Jacobian-based weighting, and viewpoint edits optimize camera parameters while preserving geometry.
fOYZ2tLlhe.key_idea: Perform dragging by optimizing explicit 3D geometry conditions (FLAME parameters or camera) so 2D handles map to persistent 3D surface points, instead of matching diffusion features.
fOYZ2tLlhe.evidence: Comparison against DragDiffusion, DragNoise, GoodDrag, and DragLoRA on the new DragFace benchmark using the proposed Geometry Mean Distance.
fOYZ2tLlhe.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text is cut off after 'more accurate geometric point').
fOYZ2tLlhe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving dragging from implicit diffusion features to an explicit 3D template space is intuitive and geometrically sound, with Jacobian weighting helping disentangle deformation.
fOYZ2tLlhe.main_concern: Limited algorithmic novelty and weak comparisons: the method reduces to classic screen-space inverse kinematics over a low-dimensional 3DMM, is compared against general non-face-specific drag methods, and omits closely related 3D-aware face editing baselines.

2LFnFGV58m.one_liner: ReHarness revises retrieved reflections using each instance's trajectory as feedback, adding backward revision to an agent memory harness.
2LFnFGV58m.problem: Agent harnesses either evolve state only through forward information flow or need extra replay or validation data, so overgeneralized or outdated reflections keep misguiding agents in streaming continual learning.
2LFnFGV58m.method: Under a strictly online streaming protocol, after each instance ReHarness uses the resulting trajectory as feedback to revise the reflections retrieved for that instance, propagating feedback backward through the textual harness state.
2LFnFGV58m.key_idea: After each instance, rewrite the reflections that were retrieved for it using the outcome trajectory, so memory is not write-once.
2LFnFGV58m.evidence: Three continual learning benchmarks (16 tasks per reviews), three language model backbones, and seven baselines including raw-context, memory, reflection-based, and prompt-optimization methods.
2LFnFGV58m.claimed_gains: The abstract says it consistently outperforms raw-context, memory-based, reflection-based, and prompt-optimization baselines on three benchmarks and three backbones, with no numbers stated.
2LFnFGV58m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is natural and clearly motivated, and the evaluation is broad with diverse baselines, notably strong raw-context ones, and useful ablations.
2LFnFGV58m.main_concern: Novelty and attribution are unclear: memory editing already exists in Mem0 and ACE, no control isolates downstream feedback from simply reconsidering the evidence, and per-instance revision cost and reflection growth are unreported.

gAMbOkVeDd.one_liner: LeanPRM uses Lean verification of paired formal proofs to label steps of natural-language proofs without human annotation.
gAMbOkVeDd.problem: Training step-level proof verifiers needs step correctness labels that are costly from humans, unavailable from final answers for proofs, and expensive to obtain by formalizing each proof in Lean.
gAMbOkVeDd.method: A model writes a natural-language proof with a paired formal proof without Lean feedback, Lean labels every step, and a second model discards failures caused only by formal syntax so negative labels mark mathematical errors. This yields LeanPRM with 10,634 proofs and 152K labeled steps.
gAMbOkVeDd.key_idea: Pair each natural-language proof with a formal proof and use Lean checking, filtered for syntax-only failures, as the step-level label source.
gAMbOkVeDd.evidence: A Qwen3-4B verifier evaluated on LeanPRM-Bench (200 held-out proofs), best-of-N selection on IMO-level problems, four external verification benchmarks, and verifiers from 0.6B up, against a PRM800K-trained verifier.
gAMbOkVeDd.claimed_gains: A Qwen3-4B verifier trained on LeanPRM raises exact step-label accuracy on LeanPRM-Bench from 48.2 to 74.7 versus 60.3 when trained on PRM800K, and beats the PRM800K verifier on three of four external benchmarks.
gAMbOkVeDd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Lean-grounded step labels without human annotation are a practical, scalable route to process supervision and that the aligned NL-Lean corpus is useful.
gAMbOkVeDd.main_concern: The reliability of the step labels is not established: they depend on LLM judgments for NL-formal alignment and for separating mathematical from formalization errors, and a frontier-model audit disagrees with some labels.

Vr4ZLl3afm.one_liner: Budgeted researcher agents build executable evaluation suites, then frozen evaluators are compared with held-out benchmark judgments.
Vr4ZLl3afm.problem: Repeatedly running complex benchmarks slows autonomous research, but agents' ability to design compact, reliable evaluators is unclear.
Vr4ZLl3afm.method: EvalResearchBench gives researcher agents target materials, references, candidate APIs, and fixed budgets to select or synthesize tasks, implement graders, and run pilot revisions. Frozen evaluators are independently assessed for score concordance and pairwise agreement.
Vr4ZLl3afm.key_idea: Require agents to submit frozen executable evaluators and test their model rankings against development and sealed target benchmarks.
Vr4ZLl3afm.evidence: The study evaluates 9 researchers and 13 candidate models against 14 target benchmarks spanning coding, co-work, and reasoning, with a human-designed public-task baseline.
Vr4ZLl3afm.claimed_gains: The best evaluators order about 75% of candidate pairs as the targets do, below the 91% ceiling set by disagreements among targets.
Vr4ZLl3afm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value autonomous evaluator construction as a meaningful research task and the held-out, executable-artifact evaluation protocol.
Vr4ZLl3afm.main_concern: Reviewers find one research episode per configuration insufficient to measure stable differences in evaluator-design capability.

QT0v53O4Kz.one_liner: A report-utility rubric gates inherited team advantages during joint training of main agents and research subagents.
QT0v53O4Kz.problem: Shared team credit can reward misleading subagent reports and penalize useful reports when the final answer has the opposite outcome.
QT0v53O4Kz.method: LEAD-RL jointly trains main agents and subagents while a training-time rubric rates each report's research utility. These ratings gate inherited team advantages, with final-answer correctness remaining the only team reward.
QT0v53O4Kz.key_idea: Gate each subagent's inherited team advantage using a training-time judgment of the research utility of its report.
QT0v53O4Kz.evidence: Experiments span five benchmarks and two model families, with main-agent-only and shared-credit joint-training comparisons from the same SFT checkpoint.
QT0v53O4Kz.claimed_gains: On BrowseComp, LEAD-RL improves accuracy by 2.49 percentage points and reduces critical-path cost by 24.5%, while validation accuracy increases by 6.78 points at approximately constant critical-path cost.
QT0v53O4Kz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a plausible shared-credit failure and a simple report-level gate supported by useful controlled training comparisons.
QT0v53O4Kz.main_concern: Reviewers question the reliability of unaudited LLM contribution judgments and whether their correctness explains the gains.

2uAueAfyFR.one_liner: Cumulative conversation clips and human gaze-guided corruption measure when and where multimodal models infer social meaning.
2uAueAfyFR.problem: Complete-episode benchmarks emphasize retrospective social recognition rather than incremental perception needed for real-time interaction.
2uAueAfyFR.method: GesBench presents cumulative sub-utterance clips to track interpretation formation and revision. Human eye-tracking guides visual corruption to test the importance of attended regions for model judgments.
2uAueAfyFR.key_idea: Track interpretation changes over cumulative clips and perturb human-attended regions to probe temporal and spatial social perception.
2uAueAfyFR.evidence: The benchmark contains 6,208 utterances, with eye-tracking annotations on 600 and spoken cumulative-clip interpretations on 590, evaluated across open and closed multimodal models.
2uAueAfyFR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value incremental social-perception evaluation and human response and gaze data beyond full-video final-answer assessment.
2uAueAfyFR.main_concern: Reviewers question whether temporal metrics and differing human-model response protocols measure perception rather than prompting and response-style effects.

mjR2Fi3wpL.one_liner: Lifting and compression operations within reverse diffusion learn low-dimensional structure for physical and image generation.
mjR2Fi3wpL.problem: Conventional denoising may fail to preserve low-dimensional structure and physical regularities in generated data.
mjR2Fi3wpL.method: Structure-aware Compression Diffusion Models insert lifting and compression operations into reverse diffusion to learn low-dimensional representations. The learned structures are examined against physical quantities and used for generation.
mjR2Fi3wpL.key_idea: Apply lifting and compression during reverse diffusion to learn and use low-dimensional data structure.
mjR2Fi3wpL.evidence: Experiments cover physical systems and CIFAR-10, including corrupted training data, subspace-size and lifting ablations, correlation analyses, runtime measurements, and failure cases.
mjR2Fi3wpL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the structural-prior motivation intuitive and recognize promising physical-data results with useful ablations.
mjR2Fi3wpL.main_concern: Reviewers find the theoretical justification for the compression update and its relationship to diffusion objectives insufficient.

YrSfjNWLbf.one_liner: Planning, data, and advisor agents iteratively connect research requirements, evidence construction, analysis, and review in empirical social science.
YrSfjNWLbf.problem: Fragmented real-world evidence is difficult to convert into reliable variables and integrate with research design and empirical interpretation.
YrSfjNWLbf.method: SocialLab coordinates a Plan Agent, Data Agent, and independent Advisor Agent through a closed-loop Coordinator. CSD-Bench evaluates open-ended empirical research using heterogeneous multi-source data.
YrSfjNWLbf.key_idea: Coordinate research planning and data construction with independent review of plans, data decisions, and conclusions in an iterative workflow.
YrSfjNWLbf.evidence: ReplicatorBench and CSD-Bench experiments compare research workflows and include component ablations and coding-agent comparisons.
YrSfjNWLbf.claimed_gains: On ReplicatorBench, SocialLab reports average gains over Replicator of 18.21, 43.99, 11.14, and 33.14 points.
YrSfjNWLbf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the evidence-construction problem and a coherent multi-agent workflow connecting research requirements to data and review.
YrSfjNWLbf.main_concern: Reviewers find baseline coverage and compute controls insufficient to establish SocialLab's advantage over existing research and coding-agent workflows.

8lGMGXFM6R.one_liner: Consensus, complementary, and conflict features feed reliability-adaptive routing and gated residual fusion for multimodal sentiment prediction.
8lGMGXFM6R.problem: Forced alignment can suppress useful modality differences, while direct conflict fusion can introduce noise and negative transfer.
8lGMGXFM6R.method: CARE-KAN decomposes multimodal representations into shared consensus, modality-unique complements, and directional conflict vectors. Reliability-adaptive routing weights these streams, and zero-gated residual fusion selectively incorporates their evidence.
8lGMGXFM6R.key_idea: Decompose consensus, complementary, and conflicting evidence, then use sample-conditioned reliability to route it through gated residual fusion.
8lGMGXFM6R.evidence: Experiments report competitive sentiment prediction across four benchmarks, with corruption and reliability analyses and component ablations.
8lGMGXFM6R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find explicit conflict modeling, reliability routing, and gated fusion a coherent design for robust multimodal prediction.
8lGMGXFM6R.main_concern: Reviewers find the distinction between meaningful emotional disagreement and corruption-induced conflict insufficiently established.

Uz0eKGU86e.one_liner: Answer-guided attention proposals, crop verification, and compact evidence canvases refine high-resolution visual reasoning at test time.
Uz0eKGU86e.problem: High-resolution multimodal models can overlook small question-relevant details despite receiving more pixels.
Uz0eKGU86e.method: RECAP localizes entities from attention maps and uses tentative answers to direct refinement toward unresolved evidence. Comparative crop verification selects visible targets for order-aware canvases, while confidence controls further refinement or answer return.
Uz0eKGU86e.key_idea: Use tentative answers to select unresolved entities, verify attention-derived crops, and compose their evidence into compact ordered canvases.
Uz0eKGU86e.evidence: A controlled background-removal study and V*Bench, HRBench-4K, and HRBench-8K evaluations span several MLLMs, with improvements across four evaluated backbones.
Uz0eKGU86e.claimed_gains: RECAP reaches 95.8% with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 92.7% with InternVL3-8B on V*Bench.
Uz0eKGU86e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a practical high-resolution perception problem and promising training-free improvements across models and benchmarks.
Uz0eKGU86e.main_concern: Controlled experiments do not adequately isolate the contribution of answer-conditioned evidence diagnosis to the reported improvements.

L1g5BFmJzD.one_liner: Before-after music examples optimize reusable soft edit conditions, with transition-aware constraints separating transformations from reference content.
L1g5BFmJzD.problem: Text instructions can be inadequate for fine-grained music edits, while demonstrations entangle transferable transformations with source-specific content.
L1g5BFmJzD.method: Edit Condition Synthesis recovers a soft condition in a frozen flow-based editor's native conditioning space. A transition-aware semantic constraint captures source-to-target changes to encourage transfer to unseen inputs.
L1g5BFmJzD.key_idea: Optimize a reusable editor condition from a before-after pair while constraining its semantic transition rather than its reference-specific musical content.
L1g5BFmJzD.evidence: Instrument and style editing experiments use paired benchmarks, no-op controls, piece-level splits, same-editor demonstration baselines, component ablations, and a small subjective study.
L1g5BFmJzD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value demonstration-based music editing as a meaningful control setting and the potential reuse of learned edit conditions.
L1g5BFmJzD.main_concern: Reviewers find generalization beyond trained edit types and fine-grained transformations insufficiently demonstrated.

cGIuLtBNt3.one_liner: Hoeffding decomposition of gradient-boosted trees yields sparse nonlinear concept aggregation and compact prime-implicant explanations.
cGIuLtBNt3.problem: Linear concept aggregation can require many concepts, miss nonlinear relations, and encourage interconcept information leakage.
cGIuLtBNt3.method: HCBM uses the Hoeffding functional decomposition of gradient-boosted trees to aggregate concept scores nonlinearly and sparsely. It derives compact explanations through prime implicants and extends the approach to object detection.
cGIuLtBNt3.key_idea: Decompose a tree-based concept predictor into sparse nonlinear concept contributions and extract prime implicants for compact predictions.
cGIuLtBNt3.evidence: The paper provides interconcept-leakage theory and classification and overhead-image detection experiments, including low-concept-budget and concept-deletion tests.
cGIuLtBNt3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful nonlinear concept aggregation and strong empirical gains at small concept budgets.
cGIuLtBNt3.main_concern: Reviewers question whether guarantees for the full Hoeffding decomposition apply to the main-effect approximation used in experiments.

IPNsjThxoU.one_liner: Depth-guided feature propagation and reciprocal pose-pixel conditioning jointly generate future egocentric videos and 3D hand poses.
IPNsjThxoU.problem: Egocentric action prediction often treats structured hand motion and detailed visual futures separately or requires restrictive future-pose conditioning.
IPNsjThxoU.method: EgoP2FN jointly generates video and hand poses with flow matching from an initial image and instruction. A geometry module propagates first-frame depth cues, while pose features derived from observation-anchored intermediates condition video latents through adaptive layer normalization.
IPNsjThxoU.key_idea: Propagate first-frame geometry through video features and feed learned pose-flow features back into video latents through adaptive normalization.
IPNsjThxoU.evidence: Experiments use AssemblyHands, Ego-Exo4D, and EgoMe-pose sources, with 18,916 training clips, 400 test samples, and geometry and pose-guidance ablations.
IPNsjThxoU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find joint image-conditioned video and pose prediction meaningful and recognize complementary geometric and pose guidance.
IPNsjThxoU.main_concern: Reviewers find the small, in-source test set insufficient to establish broad generalization.

W8mQp16leK.one_liner: Recovery demonstrations and GRPO branches from self-generated failure states train terminal agents to complete tasks after errors.
W8mQp16leK.problem: Terminal agents struggle to recover from command errors and faulty implementations during long executions.
W8mQp16leK.method: ReTerm uses ReTerm-10K recovery demonstrations for supervised initialization. ReTerm-GRPO then forks multiple independent recovery attempts from the agent's own failure states and trains on final task completion.
W8mQp16leK.key_idea: Resume multiple rollouts from saved self-generated failure states and optimize recovery using task-completion rewards.
W8mQp16leK.evidence: Qwen3.5-9B experiments cover Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Verified, OpenThoughts-TBLite, recovery categories, and supervised and RL-stage ablations.
W8mQp16leK.claimed_gains: ReTerm-9B achieves 34.8% Pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2.0, improving over the base model by 14.6 points.
W8mQp16leK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value learning from the agent's own failures and substantial empirical improvements on terminal and software-engineering tasks.
W8mQp16leK.main_concern: Reviewers find the standard-GRPO comparison underspecified, especially initialization, rollout allocation, and matched training budgets.

Ftc7CgovZ2.one_liner: Return-tilted latent modes guide context-supported policy selection and weighted continuous-bid realization from offline trajectories.
Ftc7CgovZ2.problem: Offline continuous-bid optimization faces sparse action coverage and obscures distinct bidding tendencies needed under changing market and budget conditions.
Ftc7CgovZ2.method: PRISM learns outcome-relevant latent modes through return-tilted discovery. It selects the best-evaluated contextually supported mode and realizes it using a continuous-bid policy trained with mode-referenced weights.
Ftc7CgovZ2.key_idea: Partition offline behaviors into return-relevant modes, select among context-supported modes, and decode the selection into a continuous bid.
Ftc7CgovZ2.evidence: AuctionNet experiments cover budget levels, sparse settings, ten seeds, component ablations, and fixed-mode comparisons, with additional D4RL evaluations.
Ftc7CgovZ2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical bidding problem and consistent empirical gains supported by mode-selection and component analyses.
Ftc7CgovZ2.main_concern: Reviewers question mismatches between logged behavior used for mode evaluation and the model-selected modes and actions used at deployment.

v9REGSFVbf.one_liner: A financial-prior anchor and context-conditioned latent revision predictor learn equity representations for frozen downstream readouts.
v9REGSFVbf.problem: Flexible financial models can overfit noisy data, while interpretable linear models miss nonlinear predictive signals.
v9REGSFVbf.method: Stock-JEPA projects fixed point-in-time return and risk statistics into a target encoder's latent space. A separately trained context-conditioned branch predicts future displacement from this anchor, after which frozen representations support a downstream readout.
v9REGSFVbf.key_idea: Anchor future latent prediction to financial-prior statistics and separately learn the predictable residual displacement from historical context.
v9REGSFVbf.evidence: Two equity-market evaluations measure cross-sectional ranking and portfolio performance, with matched-readout and direct-context ablations and a fixed-encoder theoretical analysis.
v9REGSFVbf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear anchor-revision decomposition and evidence that revision features add predictive information across two equity markets.
v9REGSFVbf.main_concern: Reviewers agree that headline baselines differ in readout capacity, input information, and recency of supervised history, confounding the representation-learning contribution.

JLmc35Y7Ou.one_liner: Fisher-orthogonal residualization removes visually blind editing directions while updating video-conditioned responses.
JLmc35Y7Ou.problem: Video-language model edits can succeed through textual shortcuts without depending on video content.
JLmc35Y7Ou.method: VIGOR contrasts video-conditioned responses with a structure-preserving Visual-Null intervention. It computes a closed-form minimum-information update orthogonal to the blind response in Fisher geometry and uses video-grounded editability for layer selection.
JLmc35Y7Ou.key_idea: Project video-conditioned edit directions away from the Visual-Null response in Fisher geometry while preserving the null objective to first order.
JLmc35Y7Ou.evidence: Theory links editability to functional cost, while VMEB experiments cover four Video-LLMs, counterfactual-video generation, ablations, and sequential edits.
JLmc35Y7Ou.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing successful edits from video-dependent edits and find the geometric formulation coherent.
JLmc35Y7Ou.main_concern: Reviewers seek stronger evidence of semantic video dependence and transfer to distinct videos beyond the evaluated intervention settings.

QpsLBEPeRl.one_liner: Object-size intervals and reconstructed heights jointly determine a global metric scale through convex optimization.
QpsLBEPeRl.problem: Visual geometry foundation models recover scene structure and motion without reliable physical scale.
QpsLBEPeRl.method: UniMetric elicits object-height intervals from a vision-language model and measures reconstructed heights along support-surface normals. A convex objective reconciles the resulting scale intervals and applies one sequence-level scale to points and camera translations.
QpsLBEPeRl.key_idea: Convert uncertain semantic height priors and geometric height measurements into scale intervals, then reconcile them with a shared convex objective.
QpsLBEPeRl.evidence: MetricBench evaluates twelve embodied, driving, and roadside subsets against sensor ground truth, with reviewers reporting tests across nine geometry models.
QpsLBEPeRl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the model-agnostic scale correction and broad evaluation that preserves rather than removes scale errors.
QpsLBEPeRl.main_concern: Comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the benefit of uncertain intervals and aggregation over prior object-size methods or simpler fixed-height baselines.

gu08Twu8Sb.one_liner: CanICA-derived neuron-group activity trajectories fingerprint model lineage despite structural differences.
gu08Twu8Sb.problem: Weight repackaging changes model structure and obstructs provenance checks requiring direct parameter or representation correspondence.
gu08Twu8Sb.method: FNF applies canonical independent component analysis to Transformer-block activations to identify co-activating neuron groups. It compares their activity trajectories under identical stimuli using white-box access without fingerprint-specific training.
gu08Twu8Sb.key_idea: Compare functional activity trajectories of independently extracted neuron groups rather than requiring layerwise or neuronwise correspondence between models.
gu08Twu8Sb.evidence: Evaluation uses a labeled set of $40$ model pairs across three provenance categories and examines fine-tuning, pruning, merging, and depth-changing repackaging.
gu08Twu8Sb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the correspondence-free functional fingerprint simple and well motivated for structurally modified models.
gu08Twu8Sb.main_concern: The central repackaging claim rests on only three same-lineage depth modifications, without tests of width expansion or tokenizer replacement.

enKJTA51ca.one_liner: Paired alloy structures and charge-density fields support cross-modal representation learning and low-label magnetic transfer.
enKJTA51ca.problem: High-entropy alloy learning lacks paired atomic-electronic data and consistent evaluation across spatial scales.
enKJTA51ca.method: HEABench pairs relaxed atomic configurations with electron charge densities, property targets, and magnetic labels. Benchmarks assess global prediction, controlled local structure–charge matching, and site-resolved magnetic transfer using structural and electronic representations.
enKJTA51ca.key_idea: Pretrain representations on paired atomic structure and charge-density fields, then assess local correspondence and structure-only magnetic prediction under limited labels.
enKJTA51ca.evidence: The benchmark contains 3,109 quinary 100-atom configurations spanning 60 elements and evaluates global, local, and magnetic-transfer tasks.
enKJTA51ca.claimed_gains: With 50 magnetically labeled configurations, structure–charge pretraining reduces site-moment MAE by 10.9\% relative to random initialization.
enKJTA51ca.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the expensive paired structure–charge-density dataset as a resource for electronic representation learning.
enKJTA51ca.main_concern: Benchmark validity needs stronger support, including tighter elemental-identity controls for local retrieval and accessible data with clearly specified labels.

GgxtSHSope.one_liner: Graph-based cascade auditing locates injected skill content and selects graded edits to remove it.
GgxtSHSope.problem: Skill-file injections can propagate across files while runtime guardrails leave the risky source content intact.
GgxtSHSope.method: SkillGovernor organizes a skill package into a graph and uses cascaded reasoning to connect scattered risks. A dynamic governor selects the least intervention among graded operations to remove risk while retaining legitimate functionality.
GgxtSHSope.key_idea: Trace risk across a skill graph, then choose targeted edits, rewrites, or deletions according to the least required intervention.
GgxtSHSope.evidence: Evaluation spans 78 cases from two public skill-security benchmarks and five configurations on three agent systems, with audit and governance ablations.
GgxtSHSope.claimed_gains: SkillGovernor reduces ASR by 26 percentage points on average while maintaining task completion, and raises injection point detection from 0.26 to 0.76.
GgxtSHSope.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value integrating source-level risk localization with targeted remediation and report favorable attack-success and task-completion results.
GgxtSHSope.main_concern: Small benchmark samples make margins over competing defenses and some component ablations difficult to distinguish from variability.

MFZbESZmkR.one_liner: Synchronized workshop recordings and observer-specific intent annotations connect multimodal social behavior with participants' self-reported goals.
MFZbESZmkR.problem: Social-intention datasets inadequately capture subjective interpretations alongside clear speech, nonverbal behavior, and participants' goals.
MFZbESZmkR.method: COSI-Lab records 32 academics in two 30-minute mingling sessions using individual audio and environmental and wearable sensors. Its annotation process preserves perceivers' interpretative tendencies and links apparent intentions with self-reported goals.
MFZbESZmkR.key_idea: Represent apparent intentions as observer-dependent narratives grounded in synchronized social recordings and linked to participant goals.
MFZbESZmkR.evidence: The dataset supports intent-narrative analyses and apparent-intent benchmarks using recordings from a real interdisciplinary scientific workshop.
MFZbESZmkR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the synchronized multimodal recordings of real networking interactions together with participant goals and perceived-intention annotations.
MFZbESZmkR.main_concern: The benchmark labels and metrics do not convincingly establish reliable, grounded measurement of apparent intentions.

n542Px1q4r.one_liner: Modulation-guided patch-block pruning compresses a pixel-space diffusion transformer while retaining its texture reconstruction pathway.
n542Px1q4r.problem: One-step latent diffusion super-resolution still incurs substantial VAE encoding and decoding costs.
n542Px1q4r.method: LiPDiT-SR performs one-step super-resolution directly in pixel space and prunes the computationally dominant patch pathway. MDBS selects blocks by downstream modulation disruption, while SMA aligns modulation with the preceding reference model during pruning.
n542Px1q4r.key_idea: Prune patch blocks that least disrupt pixel-path modulation and align retained modulation signals with the reference model.
n542Px1q4r.evidence: Experiments on synthetic and real-world super-resolution benchmarks include runtime profiling and ablations of block selection and modulation alignment.
n542Px1q4r.claimed_gains: LiPDiT-SR reports a 1.6× inference speedup for ×4 super-resolution with comparable visual quality.
n542Px1q4r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that runtime profiling motivates patch-path compression and supports a practical inference-speed benefit.
n542Px1q4r.main_concern: The contribution beyond PixelDiT is limited to pruning and alignment, whose advantages over alternative mechanisms remain insufficiently established.

dbWwZMdPJ3.one_liner: Stage-wise latent divergence, gated by a learned classifier, supplies intrinsic exploration rewards for language-model reasoning.
dbWwZMdPJ3.problem: Sparse answer rewards and token-level diversity signals provide limited guidance toward substantively different reasoning paths.
dbWwZMdPJ3.method: LaDex segments grouped reasoning trajectories into stages and compares their latent states. A Latent Classifier Network adjusts stage-level divergence signals before aggregation into intrinsic rewards for policy optimization.
dbWwZMdPJ3.key_idea: Reward divergence among stage-aligned latent trajectories while a learned classifier gates exploration signals.
dbWwZMdPJ3.evidence: The supplied text describes reasoning-benchmark experiments across backbones, pass@k and mean-accuracy evaluation, and a multi-turn agent environment.
dbWwZMdPJ3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the stage-level latent exploration mechanism clearly structured and compatible with existing RLVR training.
dbWwZMdPJ3.main_concern: The evidence does not establish that stage-aligned latent distances measure useful reasoning diversity better than simpler alternatives.

U2TiiqO18x.one_liner: Shared attention over text and continuous motion, with role-specific parameters, unifies motion understanding, generation, completion, and editing.
U2TiiqO18x.problem: Existing unified motion models often separate language-based understanding from generation through a separate latent diffusion module.
U2TiiqO18x.method: Möbius brings clean motion, noisy motion, and text into shared attention while assigning role-specific parameters to understanding and generation. It operates on continuous raw motion frames without discrete tokens or a pretrained motion VAE.
U2TiiqO18x.key_idea: Place clean and noisy motion alongside text in shared attention, using role-specific parameters for understanding and generation streams.
U2TiiqO18x.evidence: Experiments include HumanML3D, quantitative and qualitative motion-task evaluations, and scaling to 1.7B parameters with 1,700 hours of motion data.
U2TiiqO18x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the shared representation and report convincing quantitative and qualitative results across multiple motion tasks.
U2TiiqO18x.main_concern: The experiments do not sufficiently isolate which architectural or training choices produce the reported gains.

4gsoMIcPNt.one_liner: Learned protein-specific elastic interactions generate globally coupled displacement covariances, with marginal calibration that preserves inter-residue canonical correlations.
4gsoMIcPNt.problem: Direct covariance predictors lack directional global coupling, while elastic network models rely on fixed, hand-designed interactions.
4gsoMIcPNt.method: ENMulator maps protein sequence and structure to elastic interactions whose Hessian induces residue-level displacement covariance. A complementary branch predicts anisotropic marginals, which blockwise geodesic congruence calibrates while preserving canonical correlations.
4gsoMIcPNt.key_idea: Learn elastic interactions to induce global covariance, then calibrate residue marginals without changing inter-residue canonical correlations.
4gsoMIcPNt.evidence: ATLAS test-set covariance and sampled-ensemble evaluations compare covariance geometry, collective modes, and correlated motion against prescribed elastic networks and direct predictors.
4gsoMIcPNt.claimed_gains: The abstract reports reducing DCCM error by 17%.
4gsoMIcPNt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the physical motivation and formal treatment of directional coupling through learned elastic interactions.
4gsoMIcPNt.main_concern: The limited evaluation and mixed gains against strong alternatives leave the added architectural complexity insufficiently justified.

R3GrM89Q8y.one_liner: Complementary graph-matching experts iteratively refine confidence-weighted correspondences for incomplete multi-view clustering.
R3GrM89Q8y.problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering often treats observed cross-view correspondences as equally reliable despite inconsistent semantic and structural evidence.
R3GrM89Q8y.method: The framework initializes soft correspondences from partial overlap and selects an anchor view. Koopmans–Beckmann and anchor-based Lawler QAP experts combine local affinities and higher-order structure, with an outlier state and momentum-based confidence refinement.
R3GrM89Q8y.key_idea: Fuse local and higher-order graph-matching evidence through momentum updates to revise cross-view correspondence confidence.
R3GrM89Q8y.evidence: Review text describes clustering experiments and expert-removal ablations, while noting that several analyses cover only a subset of datasets.
R3GrM89Q8y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider reliability-aware correspondence learning and complementary structural matching reasonable approaches to incomplete multi-view clustering.
R3GrM89Q8y.main_concern: The heuristic correspondence updates and their interaction with representation learning lack sufficient justification.

91HI7K7nRb.one_liner: Raw-image statistics prune visual redundancy before decoding, followed by progressive instruction-dependent token pruning inside the language model.
91HI7K7nRb.problem: High-resolution vision-language inputs produce large visual-token sequences with substantial computational overhead.
91HI7K7nRb.method: ERASE separates image-level redundancy removal from instruction-dependent pruning in a training-free pipeline. Lightweight raw-image statistics set initial retention, and decoder-layer pruning progressively removes instruction-irrelevant tokens.
91HI7K7nRb.key_idea: Use raw-image statistics for initial token retention, then progressively prune tokens according to instruction relevance across decoder layers.
91HI7K7nRb.evidence: Experiments include Qwen2.5-VL-7B accuracy measurements under visual-token compression and ablations of the two pruning stages.
91HI7K7nRb.claimed_gains: ERASE retains 95.70% of the original model's accuracy at 25% token retention on Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
91HI7K7nRb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical separation of image redundancy and instruction relevance using inexpensive image statistics.
91HI7K7nRb.main_concern: The method largely combines established pruning ideas and handcrafted visual cues, with a limited incremental contribution from its second stage.

nAgVXhx03o.one_liner: Conditions flow-based motion generation on sparse structural cognitive maps and selects trajectories with a learned forward dynamics model.
nAgVXhx03o.problem: Conventional robotic navigation relies on dense metric maps and accurate global localization whose storage and computation scale poorly with environment size.
nAgVXhx03o.method: Map2Motion conditions a flow-based distribution of prospective local motions on current perception and sparse structural guidance from a cognitive map. A learned forward dynamics model predicts future embodied states and traversability of candidate motions for closed-loop selection and execution.
nAgVXhx03o.key_idea: Generates candidate local trajectories via a structure-conditioned flow model and evaluates their future states and traversability using a learned forward dynamics model.
nAgVXhx03o.evidence: Evaluated in simulation on the MP3D benchmark and in 3,029.4 m^2 real-world building navigation tasks.
nAgVXhx03o.claimed_gains: Achieves an 86% success rate on MP3D with 4.7% of dense-map storage (64% SR under 0.2 m localization error), and 78% SR with 21.04 ms planning latency and 2.6% storage in real-world navigation.
nAgVXhx03o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of sparse global structural guidance from local prospective motion generation and forward-dynamics evaluation intuitive and practically effective.
nAgVXhx03o.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing details on train/test scene separation and generalization protocols, insufficient isolation of the flow generator and dynamics evaluator in ablations, and overstated practical importance of map-storage savings.

mg63vQ1WXH.one_liner: Combines token-wise KL divergence between standard and guided prompts with a staged length bonus for spatial reasoning RL.
mg63vQ1WXH.problem: Standard GRPO for multi-view spatial reasoning provides only sparse outcome feedback without localizing trajectory errors or controlling verbose chain-of-thought responses.
mg63vQ1WXH.method: LENGUARD-GPC computes the token-sum KL divergence between predictive distributions under a standard prompt and a guided prompt as a dense process reward during GRPO training. To prevent the cumulative KL penalty from collapsing responses to minimal length, it adds a staged length bonus that keeps reasoning trajectories within a target range.
mg63vQ1WXH.key_idea: Penalizes token-wise KL divergence between standard and guided-prompt predictions while applying a piecewise staged length bonus to regulate chain-of-thought length.
mg63vQ1WXH.evidence: Evaluated on multi-view spatial reasoning benchmarks including MMSI and ViewSpatial against a vanilla GRPO baseline.
mg63vQ1WXH.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy over vanilla GRPO from 32.2% to 36.1% on MMSI and from 44.4% to 46.9% on ViewSpatial.
mg63vQ1WXH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the reward design consistently improves multi-view spatial reasoning accuracy while reducing response token length without adding inference overhead.
mg63vQ1WXH.main_concern: Reviewers note missing implementation details on how guided prompts and hints are constructed, lack of direct validation that low prompt-KL measures reasoning quality rather than answer leakage, and insufficient training-compute analysis.

OaHIuchkSk.one_liner: Formulates cross-model intermediate computation reuse as an online bandit-scheduling problem solved with optimistic quality estimates and adaptive stopping.
OaHIuchkSk.problem: Cross-model computation reuse lacks theoretical optimization frameworks that jointly handle unknown cross-model reuse quality and NP-hard shared-cost preparation scheduling.
OaHIuchkSk.method: The authors formulate cross-model computation reuse as an online decision problem and propose Quality-Aware Reuse Scheduling (QARS). QARS learns task-dependent reuse quality from delayed feedback via optimistic estimates and uses a quality-aware stopping rule to adapt coupled preparation and reuse scheduling accuracy to current uncertainty.
OaHIuchkSk.key_idea: Combines optimistic online bandit estimation of reuse quality with an uncertainty-matched stopping criterion for the coupled NP-hard preparation and task-assignment schedule.
OaHIuchkSk.evidence: Supported by regret analysis separating learning and optimization error and semi-synthetic simulations built on public datasets with Qwen model variants.
OaHIuchkSk.claimed_gains: Achieves O~(sqrt(T)) regret while preserving feasibility.
OaHIuchkSk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the rigorous theoretical formulation of coupled preparation costs and uncertain reuse quality, particularly the uncertainty-adaptive stopping rule.
OaHIuchkSk.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the myopic single-step regret benchmark ignores cross-step caching value over time, and experiments rely on a semi-synthetic simulator that enforces a restrictive linear quality assumption by construction.

R6A6kaeZxr.one_liner: Prunes visual tracking tokens using a reinforcement learning policy conditioned on recent target motion trajectories.
R6A6kaeZxr.problem: Existing token pruning methods for visual tracking rely on single-frame cues and overlook temporal motion continuity when estimating token importance.
R6A6kaeZxr.method: Trajectory-Guided Token Pruning (TGTP) models token pruning as a sequential decision problem using a Trajectory Policy Network that takes recent target trajectories as state to predict motion priors, motion uncertainty, and frame-wise token keep ratios. The plug-in module is trained with reinforcement learning rewards balancing tracking accuracy, FLOPs, uncertainty regularization, and target-token retention.
R6A6kaeZxr.key_idea: Uses an RL policy conditioned on historical target bounding-box trajectories to predict spatial motion priors and adaptive token retention ratios for each frame.
R6A6kaeZxr.evidence: Evaluated as a plug-in across multiple single-modal (RGB) and multi-modal visual tracking baselines and datasets.
R6A6kaeZxr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using historical motion trajectories to guide spatial token pruning is well-suited to visual tracking and plugs easily into diverse tracking architectures.
R6A6kaeZxr.main_concern: Reviewers state that the necessity of reinforcement learning over simpler rule-based or supervised motion priors is not justified, given per-frame reward formulations and incomplete accounting of policy overhead.

xoMVx0wQSt.one_liner: Decomposes multiclass utility calibration error across label-tree internal nodes and iteratively updates violated nodes to prevent error cancellation.
xoMVx0wQSt.problem: Standard Utility Calibration in hierarchical multiclass problems allows positive and negative utility errors across different internal nodes of a label tree to cancel out, hiding local miscalibration.
xoMVx0wQSt.method: The authors derive an exact decomposition of utility calibration discrepancy across the internal nodes of a label hierarchy and propose Hierarchical Utility Calibration (HUC) to audit each node's contribution before summation. They also introduce HUC Boost, an algorithm that selectively updates only violated internal nodes with finite-sample evaluation bounds.
xoMVx0wQSt.key_idea: Audits and boosts utility calibration discrepancies at each internal node of a label hierarchy separately so opposite-signed node errors cannot cancel in the aggregate utility.
xoMVx0wQSt.evidence: Supported by theoretical finite-sample bounds and empirical calibration experiments on hierarchical multiclass tasks.
xoMVx0wQSt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing utility calibration along a label tree clearly identifies cross-node error cancellation and is backed by sound theoretical analysis.
xoMVx0wQSt.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical gains over standard UC-Boost are mixed or incompletely isolated, and the theoretical guarantees assume a fixed schedule rather than the adaptive procedure used in experiments.

BnW3Ordr8O.one_liner: Mechanistically analyzes a Manhattan-navigation transformer, tracing behavioral failures to superposed intersection feature interference mitigated by affordance packing.
BnW3Ordr8O.problem: Behavioral navigation failures in transformers are often misinterpreted as the absence of an internal world model rather than localized failures in using learned representations.
BnW3Ordr8O.method: The authors apply probing, causal teleportation interventions, and ablations to TaxiGPT, a transformer trained on Manhattan random walks. They show that the model encodes intersections, street transitions, position tracking, and a goal compass, while tracing navigation slips to interference among superposed intersection features and showing how grouping intersections with identical legal moves (affordance packing) limits errors.
BnW3Ordr8O.key_idea: Uses causal activation interventions and decoding indicators to separate internal map representation, position localization under feature superposition, and affordance-grouped action selection.
BnW3Ordr8O.evidence: Evaluated via mechanistic probing and causal interventions on TaxiGPT checkpoints trained on a 4,516-intersection Manhattan grid.
BnW3Ordr8O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the causal interventions—such as activation teleportation and compass ablations—that go beyond linear probing to dissect how internal representations drive navigation.
BnW3Ordr8O.main_concern: Reviewers note that all claims rely on a single deterministic Manhattan grid environment, with uneven transition-steering reliability and incomplete positioning against prior world-model interpretability literature.

HY3KdWxPmU.one_liner: Curates a 7,542-clip multimodal 3D conversational motion dataset across 302 personas and introduces a persona-motion matching metric.
HY3KdWxPmU.problem: Existing 3D human motion datasets rarely pair natural-language personality profiles with synchronized conversational speech and motion.
HY3KdWxPmU.method: The authors introduce PersonaAct, a multimodal 3D dataset containing 7,542 clips across 302 personas that pairs persona profiles and motion descriptions with synchronized speech, body, hand, and facial motion. They also propose a contrastive persona-motion matching metric to benchmark how well generated motion reflects target character profiles alongside speech and text conditions.
HY3KdWxPmU.key_idea: Pairs 302 natural-language persona profiles with synchronized conversational speech and full-body 3D motion capture and evaluates character fidelity via a learned persona-motion matching metric.
HY3KdWxPmU.evidence: Evaluated across baseline motion generation methods on the 7,542-clip PersonaAct benchmark with conditioning ablations and human agreement checks.
HY3KdWxPmU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the dataset fills a practical gap for persona-conditioned conversational motion and captures rich full-body, hand, and facial expressions.
HY3KdWxPmU.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the lack of a new motion generation method, moderate correlation of the proposed persona-motion metric with small-sample human judgments, and missing actor collection or lip-sync evaluation details.

Ox5olvrFJe.one_liner: Reallocates frame-wise RVQ code depth in frozen speech codecs using stage-1 codes as a shared prefix with utterance-level gating.
Ox5olvrFJe.problem: Adaptive frame-wise bit allocation in neural speech codecs typically requires retraining the codec or transmitting frame-level allocation side information.
Ox5olvrFJe.method: Agreeing on Allocation uses the mandatory first-stage residual vector quantization (RVQ) codes of an utterance as a shared prefix so the encoder and decoder independently compute the same frame-wise code budget allocation in a frozen codec without frame-level signaling. A selective deployment gate at the encoder compares the adaptive reconstruction against uniform allocation and signals a single utterance-level bit to fall back when quality drops.
Ox5olvrFJe.key_idea: Derives identical frame-wise RVQ depth allocations at both encoder and decoder from shared stage-1 RVQ codes, paired with a 1-bit utterance-level fallback check.
Ox5olvrFJe.evidence: Evaluated via objective fidelity metrics (including PESQ upper confidence bounds on LibriSpeech) and a listening study on frozen neural speech codecs.
Ox5olvrFJe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the zero-side-information shared-prefix trick for frame-wise bit reallocation on frozen codecs and the thorough statistical and perceptual evaluation.
