Ox5olvrFJe.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical motivation for retrofitting a frozen codec in an offline full-utterance regime rather than using native variable-bitrate codecs, as well as heavy reliance on PESQ throughout training and evaluation.

euvTjBRqAT.one_liner: Predicts short-horizon wind at unvisited future quadrotor control locations by combining a transported onboard-sensing reference with a physics-constrained residual.
euvTjBRqAT.problem: Onboard quadrotor wind sensors only measure disturbances along past traversed positions, leaving unvisited future control query locations unobserved for preview control.
euvTjBRqAT.method: EgoCast decomposes short-horizon wind forecasting at future control queries into a deterministic reference transported from recent onboard observations and a learned neural residual for local evolution. Label-anchored physical constraints supervise the residual where direct measurements are sparse, and the resulting aerodynamic force preview is fed into a model predictive controller.
euvTjBRqAT.key_idea: Combines a motion-transported historical wind measurement reference with a physics-regularized neural residual queried at future quadrotor control coordinates.
euvTjBRqAT.evidence: Evaluated in simulated wind-field forecasting across 25 sensing-supervision configurations and closed-loop quadrotor trajectory tracking with DOB-MPC across four trajectories.
euvTjBRqAT.claimed_gains: Reduces future-query wind RMSE by 18.5–26.5% over direct full-field prediction and reduces aerodynamic force-preview RMSE by 29.1–39.3% over the data-only counterpart.
euvTjBRqAT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clean formulation of future-query wind preview and the well-controlled forecasting comparisons under matched architectures and budgets.
euvTjBRqAT.main_concern: Reviewers note that the simple deterministic Ego-Transport baseline already matches or beats the full learned model in several closed-loop tracking settings, and all experiments are limited to simulation.

gjlr1ocrqe.one_liner: Trains token-wise layer-to-layer linear maps via prediction distillation to translate KV caches between distinct frozen LLMs.
gjlr1ocrqe.problem: Switching between different LLMs over a shared context requires re-prefilling the entire prompt because KV-cache representations are model-specific.
gjlr1ocrqe.method: KV-Lingo learns a set of token-wise linear projections mapping source-model keys and values to target-model layers for a pair of frozen LLMs. Rather than only matching target KV states in closed form, the linear maps are trained via distillation to minimize the divergence between the target model's output predictions given its native cache versus the translated cache.
gjlr1ocrqe.key_idea: Applies per-layer linear transformations to token KV vectors trained by minimizing output prediction divergence against the target LLM running on its native KV cache.
gjlr1ocrqe.evidence: Evaluated across multiple frozen LLM pairs varying in size, architecture, and tokenizer on reasoning, general, and long-context retrieval benchmarks.
gjlr1ocrqe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training linear KV-cache translators with output self-distillation substantially outperforms closed-form cache reconstruction and is transparently evaluated across diverse model pairs.
gjlr1ocrqe.main_concern: Reviewers point out that small-to-large cache translation frequently fails to improve over the small model alone, degrades on long-context retrieval, and requires training pairwise directional translators without a unified latency-accuracy comparison against all baselines.

hfLwjtoM3G.one_liner: Uses graded group algebras to compute neuromanifold dimension and prove generic identifiability for polynomial group convolutional networks.
hfLwjtoM3G.problem: The geometric dimension and parameter identifiability of group-equivariant convolutional neural networks with polynomial activations over arbitrary finite groups remain uncharacterized.
hfLwjtoM3G.method: The authors formulate polynomial group convolutional neural networks (PGCNNs) for any finite group G within graded group algebras, linking Hadamard and Kronecker product parameterizations via a linear map. They compute the exact dimension of the resulting neuromanifold and show that the general fiber of both parameterizations is trivial up to the regular group action and scaling.
hfLwjtoM3G.key_idea: Factorizes polynomial group convolutions in graded group algebras via Kronecker and Hadamard representations to bound neuromanifold dimension and show fibers are trivial up to group action and scaling.
hfLwjtoM3G.evidence: Supported by algebraic-geometric proofs for arbitrary finite groups and numerical verifications on small finite groups and shallow networks.
hfLwjtoM3G.claimed_gains: Proves that the metric entropy of the PGCNN neuromanifold is smaller by a factor |G| than that of an equi-width polynomial network.
hfLwjtoM3G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the rigorous algebraic-geometric framework proving neuromanifold dimension and generic identifiability across arbitrary finite groups and polynomial degrees.
hfLwjtoM3G.main_concern: Reviewers note unclear technical novelty over the authors' closely related prior work, a restrictive assumption that the input domain equals the finite group G, and the absence of practical ML experiments.

8GE0wxbmR0.one_liner: Infers forgotten class labels in federated unlearning from an ordinary client vantage by matching broadcast classifier-layer changes to local templates.
8GE0wxbmR0.problem: Prior forgotten-label inference attacks in federated unlearning assume a privileged server vantage with access to individual client updates, leaving client-side privacy risks under a trusted server unexplored.
8GE0wxbmR0.method: Active Unlearning Probing (AUP) operates from a normal federated client that computes per-class gradient templates using only its own local labeled data. When a global model update reflects an unlearning event, the client matches the direction of the broadcast classifier-layer parameter change against its local class templates to infer which label class another client requested to forget.
8GE0wxbmR0.key_idea: Matches the classifier-layer parameter difference of broadcast global models against locally constructed class-specific unlearning gradient templates.
8GE0wxbmR0.evidence: Evaluated on CIFAR-10, MNIST, CIFAR-100 (with ViT-B/16), and Yahoo Answers across two unlearning mechanisms and multi-class deletion settings.
8GE0wxbmR0.claimed_gains: Conditional on event detection, identifies the forgotten label at 0.96 accuracy on CIFAR-10 and 0.80 on MNIST, and recovers three simultaneously deleted classes at 0.58 IoU.
8GE0wxbmR0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that demonstrating forgotten-label inference from an ordinary client's perspective using only broadcast global models exposes a realistic and previously overlooked privacy threat.
8GE0wxbmR0.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that attack accuracy is reported conditional on detecting an unlearning event without thoroughly evaluating end-to-end event detection rates and false-positive rates.

pBfyP0gHsJ.one_liner: Formulates multi-prompt factual unlearning in LLMs as a quadratic protected common-descent optimization over low-rank transformer memory updates.
pBfyP0gHsJ.problem: Single-target knowledge editing fails to verify whether one knowledge-preserving parameter update can simultaneously suppress an old fact across multiple conflicting prompts and internal access routes.
pBfyP0gHsJ.method: U2E casts targeted factual unlearning as a quadratic protected common-descent problem that checks whether multiple access-specific score decreases admit a shared parameter update under covariance and null-space preservation constraints. It constructs low-rank candidate updates from local progress estimates and validates them on the full nonlinear model before committing.
pBfyP0gHsJ.key_idea: Solves a constrained quadratic program to find a shared low-rank weight update that jointly decreases old-answer scores across multiple prompt accesses within a knowledge-preserving null space.
pBfyP0gHsJ.evidence: Evaluated on factual unlearning benchmarks (including MultiCounterFact on Llama and Qwen models) against loss-based and editing baselines, including unseen access routes and extraction attacks.
pBfyP0gHsJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the principled formulation of multi-access factual suppression under shared knowledge-preservation constraints.
pBfyP0gHsJ.main_concern: Reviewers point to a mismatch between the constrained trust-region theory and the final committed update equation, poorly tuned or collapsing baselines, and missing implementation details.

P1licWLgVf.one_liner: Uses a meta-agent to dynamically spawn specialized worker agents, route checkpointed structured memories over sparse graphs, and synthesize answers.
P1licWLgVf.problem: Existing multi-agent LLM frameworks typically fix worker roles, communication topologies, or aggregation rules beforehand rather than adapting the entire lifecycle to each task.
P1licWLgVf.method: TANGO uses a meta-agent to manage three stages for each input task: creating specialized worker agents with distinct strategies and tools, periodically constructing a sparse directed communication graph to route information packets from workers' structured memory states, and synthesizing a final response from terminal answers and memory records.
P1licWLgVf.key_idea: Coordinates task-specific worker agents through periodic meta-agent checkpoints that build sparse directed routing topologies over structured worker memories recording progress, hypotheses, and open questions.
P1licWLgVf.evidence: Evaluated with Gemini-2.5-Flash on GAIA, GPQA-Diamond, Omni-MATH, and HumanEval using 3-run mean accuracy and Pass@3.
P1licWLgVf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that integrating task-specific worker creation, structured memory, and selective meta-agent routing yields strong accuracy improvements on challenging benchmarks such as GAIA.
P1licWLgVf.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments use only a single LLM backbone (Gemini-2.5-Flash), lack an end-to-end compute and token cost breakdown, and combine familiar prompt-based orchestration components with underspecified formal notation.

YPn1sxZ3UV.one_liner: Co-designs integer rank-based federated learning with membership-gated robust aggregation and additive homomorphic encryption.
YPn1sxZ3UV.problem: Combining real-valued client updates, Byzantine-robust aggregation, and homomorphic encryption in federated learning incurs heavy computation and communication overhead.
YPn1sxZ3UV.method: CertiRank replaces real-valued model updates with integer parameter rankings and introduces Certified Membership-gated Ranking Aggregation (CMGRA), which separates subnetwork membership selection from fine-grained rank ordering. It pairs CMGRA with coefficient-packed RLWE additive homomorphic encryption (SEncode) and validity verification so the server aggregates and certifies encrypted rankings using lightweight additions.
YPn1sxZ3UV.key_idea: Encodes client updates as integer rankings packed into RLWE ciphertexts, allowing Byzantine-robust subnetwork membership gating and rank aggregation via homomorphic addition.
YPn1sxZ3UV.evidence: Evaluated under poisoning attacks against existing homomorphic-encryption-based Byzantine-robust federated learning baselines.
YPn1sxZ3UV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that co-designing integer rank updates with additive homomorphic encryption substantially reduces cryptographic computation and communication overhead compared to real-valued encrypted baselines.
YPn1sxZ3UV.main_concern: Reviewers identify security and robustness gaps in the verification protocol, noting that per-client verification plaintexts leak rank and block information to the secret-key server and unbounded ciphertext noise could corrupt decrypted aggregates.

rfgZPSOF2L.one_liner: Predicts LLM repetition collapse onset from prompt-estimated drifting and merging timescales and regularizes merging time during fine-tuning.
rfgZPSOF2L.problem: The dynamical mechanisms that cause long-horizon autoregressive LLM generation to degenerate into persistent repetition remain poorly quantified.
rfgZPSOF2L.method: The authors decompose autoregressive text degeneration into two timescales measured directly from prompts: drifting time (departure from the natural-language distribution via excess cross-entropy) and merging time (convergence of predictions from distinct histories). They fit a regression model using these two timescales to predict repetition collapse onset and introduce a self-supervised fine-tuning loss that increases merging time.
rfgZPSOF2L.key_idea: Estimates distribution-drift and history-merging timescales directly from prompt representations to predict repetition onset and penalizes fast history merging during fine-tuning.
rfgZPSOF2L.evidence: Evaluated across 16 LLMs, five corpora, and five attention temperatures, plus fine-tuning experiments on Llama-3.1-8B.
rfgZPSOF2L.claimed_gains: Explains 93.8% of the variance in mean log collapse time on fitting data, and fine-tuning increases Llama-3.1-8B's geometric-mean collapse time to 5.52x its original value with zero additional data.
rfgZPSOF2L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decomposition of autoregressive degeneration into prompt-measurable drifting and merging timescales insightful and well supported by predictive fits and fine-tuning intervention.
rfgZPSOF2L.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical validation focuses almost entirely on greedy-decoding repetition (REP-4) in base models rather than broader generation quality or instruction-tuned sampling, and question the functional form combining the two timescales.

Edbm1wp43K.one_liner: Routes multi-style augmented images across photometric, textural, and spatial prototype experts via preference learning for single-domain generalized object detection.
Edbm1wp43K.problem: Object detectors trained on a single source domain struggle to generalize to unseen target domains comprising complex combinations of illumination, weather, and style shifts.
Edbm1wp43K.method: Mixture of Prototype Experts (MoPE) pairs predefined atomic visual prototypes across photometric, textural, and spatial dimensions with dedicated expert modules and a shared expert. Grounded by a Multi-Style Augmentation (MSA) pipeline, a router is trained with a preference optimization loss to assign higher selection probabilities to scene-relevant prototype experts than to irrelevant ones.
Edbm1wp43K.key_idea: Trains an expert router with a pairwise preference objective over synthetic multi-style augmentations to sparsely combine photometric, textural, and spatial prototype experts.
Edbm1wp43K.evidence: Evaluated on single-domain generalized object detection benchmarks across unseen weather conditions, artistic styles, and detector backbones.
Edbm1wp43K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that factorizing domain shifts into semantic prototype experts is clearly presented and yields consistent cross-domain detection improvements.
Edbm1wp43K.main_concern: Reviewers note that most of the mAP gain comes from the synthetic Multi-Style Augmentation rather than the preference-routed MoE, and comparisons against standard MoE or simpler multi-label routing losses under the same augmentation are missing.

iYFdGsk9V7.one_liner: Selects discriminative CLIP image patches using LLM-generated class descriptions and aligns them via optimal transport for class-incremental learning.
iYFdGsk9V7.problem: CLIP-based class-incremental learning methods typically align only global image and text tokens, discarding fine-grained local patch semantics that distinguish visually similar classes.
iYFdGsk9V7.method: Semantic-guided Patch-level Alignment (SPA) feeds representative class images to GPT-5 to generate fine-grained class-wise semantic descriptions, which guide the selection of discriminative local image patches from a frozen CLIP encoder. It then applies optimal transport to align the selected visual patch tokens with the fine-grained textual tokens alongside task-specific projectors and feature replay.
iYFdGsk9V7.key_idea: Uses LLM-generated class attribute descriptions to filter informative visual patch tokens and aligns them with text tokens via optimal transport on top of a frozen CLIP backbone.
iYFdGsk9V7.evidence: Evaluated across nine class-incremental learning benchmarks and two class-split protocols with controlled semantic-prior ablations.
iYFdGsk9V7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad evaluation across nine datasets and the controlled five-seed experiments isolating the patch-alignment mechanism under identical GPT-generated class descriptions.
iYFdGsk9V7.main_concern: Reviewers view the technical components—patch-text optimal transport, LLM attribute descriptions, expanding projectors, and Gaussian pseudo-feature replay—as closely following existing vision-language and incremental learning methods such as PLOT and GalLoP.

Th9EmakZ47.one_liner: Projects gradients and optimizer updates out of cumulative task-update subspaces while ordering and cycling tasks in multi-teacher on-policy distillation.
Th9EmakZ47.problem: Distilling multiple specialized teachers into a single student model via on-policy distillation causes cross-task interference where improving one capability degrades previously learned ones.
Th9EmakZ47.method: Projection-based Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (PMOPD) tracks low-dimensional subspaces formed by cumulative parameter displacements of each task and projects both raw gradients and preconditioned optimizer updates to remove components overlapping with protected subspaces. It pairs this projection with a conflict probe that determines task ordering and a multi-cycle training schedule.
Th9EmakZ47.key_idea: Projects both gradients and adaptive optimizer updates orthogonal to low-rank subspaces extracted from cumulative per-task parameter displacements across cyclic multi-teacher distillation.
Th9EmakZ47.evidence: Evaluated on multi-teacher on-policy distillation across Code, Reason, and Math tasks on two LLM families.
Th9EmakZ47.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that tracking cumulative parameter displacements and projecting both gradients and preconditioned optimizer updates (e.g., under Adafactor) is a well-motivated way to reduce multi-teacher interference.
Th9EmakZ47.main_concern: Reviewers point out that subspace overlap can reflect beneficial positive transfer rather than destructive conflict, and the selection of task ordering and cycle counts lacks an independent validation protocol.

3SWlPGX3Di.one_liner: Predicts per-triangle Jacobian mesh correctives from tracked surface strain to reconstruct explicit wrinkle geometry in 3D Gaussian head avatars.
3SWlPGX3Di.problem: Multi-view head avatar reconstruction methods typically bake expression wrinkles into appearance textures or unconstrained displacements rather than modeling their mechanical geometric cause.
3SWlPGX3Di.method: StrainAvatar computes the analytical Green-Lagrange strain of a coarse tracked facial mesh as an identity-agnostic compression signal and uses a subject-specific network to predict per-triangle Jacobian correctives, which are integrated into a refined mesh via a Poisson solve. Gaussian primitives are then transported using the deformation gradient of the strain-corrected mesh.
3SWlPGX3Di.key_idea: Maps local surface strain of a tracked mesh to per-triangle Jacobian correctives solved via a Poisson system, and transports 3D Gaussians with the resulting deformation gradient.
3SWlPGX3Di.evidence: Evaluated on multi-view RGB head avatar datasets measuring rendering quality, surface-normal accuracy, and stereo mesh depth error.
3SWlPGX3Di.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the biomechanically motivated factorization of expression strain and per-triangle Jacobian Poisson integration well-grounded for guaranteeing zero-corrective consistency with the base tracker.
3SWlPGX3Di.main_concern: Reviewers note that quantitative depth and normal references cannot resolve fine wrinkle geometry, and ablations do not cleanly isolate strain conditioning from general mesh refinement or Gaussian alignment losses.

6kwgPuiq8R.one_liner: Antisymmetric encoder differences convert pixel-space corrections into latent updates without decoder backpropagation.
6kwgPuiq8R.problem: Decoder-backward guidance dominates latent diffusion inverse-solving cost, while direct re-encoding can distort the latent prior.
6kwgPuiq8R.method: ASLU computes a scaled half-difference between encoder outputs at positive and negative pixel-space perturbations. This update vanishes for zero correction and cancels second-order encoder-curvature terms while retaining the first-order Jacobian response.
6kwgPuiq8R.key_idea: Subtract encoder evaluations at opposite pixel-space perturbations to cancel second-order curvature bias and avoid decoder gradients.
6kwgPuiq8R.evidence: Controlled correction experiments and integrations into high-resolution image inverse solvers, CT reconstruction, and black-hole video reconstruction assess memory and reconstruction quality.
6kwgPuiq8R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the simple forward-only update for addressing a real memory and runtime bottleneck.
6kwgPuiq8R.main_concern: The experiments do not convincingly isolate antisymmetric curvature cancellation from the efficiency benefits shared by one-sided forward-only updates.

wcJotvOM5x.one_liner: Separate body, hand, and object latents exchange full-state information during coupled flow updates for human-object interaction modeling.
wcJotvOM5x.problem: Human-object interaction generation must preserve distinct motion structures while coordinating contact, relative pose, and timing.
wcJotvOM5x.method: TRACE encodes body, object, and hand motion separately and predicts each stream's velocity from the complete interaction state. Decoded geometric losses constrain contact and object-relative motion, while joint completion training supports missing-stream reconstruction and frozen features support language-based understanding.
wcJotvOM5x.key_idea: Keep motion-stream states separate but condition every stream's velocity on all streams, with geometric constraints after decoding.
wcJotvOM5x.evidence: InterAct, OMOMO, and BEHAVE experiments examine generation, stream completion, and understanding, with contact metrics and geometric-loss ablations.
wcJotvOM5x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the architecture suits coordinated motion modeling and produces strong contact-consistency results.
wcJotvOM5x.main_concern: The contribution beyond existing decomposed or jointly interacting motion models is unclear, and stream-modeling ablations lack sufficient implementation detail.

slvB1hDWUu.one_liner: Joint hint generation and solving identify verified improvements, then attribution-weighted training internalizes them for hint-free agent execution.
slvB1hDWUu.problem: Agent self-improvement often separates experience extraction from learning, so extracted guidance does not track evolving capability gaps.
slvB1hDWUu.method: HELICES jointly optimizes hint generation and utilization, identifying useful hints by gains over unguided execution. After independent confirmation, it internalizes gains through full action supervision and selective reasoning-token weights based on hint attribution.
slvB1hDWUu.key_idea: Probe capabilities with self-generated hints, independently verify gains, and internalize them using action supervision and hint-attributed reasoning weights.
slvB1hDWUu.evidence: Three agent benchmarks include unseen-task hint-free evaluation, multiple full-pipeline seeds, matched-budget comparisons, and internalization controls.
slvB1hDWUu.claimed_gains: HELICES surpasses strong baselines by up to 7.2 percentage points.
slvB1hDWUu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit independent gain confirmation and controlled, repeated evaluations of hint-free performance.
slvB1hDWUu.main_concern: The method's distinction from prior hint-guided learning and self-distillation approaches remains insufficiently established.

TQM6zSBRcF.one_liner: Ridge-flow prediction, phase-free spectral loss, and attention across capture frames complete partial contactless fingerprints.
TQM6zSBRcF.problem: Partial, degraded contactless fingerprints leave ridge phase outside the visible region undetermined, complicating faithful completion.
TQM6zSBRcF.method: SweepFill predicts whole-print ridge flow and frequency at its bottleneck before decoding pixels with a phase-free spectral loss. Joint attention over frames from the same finger sweep supplies evidence for hidden regions.
TQM6zSBRcF.key_idea: Predict ridge flow and frequency before pixels, supervise spectral amplitude without phase, and attend to other capture-sweep frames.
TQM6zSBRcF.evidence: MMFV experiments use two fingerprint matchers under cross-session evaluation, with spectral-loss ablations and analyses of reference frames, minutiae, and ridge phase.
TQM6zSBRcF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the use of ridge structure and capture-sweep evidence well motivated and value evaluation through fingerprint recognition.
TQM6zSBRcF.main_concern: Unequal comparison budgets and insufficient reference-guided baselines leave the proposed design's contribution beyond access to additional frames unclear.

iDT8UhdSkV.one_liner: Balanced, gene-entropy-weighted detection prediction tests which preservation objectives support single-cell JEPA representations.
iDT8UhdSkV.problem: Single-cell JEPA studies change several components together, obscuring how collapse prevention and information-preservation targets affect transfer.
iDT8UhdSkV.method: The study fixes the encoder, views, training budget, and evaluation while varying regularization and preservation targets. DET-JEPA combines projector-space latent prediction with PCG-BCE, a per-cell-balanced, gene-entropy-weighted gene-detection loss.
iDT8UhdSkV.key_idea: Use per-cell balancing and gene-entropy weighting in a gene-detection objective paired with latent prediction.
iDT8UhdSkV.evidence: Controlled ablations evaluate zero-shot cell-type annotation and scIB biological conservation, with HLCA, PBMC, Great Apes, and protein-prediction results discussed in reviews.
iDT8UhdSkV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled component comparisons and ablations that isolate the contribution of gene-detection supervision.
iDT8UhdSkV.main_concern: PCG-BCE alone performs almost identically to DET-JEPA, leaving little evidence that the added latent-prediction branch contributes.

WJautZRC6V.one_liner: An odd-listener self-play game turns contrasting audio clips into verifiable rewards for fine-grained audio reasoning.
WJautZRC6V.problem: Audio language models struggle with event order, repetition, and duration, while post-training depends on costly labels or coarse signals.
WJautZRC6V.method: Audio-Zero assigns a reference audio to most players and a subtle variant to one listener, then generates clues and identifies the odd listener from their inconsistencies. The known assignment supplies rewards without annotated answers.
WJautZRC6V.key_idea: Use a known odd-listener assignment in audio-contrast self-play to reward clue generation and inconsistency-based identification.
WJautZRC6V.evidence: Experiments evaluate Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-Omni-7B on TREA, MMAU Test-mini, and MMAR, alongside game-component ablations and diagnostic analyses.
WJautZRC6V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the annotation-free self-play signal and the reported audio-reasoning improvements across two model backbones.
WJautZRC6V.main_concern: Reviewers find the methodological distinction from Vision-Zero insufficiently explained.

mFrtGjGu8e.one_liner: FedC² weights federated collaborators using bag-proportion compatibility and class-specific coverage and consistency.
mFrtGjGu8e.problem: Aggregate label supervision makes heterogeneous clients difficult to characterize and combine in federated learning from label proportions.
mFrtGjGu8e.method: FedC² builds target-specific collaboration weights from the geometry of observed bag proportions, then conservatively adjusts class-wise contributions using coverage and local proportion consistency.
mFrtGjGu8e.key_idea: Use bag-proportion geometry to select compatible clients before refining their contributions separately for each class.
mFrtGjGu8e.evidence: The paper gives class-specific aggregation-error bounds and experiments across four benchmarks and three client-heterogeneity levels.
mFrtGjGu8e.claimed_gains: FedC² achieves the best accuracy in 10 of 12 settings.
mFrtGjGu8e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find heterogeneous proportion-supervised collaboration well motivated and the compatibility-based design intuitive.
mFrtGjGu8e.main_concern: The theoretical improvement conditions depend on unobserved relationships that the experiments do not verify.

yN13EWISdv.one_liner: SkillZip Pro jointly compresses agent skill content and file-loading structure while auditing routes and interfaces.
yN13EWISdv.problem: Compressing skill directories as flat prompts can increase loaded context or make required subskills inaccessible.
yN13EWISdv.method: The compiler shares instructions within relevant branches, removes obligations supplied by declared context, and defers guarded sections. Typed removal evidence and an independent emitted-file audit check routing, interfaces, and standalone entries.
yN13EWISdv.key_idea: Compress instructions together with their loading graph, using explicit removal evidence and final-file audits to preserve declared execution routes.
yN13EWISdv.evidence: Evaluation covers three task suites, one-shot and continual schedules, and a production moderation service.
yN13EWISdv.claimed_gains: The abstract reports 19.7% shipped-token and 14.3% mean-run-token savings under a five-point quality margin, plus 38.1% skill-token and 10.4% end-to-end runtime-token savings in production.
yN13EWISdv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard execution-aware skill compression as a practical problem and appreciate modeling loading costs and entry-point validity.
yN13EWISdv.main_concern: The quality-preservation claim depends on a permissive non-inferiority margin despite measurable production accuracy losses.

KsxXQlzWhs.one_liner: GalerkinFlow learns flow matching over spline coefficients and decodes generated time series onto a grid once.
KsxXQlzWhs.problem: Grid-based functional generators repeatedly update every sample point even when a signal admits a compact smooth representation.
KsxXQlzWhs.method: Ridge fitting projects time-series windows into cubic B-spline coefficients, and a Transformer learns their joint distribution through flow matching. A linear decoder maps the final coefficients onto the requested grid.
KsxXQlzWhs.key_idea: Run the entire generative flow in spline-coefficient space and apply the linear grid decoder only after sampling.
KsxXQlzWhs.evidence: Wasserstein error analysis separates basis and training errors, while experiments compare five trained generators per method on six regular benchmarks.
KsxXQlzWhs.claimed_gains: A complete training update is 4.1 to 9.0 times cheaper than Spectral Mean Flow.
KsxXQlzWhs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical coefficient-space formulation and its accompanying error decomposition.
KsxXQlzWhs.main_concern: Reviewers find the empirical superiority claims insufficiently supported by the baseline coverage and uncertainty analysis.

iZ46LMoxj9.one_liner: PTTS jointly plans distinct reasoning outlines before frozen executors expand them into parallel solutions.
iZ46LMoxj9.problem: Independent repeated sampling can waste inference compute on redundant reasoning paths.
iZ46LMoxj9.method: PTTS-ZS jointly prompts solution outlines in one autoregressive pass, while PTTS-RL trains a planner against pass@k rewards using truncated execution rollouts. Both condition fixed reasoning executors on the resulting outlines.
iZ46LMoxj9.key_idea: Coordinate branch outlines through a joint planner policy before executing each reasoning path with a frozen model.
iZ46LMoxj9.evidence: A stylized theoretical analysis studies complementary-mode coverage, and experiments use five mathematical reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3-1.7B and 4B.
iZ46LMoxj9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple planner-executor design and reported pass@k improvements across mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
iZ46LMoxj9.main_concern: The efficiency comparisons do not adequately account for planner overhead in matched-compute evaluation.

2itR9JhMnz.one_liner: Aggregating conversational agreement probes reveals population-level relationships between LLM internal activations and expressed agreement.
2itR9JhMnz.problem: Agreement representations vary substantially across individual conversations and do not reliably track expressed agreement turn by turn.
2itR9JhMnz.method: The study learns a linear agreement probe from activations and pools agreement across conversations. It fits external agreement with a first-order Markov model and relates pooled internal and external agreement through a power-law mapping.
2itR9JhMnz.key_idea: Aggregate activation-based agreement scores across conversations before modeling their relationship to observable agreement dynamics.
2itR9JhMnz.evidence: Multi-turn conversations between two LLMs across several models and datasets compare internal projections, expressed agreement, and timing after stance changes.
2itR9JhMnz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value studying conversational agreement jointly through internal representations and observable behavior.
2itR9JhMnz.main_concern: Fitting pooled agreement curves does not establish that the underlying conversational process is first-order Markovian.

6NAysfxIJ4.one_liner: Matched expert-budget comparisons test whether dynamic MoE skipping improves on simply reducing the static expert count.
6NAysfxIJ4.problem: Different calibration regimes and effective expert counts confound comparisons of dynamic expert-skipping methods.
6NAysfxIJ4.method: The study organizes four dynamic methods into a taxonomy and compares them with uniform static expert-count reduction at measured expert-compute budgets, including modality-aware static controls.
6NAysfxIJ4.key_idea: Match measured active-expert budgets across dynamic skipping and static routing before comparing model quality.
6NAysfxIJ4.evidence: Experiments cover text-only Gemma4-26B-A4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, multimodal Qwen3-VL, and varied calibration settings and compute budgets.
6NAysfxIJ4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled negative result and the distinction between calibrated and measured expert usage.
6NAysfxIJ4.main_concern: Expert-count comparisons lack direct throughput or runtime measurements needed to establish practical efficiency trade-offs.

zYJDQQit9k.one_liner: NavHarness connects adaptive navigation goals, observation-based completion checks, and goal-triggered memory compression.
zYJDQQit9k.problem: Locally plausible actions can deviate from long-horizon route instructions while growing interaction histories increase inference costs.
zYJDQQit9k.method: A Goal Agent proposes adaptive goals for a Visuomotor Agent, and a Verify Agent checks completion using goal-specific questions. Confirmed completion triggers a Memory Agent to compress the corresponding multimodal history.
zYJDQQit9k.key_idea: Use verified subgoal completion as the boundary for compressing navigation history while preserving unresolved execution context.
zYJDQQit9k.evidence: Evaluation covers R2R-CE, RxR-CE, multiple model backbones, and real-world quadruped navigation.
zYJDQQit9k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the navigation gains and the practical connection between adaptive goals, completion verification, and memory management.
zYJDQQit9k.main_concern: Missing independent ablations of goal generation and verification prevent attribution of gains to the proposed component coupling.

qZUlpvfhDd.one_liner: ProFiNER expands entity candidates, calibrates boundaries and types, and resolves structural conflicts through global inference.
qZUlpvfhDd.problem: Direct zero-shot NER prompting misses entities and produces boundary errors, type confusion, and incompatible predictions.
qZUlpvfhDd.method: ProFiNER combines mention mining, type-wise questions, and iterative sampling to collect candidates, then refines uncertain spans and calibrates types with normalized scores and pairwise comparisons. A conflict graph supports evidence-based adjudication and global selection.
qZUlpvfhDd.key_idea: Build a high-recall candidate pool, calibrate labels including non-entity, and jointly select structurally compatible entities through a conflict graph.
qZUlpvfhDd.evidence: Experiments compare multiple language-model backbones on four NER benchmarks and ablate calibration and conflict-aware inference.
qZUlpvfhDd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that ProFiNER improves entity recognition across multiple benchmarks and model backbones.
qZUlpvfhDd.main_concern: Missing latency, token-cost, and compute-matched baseline comparisons leave the value of the substantial inference overhead unclear.

XLQLkrzbtZ.one_liner: TACO tracks black-box agent rollouts through configuration fields and accelerates reinforcement learning with approximate trajectory packing.
XLQLkrzbtZ.problem: Existing RL runtimes often require relocating agent loops, complicating training of deployed services with fixed execution environments.
XLQLkrzbtZ.method: TACO carries worker identifiers through an unchanged model configuration field to recover rollout identity without editing agent source. It packs near-matching contexts using bounded token edit distance and overlaps rollouts with training while draining tasks before synchronization.
XLQLkrzbtZ.key_idea: Track rollouts through pass-through configuration identifiers, reuse near-matching trajectory contexts, and drain active tasks before synchronizing model weights.
XLQLkrzbtZ.evidence: Experiments integrate a ReTool-style math agent, a TritonForge-style kernel agent, and the long-running Rust service ZeroClaw.
XLQLkrzbtZ.claimed_gains: Integration requires 122–334 adapter-code lines; packing reduces processed tokens by 3.0× and packing with asynchrony yields a 2.51× end-to-end speedup on the multi-turn math agent.
XLQLkrzbtZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value training existing agent services without source changes and the demonstrations across three different agents.
XLQLkrzbtZ.main_concern: Insufficient comparison with closely related non-intrusive agent-training frameworks leaves the technical contribution unclear.

jH6jzA76DF.one_liner: GEM3D pretrains amodal geometry through reconstruction and rendering, then distills it into single-view robotic policies.
jH6jzA76DF.problem: Robotic policies struggle with unseen camera views, incomplete geometry, and transferring pretrained 3D knowledge into single-view control.
jH6jzA76DF.method: GEM3D learns amodal representations from single-view RGB-D using point-cloud reconstruction and Gaussian-splatting novel-view consistency during pretraining. Multi-step distillation transfers those representations into a single-view visuomotor policy.
jH6jzA76DF.key_idea: Combine point-cloud and novel-view rendering supervision, then align features across steps to transfer geometric representations into a deployable policy.
jH6jzA76DF.evidence: Experiments test zero-shot generalization to unseen camera poses across 12 RLBench tasks and three real-world manipulation tasks.
jH6jzA76DF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard single-view deployment with viewpoint generalization as practically useful and appreciate simulation and real-robot evaluation.
jH6jzA76DF.main_concern: The experiments do not cleanly isolate the contribution of individual geometric-learning and distillation components.

rO2tmQOXna.one_liner: Layerwise activation analysis links intermediate-layer task readouts to dominant geometric directions in vision-language models.
rO2tmQOXna.problem: The dynamics connecting task-relevant internal representations to model answers remain insufficiently characterized.
rO2tmQOXna.method: The paper analyzes task-relevant directions across inference layers and derives criteria for spectral dominance while accounting for component interactions. It tests readout transfer and uses the readout to rerank visual evidence for retrieval-augmented generation.
rO2tmQOXna.key_idea: Relate a task-relevant activation direction to the leading principal component through spectral-dominance and alignment conditions.
rO2tmQOXna.evidence: Experiments cover five vision-language models, cross-dataset readout transfer, layerwise emergence, theoretical alignment bounds, and visual-evidence reranking.
rO2tmQOXna.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the geometric analysis connecting internal task representations with model decisions.
rO2tmQOXna.main_concern: The experiments need more direct validation that improved intermediate-layer readout reflects the claimed concentration and alignment of task information.

xH8QOtfbz3.one_liner: Masked self-distillation omits loss at epistemic markers to preserve exploration and reflection in reasoning models.
xH8QOtfbz3.problem: A solution-aware teacher can suppress exploratory and reflective tokens when uniform self-distillation transfers its preferences to a student.
xH8QOtfbz3.method: The method identifies a fixed lexicon of epistemic markers and withholds distillation loss at those positions while retaining the objective elsewhere.
xH8QOtfbz3.key_idea: Mask distillation loss on tokens such as 'Wait' and 'perhaps' that a privileged teacher disproportionately discourages.
xH8QOtfbz3.evidence: Competition-mathematics experiments compare OPSD, SFT, and GRPO, with same-prefix diagnostics and matched non-marker masking controls.
xH8QOtfbz3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnosis well motivated and the targeted masking effective at avoiding ordinary self-distillation degradation.
xH8QOtfbz3.main_concern: The fixed lexicon-based intervention offers limited methodological differentiation from prior self-distillation diagnoses and remedies.

UsaOgokV5i.one_liner: EvoCred tests hindsight skills on sibling rollouts before redistributing verifier-defined token credit.
UsaOgokV5i.problem: Skills inferred from completed trajectories can merely reconstruct their source actions rather than supply reliable training credit.
UsaOgokV5i.method: A frozen policy scores fixed target actions under skills from other rollouts of the same task, with admission based on evidence strength and verifier compatibility. A positive bounded transformation redistributes token advantages while preserving signs and total absolute trajectory credit.
UsaOgokV5i.key_idea: Cross-evaluate hindsight skills on sibling trajectories, then gate sign-preserving redistribution within a verifier-fixed credit budget.
UsaOgokV5i.evidence: Experiments use ALFWorld, Knowledge QA, and WebShop with three Qwen backbones and compare GRPO, SEED, and AgentOPSD.
UsaOgokV5i.claimed_gains: EvoCred ranks first on ten of twelve aggregate comparisons and beats GRPO, SEED, and AgentOPSD on all twelve, raising Qwen3-1.7B ALFWorld success from 42.1% to 91.2% and WebShop success from 38.3% to 76.5% over GRPO.
UsaOgokV5i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate identifying source-trajectory reuse as an ambiguity in hindsight-based credit assignment.
UsaOgokV5i.main_concern: The evidence does not establish that correlated sibling trajectories provide reliable, transferable validation of hindsight skills.

w0m2VBI6Wq.one_liner: PACE uses visual history and upcoming actions to allocate context, attention, and denoising computation in video world models.
w0m2VBI6Wq.problem: Repeated diffusion denoising over long visual histories makes interactive world generation slow, while fixed compression can degrade quality.
w0m2VBI6Wq.method: PACE filters historical blocks by visual redundancy and target-view relevance, distributes attention budgets between past and current tokens, and reuses denoising computation using perception and action cues.
w0m2VBI6Wq.key_idea: Combine completed visual evidence with the upcoming action to choose which context, attention interactions, and denoising computations to retain.
w0m2VBI6Wq.evidence: Experiments report latency, memory, quality, and component ablations on HY-WorldPlay, with additional testing on Matrix-Game 3.0.
w0m2VBI6Wq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find action-conditioned computation allocation well motivated and appreciate measured inference-cost reductions.
w0m2VBI6Wq.main_concern: Evaluation on predefined camera trajectories leaves generalization to broader actions and interactions unestablished.

5DMrK9p3HZ.one_liner: Sinkhorn-based conformal calibration builds Wasserstein ambiguity sets for end-to-end distributionally robust decision-focused learning.
5DMrK9p3HZ.problem: Decisions based on point predictions or a single learned distribution remain vulnerable to errors in that distribution.
5DMrK9p3HZ.method: DRDFL learns a conditional distribution and calibrates its Wasserstein ambiguity radius using empirical Sinkhorn nonconformity scores corrected for regularization and sampling error. Gradients through calibration and robust optimization support task-aware end-to-end training.
5DMrK9p3HZ.key_idea: Use corrected Sinkhorn scores to conformally calibrate distributional ambiguity sets and differentiate through the resulting robust decision problem.
5DMrK9p3HZ.evidence: The paper derives finite-sample marginal coverage and conditional-loss bounds under stated assumptions and evaluates portfolio allocation against two-stage and stochastic DFL baselines.
5DMrK9p3HZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize Sinkhorn-based distributional calibration as a useful connection between statistical coverage and robust decision training.
5DMrK9p3HZ.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the benefit of conformal radius selection over closely related robust decision-learning approaches.

mRLcwDPSTy.one_liner: Chameleon selects numerical formats per weight channel, activation layer, and optional timestep bucket while keeping bit width fixed.
mRLcwDPSTy.problem: A fixed quantization format cannot accommodate tensor distributions that differ across diffusion layers, channels, and timesteps.
mRLcwDPSTy.method: Chameleon chooses from integer, floating-point, and microscaling formats using tensor statistics and diffusion signal-to-noise information. It stores format choices for inference and can jointly search group sizes and formats.
mRLcwDPSTy.key_idea: Treat the numerical format as a discrete quantization variable selected by tensor distribution at fixed bit width.
mRLcwDPSTy.evidence: Experiments evaluate quantized image generation across three diffusion architectures, including SDXL-Turbo and PixArt-α, using fake quantization.
mRLcwDPSTy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find distribution-dependent format selection useful and recognize improvements across diffusion architectures.
mRLcwDPSTy.main_concern: The paper does not sufficiently distinguish its format-selection strategy from prior quantization methods through recent baseline comparisons.

xOiefUOfcn.one_liner: CLEAR-ID uses multimodal-language-model priors and constrained residual modulation to distinguish document tampering from benign visual disturbances.
xOiefUOfcn.problem: Glare, mosaics, stains, and other benign disturbances resemble tampering artifacts and can mislead ID-document forensic systems.
xOiefUOfcn.method: CLEAR-ID uses MLLM priors to represent forensic evidence as disturbance-oriented or tampering-oriented cues, then limits modulation through a low-rank residual space. DISTURBID-180k supplies separate disturbance and tampering annotations.
xOiefUOfcn.key_idea: Separate disturbance and tampering evidence using semantic priors, then constrain evidence modulation within a low-rank residual space.
xOiefUOfcn.evidence: Experiments use DISTURBID-180k with 42 disturbance types, severity and localization annotations, component ablations, and cross-domain tests.
xOiefUOfcn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that disturbance-induced forensic errors are practically relevant and that the dataset provides useful evaluation coverage.
xOiefUOfcn.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the contribution of MLLM semantics or establish the need for a large model over simpler disturbance predictors.

70cKe1Whfr.one_liner: Models causal decoder caches as one-way communication messages to derive information-theoretic lower bounds relating retained memory to recall error.
70cKe1Whfr.problem: Long-context cache compression methods rely on heuristics without characterizing how much persistent input-dependent state a causal decoder fundamentally needs for target recall accuracy.
70cKe1Whfr.method: Counting all input-dependent information, selection indices, and reusable randomness retained before query arrival, the paper derives communication-theoretic memory lower bounds and asymptotically matching coding schemes under uniform and non-uniform query distributions. It compares compressed summary encodings against exact record-subset storage and separates retained post-compression memory from peak and physical cache storage.
70cKe1Whfr.key_idea: Cast a causal decoder's persistent state as a one-way communication message compressed before query arrival to bound retained bits against target recall error.
70cKe1Whfr.evidence: Supported by communication-complexity lower bounds and coding constructions alongside experiments on finite-state models and Transformer KV caches across formal language recognition, synthetic associative recall, and string retrieval.
70cKe1Whfr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value framing persistent decoder caches as one-way communication messages to establish formal memory-accuracy bounds supported by finite-state and Transformer cache experiments.
70cKe1Whfr.main_concern: Reviewers question whether idealized streaming assumptions—unbounded per-step compute, independent uniform records, data-independent queries, and free shared randomness—reflect real LLMs, alongside dense terminology and overlap with prior bounds.

3XeSf6QUMN.one_liner: Collapses equivalent metabolic reaction edits into mechanistic cores and optimizes exploration over the quotient space via kernelized Rényi estimation.
3XeSf6QUMN.problem: In genome-scale metabolic model repair, many distinct reaction-edit sets correspond to the same biological mechanism under functional verification, so output-space diversity fails to produce diverse scientific hypotheses.
3XeSf6QUMN.method: QuotientPO collapses verifier-equivalent reaction repairs via greedy deletion into canonical mechanistic cores and optimizes policy exploration directly over the resulting quotient space. To provide informative exploration signals under finite rollouts, it uses a kernelized Rényi estimator that measures graded crowding among distinct repair cores beyond exact-match counts.
3XeSf6QUMN.key_idea: Collapse verifier-equivalent reaction edits into canonical mechanistic cores and optimize exploration over the induced quotient space using a kernelized Rényi crowding estimator.
3XeSf6QUMN.evidence: Evaluated on 2,212 held-out genome-scale metabolic models alongside component ablations against exploration baselines.
3XeSf6QUMN.claimed_gains: On 2,212 held-out GEMs, QuotientPO improves Success@32 from 17.93% to 20.10% (+12.1% relative) while consistently increasing distinct successful-core discovery under the same sampling budget.
3XeSf6QUMN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that defining diversity over verifier-induced equivalence classes rather than raw reaction edits is well motivated for metabolic model repair and yields consistent metric improvements over baselines.
3XeSf6QUMN.main_concern: Reviewers question the greedy deletion canonicalization, independent Bernoulli edit modeling that ignores edit dependencies, and limited methodological originality relative to prior RL and LLM equivalence-class diversity work.

okgYH8LOor.one_liner: Combines on-policy background planning over imagined rollouts with annealed curiosity rewards and compares against test-time planning in high-dimensional control.
okgYH8LOor.problem: Test-time planning with learned world models in high-dimensional continuous control exhibits mixed empirical gains and suffers from actor-planner divergence.
okgYH8LOor.method: The authors combine on-policy background planning on imagined world-model rollouts using Gaussian stochastic latents with an annealed curiosity intrinsic reward. They also conduct controlled hyperparameter sweeps across planner and action-imitation temperatures over 132 task-configuration cells to compare background planning, test-time planning, and planner-action imitation.
okgYH8LOor.key_idea: Replace default test-time planning with on-policy background planning on imagined rollouts augmented by an annealed curiosity intrinsic reward.
okgYH8LOor.evidence: Evaluated on DeepMind Control Suite (DMC) and HumanoidBench under matched environment interaction budgets with five-seed runs, ablations, and hyperparameter sweeps across 132 task-configuration cells.
okgYH8LOor.claimed_gains: Improves mean performance over the strongest prior high-dimensional control method by 8.57% on DMC and 9.99% on HumanoidBench under a matched environment interaction budget.
okgYH8LOor.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the empirical comparisons and ablations offer practical insight into when curiosity exploration, latent choices, test-time planning, and planner imitation help or fail in high-dimensional model-based RL.
okgYH8LOor.main_concern: Reviewers note unclear positioning between an empirical study and a method contribution, average gains disproportionately driven by two tasks out of eleven, missing exploration baselines, and discrepancies between equations and code.

claOC2YjNC.one_liner: Trains a contrastive GAT over class-attribute pairs to select diverse or discriminative attributes for calibrated test-time prompt tuning.
claOC2YjNC.problem: Entropy-minimizing test-time prompt tuning for vision-language models induces overconfidence and degrades calibration, while existing attribute-initialized methods treat LLM-generated attributes independently and ignore intra-class redundancy and inter-class ambiguity.
claOC2YjNC.method: ARGTCA represents class-attribute pairs as nodes in a Symbolic Attribute Graph linking within-class siblings and identical attributes across classes, then trains a graph attention network (GAT) with supervised contrastive learning so distance from the class centroid reflects attribute genericity. Two offline selection strategies—ARGTCA-Div for diverse attributes and ARGTCA-Disc for discriminative ones—choose attributes to initialize CLIP test-time prompts.
claOC2YjNC.key_idea: Embed class-attribute pairs via supervised contrastive learning on a relational graph of intra-class and cross-class attribute links to select diverse or discriminative prompt initializations.
claOC2YjNC.evidence: Evaluated across ten visual-classification benchmarks (including Caltech101, ImageNet, ImageNet-R, and EuroSAT) using CLIP ViT-B/16 and ResNet-50 backbones with graph and selection ablations.
claOC2YjNC.claimed_gains: Increases attribute-genericity correlation with distance from the class centroid on Caltech101 from Spearman rho -0.130 to +0.588, and ARGTCA-Div reduces average ECE across ten benchmarks on CLIP ViT-B/16 to 4.46, a reduction of up to 58.3%.
claOC2YjNC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling intra-class and inter-class attribute relations via an offline graph is intuitive, adds no extra test-time inference cost beyond TCA, and lowers average ECE on both CLIP backbones.
claOC2YjNC.main_concern: Reviewers highlight uneven dataset-level calibration and accuracy trade-offs (such as degraded ECE and accuracy on EuroSAT), baseline comparability questions on ImageNet, and incremental design over TCA.

wgN0a1GLmM.one_liner: Optimizes RAG retrievers and rerankers using verifier-labeled document progression trajectories converted into query-level preferences without gold evidence.
wgN0a1GLmM.problem: Optimizing multi-stage RAG cascades from final answers alone faces expensive gold supporting-document annotation and credit ambiguity about which stage lost supporting evidence.
wgN0a1GLmM.method: StageRAG logs candidate document progression across retrieval and reranking stages, applies an answer-and-citation verifier to determine answer correctness and support attribution, and converts the resulting trajectory states into per-query capped preference pairs to train both retriever and reranker. The authors also formalize a pipeline-aware ranking objective and bound regret for a pointwise rule under bounded evidence interactions.
wgN0a1GLmM.key_idea: Convert verifier-attributed document progression states across logged retrieval and reranking stages into capped query-level preference pairs to jointly optimize retriever and reranker without gold evidence labels.
wgN0a1GLmM.evidence: Evaluated on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and TAT-QA with MiniLM and Qwen3 backbones alongside theoretical regret bounds, stage ablations, and cascade evidence-transition diagnostics.
wgN0a1GLmM.claimed_gains: On HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and TAT-QA, StageRAG improves F1 over the strongest compared answer-supervised baseline by 5.65, 12.44, and 6.43 points, respectively.
wgN0a1GLmM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing both retrieval stages from question-answer supervision without adding inference-time modules is practically useful and yields consistent gains over matched baselines across three datasets.
wgN0a1GLmM.main_concern: Reviewers find the multi-state preference ordering heuristic and note that full-state supervision improves HotpotQA F1 by only 0.57 points over simpler binary supervision.

2A2H1qVcPt.one_liner: Softly routes joints into six dynamic body parts processed by a spatial state-space model and causal coordination rectifier.
2A2H1qVcPt.problem: Holistic text-to-motion models miss fine-grained local joint articulations, whereas fixed body-part partitions fail to capture motion-dependent whole-body coordination.
2A2H1qVcPt.method: DyCoPart encodes joint-level kinematic dependencies with a lightweight graph module, softly routes joints into six dynamic parts under anatomical-prior guidance, and models whole-body spatial structure via a shared spatial Part State Space Model. A directed causal coordination rectifier then propagates temporally causal cross-part messages across dynamic-part slots to maintain whole-body coherence.
2A2H1qVcPt.key_idea: Softly route joints into anatomically guided dynamic body-part tokens and propagate temporally causal cross-part messages via a spatial part state-space model and coordination rectifier.
2A2H1qVcPt.evidence: Evaluated on HumanML3D and KIT-ML text-to-motion benchmarks with same-backbone ablations comparing fixed partitions, dynamic part learning, and causal rectification across fidelity, coordination, and physical metrics.
2A2H1qVcPt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that anatomically guided dynamic soft routing is sensible and that same-backbone ablations usefully demonstrate how soft part routing avoids the coordination drop of hard fixed partitions.
2A2H1qVcPt.main_concern: Reviewers note a complex multi-module architecture whose individual mechanisms (dynamic vs. time-invariant soft routing and causal rectification) are insufficiently isolated, alongside missing recent joint-level and part-based baselines.

1XsY1HcKm7.one_liner: Joint pretraining with channel regularization and interpolation decoding unifies visual alignment, reconstruction, and generation.
1XsY1HcKm7.problem: Separate visual representation paradigms specialize semantics, multimodal alignment, and tokenization instead of supporting open-ended tasks together.
1XsY1HcKm7.method: GAMUT uses a three-stage joint pretraining pipeline to avoid prolonged multi-objective training. Latent channel regularization prevents energy concentration and collapse, while latent interpolation decoding adapts the representation for generation.
1XsY1HcKm7.key_idea: Stabilize a shared high-dimensional visual latent through channel-energy regularization and interpolation-based decoding during joint pretraining.
1XsY1HcKm7.evidence: Experiments assess image-text alignment, retrieval, classification, reconstruction, segmentation, and class-conditional ImageNet generation.
1XsY1HcKm7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value retaining semantic and visual detail in one representation and the direct evidence that channel regularization reverses collapse.
1XsY1HcKm7.main_concern: Generation tests only ImageNet 256×256 class-conditional synthesis and omit downstream MLLM/VQA evaluation, limiting the unified-use claim.

LwKD10S3DY.one_liner: TSFT allocates fine-tuning budgets across task regions using performance prediction and dynamic programming.
LwKD10S3DY.problem: Contextual RL lacks a sample-efficient way to decide how much fine-tuning each task region should receive from a pretrained policy under a fixed budget.
LwKD10S3DY.method: TSFT pretrains one policy and fine-tunes multiple task-specialist policies while formulating budget allocation as a Markov decision process. A parametric model predicts fine-tuning performance, dynamic programming computes allocations, and a receding-horizon variant reduces planning cost.
LwKD10S3DY.key_idea: Predict heterogeneous fine-tuning returns by task region, then use dynamic programming to allocate a shared budget across specialized policies.
LwKD10S3DY.evidence: Experiments span combinatorial optimization, continuous control, and LLM fine-tuning, measuring task coverage against baselines and an oracle.
LwKD10S3DY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the allocation problem is well motivated and that the broad experiments and mathematical formulation support the framework.
LwKD10S3DY.main_concern: The allocation baselines are insufficiently competitive and controlled, leaving the value of exact optimization and online replanning unclear.

JtVKO5mc0B.one_liner: UOT-Unlearn redistributes a forgotten class's probability mass across remaining classes in one-step generators.
JtVKO5mc0B.problem: Existing diffusion unlearning methods rely on multi-step denoising and often collapse removed probability mass into noise, making them unsuitable for one-step generators.
JtVKO5mc0B.method: UOT-Unlearn formulates class unlearning with unbalanced optimal transport, combining a forget cost with an f-divergence penalty and relaxed marginal constraints. It transfers the target class's probability mass to remaining classes while keeping generations near the data support.
JtVKO5mc0B.key_idea: Use relaxed unbalanced transport to redistribute forgotten-class mass instead of mapping forgotten inputs to Gaussian noise.
JtVKO5mc0B.evidence: Experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-256 evaluate unlearning and generation quality, with an extension to one-step text-to-image generation.
JtVKO5mc0B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that one-step generator unlearning is useful and that the method reports favorable forgetting and generation-quality trade-offs.
JtVKO5mc0B.main_concern: The comparisons do not isolate the unbalanced optimal transport formulation from the forgetting cost and class-redirection strategy.

okoFMGukdF.one_liner: Decouples RLVR rollout and update horizons by continuing truncated responses under a frozen policy solely for outcome verification.
okoFMGukdF.problem: Long RLVR horizons delay answers and waste compute, while short horizons mislabel truncated prefixes that could still succeed.
okoFMGukdF.method: Natural-Continuation Boundary Return (NCBR) lets a frozen continuation policy complete truncated rollouts for outcome verification while applying policy-gradient updates only to the original short-horizon tokens.
okoFMGukdF.key_idea: Continues truncated rollouts with a frozen policy to estimate continuation value while updating only the original short-horizon actor tokens.
okoFMGukdF.evidence: Evaluated across three mathematical reasoning benchmarks with DAPO and GRPO.
okoFMGukdF.claimed_gains: With DAPO, achieves a 57.4% relative improvement in AIME'24 Pass@1 over the 2K DAPO baseline and outperforms Full 8K training with 54.5% fewer GPU-hours.
okoFMGukdF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating observation and update horizons is well-motivated and yields strong cost-performance trade-offs.
okoFMGukdF.main_concern: Reviewers point out that efficiency is compared at fixed update steps rather than equal compute, long-horizon baselines appear untuned/diverged, and code is missing.

aO1fGNZQyL.one_liner: Lightweight multimodal safety detector for frozen MLLMs using sparse selection and utility-guided fusion of internal representations.
aO1fGNZQyL.problem: Realigning entire MLLMs for safety across model families and taxonomies is computationally expensive.
aO1fGNZQyL.method: SEFIR summarizes intermediate representations from the visual encoder, projector, and language model, selects safety-discriminative coordinates via sparse diagnostic selection, and fuses them by held-out component utility into a small classifier.
aO1fGNZQyL.key_idea: Extracts, sparsely selects, and utility-weights intermediate representations across frozen vision, projector, and LLM components for safety classification.
aO1fGNZQyL.evidence: Evaluated across seven multimodal safety datasets and four MLLM backbones.
aO1fGNZQyL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that detecting safety from frozen internal MLLM representations avoids costly backbone retraining and is broadly evaluated.
aO1fGNZQyL.main_concern: Reviewers note that main results compare in-domain trained SEFIR against zero-shot baselines, cross-domain transfer drops, and gains over prior sparse probes (SIREN) are unclear.

wzU6tnYYsI.one_liner: Systematically externalizes evidence state, search, and termination from medical LLMs into an executable diagnostic-program harness.
wzU6tnYYsI.problem: LLM medical agents typically keep sequential diagnostic control inside the model, conflating procedural knowledge access with reliable execution.
wzU6tnYYsI.method: They decompose interactive diagnosis into evidence-state maintenance, search strategy, and terminal control, progressively moving them into a rule-bound runtime executing compiled clinical programs while restricting the LLM to grounding and residual cases.
wzU6tnYYsI.key_idea: Externalizes state tracking, search, and termination into a rule-bound runtime executing compiled clinical programs, leaving grounding to the LLM.
wzU6tnYYsI.evidence: Evaluated across three interactive medical diagnosis benchmarks and multiple model scales against prompting with the same diagnostic programs.
wzU6tnYYsI.claimed_gains: Across three interactive medical benchmarks, the full harness improves diagnostic correctness by 24.7-49.7 percentage points over prompting with the same programs.
wzU6tnYYsI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value systematically isolating model versus harness responsibilities in interactive medical diagnosis and demonstrating large gains from executable runtime control.
wzU6tnYYsI.main_concern: Externalizing state and workflow control has limited novelty over clinical decision-support systems, components are externalized in a fixed order without interaction ablations, and handcrafted utilities lack justification.

g7K1nTB5yL.one_liner: Proposes RAMP, adding dance-rhythm control to pretrained text-to-music models via global-to-local rhythm routing and teacher regularization.
g7K1nTB5yL.problem: Dance-to-music generation needs fine-grained motion-rhythm synchronization without losing semantic text and lyric controllability.
g7K1nTB5yL.method: RAMP introduces the Style-Adaptive Rhythm Tokenizer (SART) for global style and local motion routing over rhythm-biased experts, trained via staged adaptation with text-only velocity regularization toward a Stage-1 teacher.
g7K1nTB5yL.key_idea: Routes dance motion through global style and local residual rhythm experts while regularizing text-only predictions toward a Stage-1 teacher.
g7K1nTB5yL.evidence: Constructed Dance100K and a 3K evaluation benchmark, measuring rhythmic alignment, semantic consistency, and perceptual quality.
g7K1nTB5yL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the Style-Adaptive Rhythm Tokenizer's hierarchical global-to-local rhythm routing and teacher-regularized adaptation for dance-to-music generation.
g7K1nTB5yL.main_concern: Key architectural choices in SART (e.g., 4 hardcoded experts, arbitrary token counts) lack ablation or justification, and evaluation is restricted to 5-second clips without verified song-disjoint splits.

nCeJglsRSA.one_liner: Introduces StreamAct-Bench and StreamAct-SFT to evaluate and train strict-causal online state, readiness, and action in streaming video LLMs.
nCeJglsRSA.problem: Evaluating streaming video models at evaluator-chosen moments masks their inability to autonomously track state, judge readiness, and time responses.
nCeJglsRSA.method: StreamAct-Bench evaluates 5,436 replayable trajectories over state, readiness, action, and answer under strict causality; StreamAct-SFT supervises these intermediate trajectory signals.
nCeJglsRSA.key_idea: Evaluates strict-causal online trajectories over explicit state, readiness, action, and answer rather than evaluator-timed Q&A.
nCeJglsRSA.evidence: Evaluated Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B and other models on 5,436 trajectories in StreamAct-Bench and 5,195 paired OVO-Bench/StreamingBench items.
nCeJglsRSA.claimed_gains: Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B achieves 45.02% target-time answer accuracy on StreamAct-Bench, yet only 6.68% of its first self-timed responses are timely and correct.
nCeJglsRSA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the importance of distinguishing causal answerability from autonomous streaming behavior via paired evaluator-timed versus self-timed evaluation.
nCeJglsRSA.main_concern: StreamAct-SFT yields only modest valid-first-response gains (6.68% to 11.11%) while raising premature responses, tests only one backbone, and constrains models to a 20-word state interface.

aSzoQyDp60.one_liner: Proposes COMPASS, gating adversarial supervision by clean sample reliability and recalibrating classifiers for long-tailed adversarial training.
aSzoQyDp60.problem: Long-tailed adversarial training suffers when strong perturbations destabilize unreliable tail samples and classifiers retain head-class prior bias.
aSzoQyDp60.method: COMPASS uses Robust Supervision Recalibration (RSR) to gate adversarial strength by clean-sample reliability and Train-only Classifier Recalibration (TCR) to interpolate with a class-balanced classifier selected on training data.
aSzoQyDp60.key_idea: Gates class-level adversarial supervision by sample-level clean reliability and interpolates the frozen classifier with a train-only balanced head.
aSzoQyDp60.evidence: Evaluated across multiple datasets, architectures, base learners, and attacks including AutoAttack.
aSzoQyDp60.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers appreciate identifying clean-reliability mismatch in long-tailed adversarial training and the complementary RSR and TCR modules tested across datasets and attacks.
aSzoQyDp60.main_concern: Novelty over existing adaptive-perturbation and decoupled long-tailed AT methods is unclear, TCR split details are underspecified, and one reviewer sees no direct evidence that clean-unstable samples cause baseline failures.

rMKGl4z0Ee.one_liner: Proposes Diagno-SV, decoupling perception, reasoning, and knowledge with curriculum DPO to mitigate retrospective forgery in medical VLMs.
rMKGl4z0Ee.problem: Medical VLMs often conflate perception, deduction, and knowledge in chain-of-thought, enabling post-hoc fabrication of visual findings to justify wrong diagnoses.
rMKGl4z0Ee.method: Diagno-SV enforces tri-level CoT decomposition into perception, deduction, and knowledge, and uses a diagnostic module to pinpoint error types and construct curriculum DPO preference pairs.
rMKGl4z0Ee.key_idea: Decomposes medical VLM CoT into perception, deduction, and knowledge steps to build error-localized curriculum DPO pairs.
rMKGl4z0Ee.evidence: Evaluated across six medical VQA benchmarks including MMMU-Med and PMC-VQA, plus GPT-4o forgery-rate analysis.
rMKGl4z0Ee.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling perception, reasoning, and knowledge to diagnose retrospective forgery in medical VLMs is well-motivated and yields strong VQA gains.
rMKGl4z0Ee.main_concern: Potential train-test data leakage on PMC-VQA is not ruled out, GPT-4o is used for both data generation and forgery evaluation, and ablations do not isolate tri-level decomposition from DPO.

aZnBv0O6cy.one_liner: Uses a function-valued order parameter and the replica method to derive asymptotic generalization error under entrywise heavy-tailed data.
aZnBv0O6cy.problem: Rare extreme feature entries in heavy-tailed data retain non-vanishing effects in high dimensions, preventing Gaussian-based asymptotic characterizations of ERM.
aZnBv0O6cy.method: They introduce a function-valued order parameter for the random effective problem per coefficient and apply the replica method to entrywise i.i.d. symmetric alpha-stable linear regression in the proportional limit.
aZnBv0O6cy.key_idea: Reduces high-dimensional heavy-tailed ERM to a 1-D random optimization via a function-valued replica order parameter.
aZnBv0O6cy.evidence: Asymptotic replica derivations of generalization error, universality laws, and Bayes-optimal error, compared with numerical simulations.
aZnBv0O6cy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extending replica-method asymptotic characterization to ERM with entrywise i.i.d. heavy-tailed features beyond Gaussian and elliptical models.
aZnBv0O6cy.main_concern: Technical novelty over prior functional order-parameter methods in statistical physics is unclear, strong i.i.d. assumptions lack misspecification studies, and key definitions are relegated to the appendix.

b4kNmxT254.one_liner: Solves PAC CVaR-constrained RL via a three-phase VaR-grid LP, global model estimation, and feasibility filtering with sample-complexity bounds.
b4kNmxT254.problem: Safety-critical RL requires minimizing expected cost subject to a tail-risk CVaR constraint, which lacks finite-sample PAC guarantees.
b4kNmxT254.method: The authors prove an optimal stochastic Markov policy exists on an augmented state space and propose CVaR-PDS, which solves VaR-indexed linear-constrained subproblems, estimates a global model for evaluation, and applies post-hoc feasibility filtering.
b4kNmxT254.key_idea: Discretizes VaR thresholds into linear-constrained augmented-state RL subproblems and uses a single global model for post-hoc feasibility filtering under relaxed Slater conditions.
b4kNmxT254.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower PAC sample-complexity bounds alongside a small-scale illustrative experiment.
b4kNmxT254.claimed_gains: Establishes an O_tilde(S^2 A H^4 tau / (alpha^2 eps^3) + S A H^5 tau / (alpha^2 eps^4) + H^7 tau / (zeta_xi^2 alpha^2 eps^3)) upper bound and an Omega(S A H^2 / (alpha eps^2)) lower bound.
b4kNmxT254.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the first finite-sample PAC guarantee for CVaR-constrained RL and the careful augmented-state reduction.
b4kNmxT254.main_concern: Reviewers question why the three-phase design is needed instead of single-phase exploration plus relaxed LP planning, and note a large gap between upper and lower bounds.

4qQpN05GkV.one_liner: Anchors amortized KV-cache compaction for procedural skills with a low-weight reconstruction loss during on-policy tool-calling distillation.
4qQpN05GkV.problem: Sequential reconstruction and instruction-following training erases stored tool schemas in compacted KV prefixes, degrading tool-calling accuracy.
4qQpN05GkV.method: ANCHOR trains an amortized KV-cache emitter using on-policy distillation anchored by a low-weight reconstruction objective, and introduces DomainBench with 716 skill-dependent tasks across 100 procedural skills.
4qQpN05GkV.key_idea: Combines on-policy tool-calling distillation with a simultaneous low-weight reconstruction anchor to prevent schema forgetting in compacted KV prefixes.
4qQpN05GkV.evidence: Evaluated on DomainBench (716 tasks, 100 skills) using hierarchical Tool-F1, Schema-F1, and Call-F1 metrics with ablations.
4qQpN05GkV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper identifies a genuine anchoring tension between skill preservation and instruction following, supported by a useful benchmark.
4qQpN05GkV.main_concern: Reviewers note that DomainBench relies on synthetic uniform skill documents and uses unordered set matching that ignores sequential tool-call dependencies.

pIHoiEG2Yi.one_liner: Projects a 4B VLM's dense metric depth predictions into object-aligned continuous geometry tokens for metric spatial reasoning.
pIHoiEG2Yi.problem: Depth-aware VLMs predict depth in parallel with text without grounding language reasoning in recoverable object-level metric geometry.
pIHoiEG2Yi.method: DepthEvidence equips a 4B VLM with a camera-conditioned multi-scale depth decoder and a dense-to-language interface converting predicted depths and features into object-aligned tokens anchored to object IDs. Auxiliary geometric supervision preserves metric recoverability alongside instruction tuning on a new Depth-VQA benchmark.
pIHoiEG2Yi.key_idea: Converts predicted dense metric depth into object-aligned continuous geometry tokens supervised for recoverability during multimodal language reasoning.
pIHoiEG2Yi.evidence: Evaluated on nine dense depth datasets, instance-level depth estimation, general VQA, and the introduced Depth-VQA relative and metric reasoning tracks.
pIHoiEG2Yi.claimed_gains: Achieves 0.7972 average delta_1 across nine datasets (versus 0.6673 for DepthVLM-4B and +0.1033 over DepthLM-12B) and improves metric-constrained reasoning from 76.92% to 85.04% in ablation.
pIHoiEG2Yi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree closing the loop between dense metric depth prediction and object-grounded language reasoning is well-motivated and effective at 4B scale.
pIHoiEG2Yi.main_concern: Reviewers note the nine-dataset depth lead relies on an anomalous SUN RGB-D score for UniDepth V2, ablations show answer-loss-only interface gains are minimal, and Depth-VQA outdoor depth completion lacks validation.

IkeJ3X2aDO.one_liner: Modifies Adam to take momentum-sign directions with normalized gradient magnitudes and finite-time second-moment contraction for noisy RL.
IkeJ3X2aDO.problem: Under noisy, drifting deep RL objectives, Adam's linear momentum shrinks step sizes and its second-moment estimate recovers slowly after gradient bursts.
IkeJ3X2aDO.method: Ano keeps Adam's state tensors and hyperparameters but uses the sign of momentum for coordinate direction paired with the current normalized gradient's magnitude. It also introduces an Active Contraction Accumulator to return the second-moment estimate to post-burst gradient scales in finite time.
IkeJ3X2aDO.key_idea: Uses momentum sign for update direction and normalized current gradient magnitude for step size alongside finite-time second-moment contraction.
IkeJ3X2aDO.evidence: Supported by high-noise signal-alignment theory, SAC gradient stream diagnostics, and 25-seed evaluations across 10 MuJoCo and Atari environments.
