IkeJ3X2aDO.claimed_gains: Roughly triples signal-aligned progress per step in the high-noise limit compared to Adam at fixed learning rate.
IkeJ3X2aDO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the zero-extra-hyperparameter design, clear separation of direction and step size, and 25-seed RL benchmarks.
IkeJ3X2aDO.main_concern: Reviewers question whether fixed-learning-rate comparisons confound step-size scaling, critique the signal-aligned progress definition and non-RL-specific theory, and flag flawed hyperparameter transfer protocols.

IP9k9VdnnS.one_liner: Quantifies image degradations as band-wise frequency energy ratios and decomposes them into spectral tokens for restoration.
IP9k9VdnnS.problem: All-in-one blind image restoration typically models degradations implicitly, struggling under mixed, compound, or unseen degradations.
IP9k9VdnnS.method: DFC computes band-wise residual-to-degraded energy ratios in the frequency domain, decomposes them into spectral tokens, and guides DFC-IR to progressively estimate DFCs and condition multi-scale restoration.
IP9k9VdnnS.key_idea: Represents image degradations explicitly as band-wise residual-to-degraded frequency energy ratio curves decomposed into reusable spectral tokens.
IP9k9VdnnS.evidence: Experiments on standard three- and five-degradation benchmarks, composite, unseen, and real-world degradation datasets.
IP9k9VdnnS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the explicit frequency-ratio representation intuitive and note broad evaluation coverage across standard, composite, and unseen degradations.
IP9k9VdnnS.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations do not cleanly isolate DFC's contribution from parameter increases and supervision changes, and that inference relies on potentially noisy intermediate restorations.

nSuguQG3aG.one_liner: Reconstructs failed coding-agent trajectories into executable surrogate tasks in public repositories to reproduce failure patterns.
nSuguQG3aG.problem: Failed coding-agent trajectories cannot be replayed for evaluation or self-improvement when original private repositories and execution environments are unavailable.
nSuguQG3aG.method: FAIL2TASK extracts evidence-supported failure patterns, selects public repositories, generates runnable tasks, tests, and solutions, and iteratively refines them via execution validation and trajectory alignment.
nSuguQG3aG.key_idea: Synthesizes executable surrogate tasks in public repositories that reproduce a source trajectory's failure mechanism via closed-loop replay alignment.
nSuguQG3aG.evidence: Evaluations on 96 source failures from SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0, measuring replay alignment and downstream harness self-evolution.
nSuguQG3aG.claimed_gains: FAIL2TASK produces accepted tasks for all 96 cases with 80.18% failure-pattern alignment, and harness self-evolution achieves 27.1–31.3% pass rates on SWE-bench (vs. 14.6–20.8% best baseline) and 16.7–20.8% on Terminal-Bench (vs. 4.2–12.5%).
nSuguQG3aG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a practical setting where failure traces exist without repository access and constructs a coherent closed-loop pipeline.
nSuguQG3aG.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about task validity without independent verifier audits, differences in task difficulty across baselines, and high upstream token costs (~17.4M tokens per task).

mg8ETguyGt.one_liner: Trains a response-aware multi-turn safety monitor using earliest harm-enabling turn annotations and multi-turn RL.
mg8ETguyGt.problem: Trace-level safety labels miss the exact turn where multi-turn dialogue accumulates enough information to enable harm, causing premature refusals or late blocks.
mg8ETguyGt.method: The authors define the earliest harm-enabling turn, build the Multi-Turn Intent Dataset (MTID) with adaptive attack rollouts and matched benign hard negatives, and train TurnGate—a response-aware monitor optimized with supervised fine-tuning and multi-turn RL.
mg8ETguyGt.key_idea: Annotates the earliest turn where a candidate response enables harmful action and trains a response-aware monitor with multi-turn RL on MTID.
mg8ETguyGt.evidence: Evaluated on MTID, cross-domain, target-model, and attacker-pipeline shifts, plus closed-loop online adaptive attacks.
mg8ETguyGt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that intervention timing in multi-turn dialogues is a practical safety problem and appreciate the MTID dataset with benign hard negatives and online adaptive tests.
mg8ETguyGt.main_concern: Reviewers question the justification of the earliest-harm-enabling definition, note limited novelty and outdated models, and observe high ASR (>0.60) and missing SFT controls in online tests.

ztlzkA9RvM.one_liner: Pretrains 3D neural physics surrogates on cheap low-fidelity fluid and solid-mechanics simulations before fine-tuning on high-fidelity data.
ztlzkA9RvM.problem: High-fidelity 3D physics simulation labels are expensive, limiting the data available to train neural surrogates.
ztlzkA9RvM.method: Using open-source fluid and solid-mechanics solvers on independent geometries, the authors generate large-scale low-fidelity simulation corpora, pretrain standard 3D surrogate backbones, and fine-tune them on high-fidelity downstream targets.
ztlzkA9RvM.key_idea: Uses cheap open-source low-fidelity solver outputs on independent geometries to pretrain 3D surrogate backbones for data-efficient high-fidelity fine-tuning.
ztlzkA9RvM.evidence: Evaluated across unstructured 3D fluid fields, deformable-body responses, cross-operator transfer, and scaling studies over corpus size, capacity, and condition coverage.
ztlzkA9RvM.claimed_gains: Reduces high-fidelity data requirements by up to 77% at matched accuracy.
ztlzkA9RvM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practically important and appreciate the curated corpora and broad transfer evaluation, including cross-operator and single-condition tests.
ztlzkA9RvM.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty, single-seed reduced-data curves, missing high-fidelity-matched pretraining cost comparisons, and lack of analysis explaining why transfer works.

PlvyTzSqln.one_liner: Embeds visible, content-harmonized watermarks during diffusion generation using a four-stage differentiable renderer.
PlvyTzSqln.problem: Synthetic media needs visible in-content provenance disclosure and attribution that resists removal without degrading image aesthetics.
PlvyTzSqln.method: DiffStamp integrates a differentiable renderer into diffusion inference to jointly optimize stamp placement and image content across locating, blending, filtering, and embossing stages, with an extension that localizes concept-specific stamps via cross-attention maps.
PlvyTzSqln.key_idea: Integrates a four-stage differentiable renderer into diffusion inference to optimize visible watermark placement and appearance on predicted clean images.
PlvyTzSqln.evidence: Experiments on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image-Edit, and HunyuanVideo against watermark removers and regeneration attacks, plus a 108-participant visual-search study.
PlvyTzSqln.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note that coupling a differentiable renderer to diffusion inference is model-agnostic and demonstrated across image, editing, and video models.
PlvyTzSqln.main_concern: Suppressing stamp noticeability conflicts with regulatory requirements for immediate disclosure, and the generation-time overhead lacks clear justification over post-processing.

MkNQtnWiuP.one_liner: Diagnoses recurring self-play failures into a skill-grouped error memory to guide challenger question generation without external data.
MkNQtnWiuP.problem: Unguided self-play methods plateau because difficulty or diversity signals do not target which specific reasoning weaknesses a solver still has.
MkNQtnWiuP.method: DiagEvo uses a diagnostician to contrast agreeing and disagreeing trajectories, logs recurring error causes as Active or Mastered under skill nodes, and guides challenger generation with double-confidence filtering.
MkNQtnWiuP.key_idea: Extracts recurring error causes from self-play trajectory contrasts into an Active/Mastered skill memory that directs challenger question generation.
MkNQtnWiuP.evidence: Evaluations across nine benchmarks on Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and OctoThinker-8B with three runs and component ablations.
MkNQtnWiuP.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-8B, DiagEvo reaches 72.3% mean accuracy across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, 3.9 percentage points above their R-Zero reproduction.
MkNQtnWiuP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the coherent closed-loop failure-diagnosis design, the broad nine-benchmark scope, and the component ablations.
MkNQtnWiuP.main_concern: Diagnosis relies on majority-vote pseudo-labels rather than verified correctness, and baseline comparisons suffer from inherited numbers and unclear compute matching.

fyg41v8ETo.one_liner: Trains LLMs for accuracy first and applies a post-hoc probing confidence threshold to control abstention coverage without abstention training.
fyg41v8ETo.problem: Abstention training improves selective error rates over naive baselines but locks in a fixed coverage rate, and prior evaluations conflate coverage with accuracy.
fyg41v8ETo.method: The authors decompose matched-coverage risk into answering ability and distinguishing ability, finding that abstention training helps mainly by improving answer accuracy. Based on this, TAPS (Train for Accuracy, then Post-hoc Select) performs standard accuracy post-training and refits an off-the-shelf probing confidence estimator for controllable thresholding.
fyg41v8ETo.key_idea: Decomposes matched-coverage abstention risk into answering and distinguishing ability, motivating standard accuracy training followed by refitting a probing-based confidence selector.
fyg41v8ETo.evidence: Evaluated across three LLMs (Qwen3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B) and three factual QA benchmarks against three abstention-training methods.
fyg41v8ETo.claimed_gains: TAPS with a probing-based confidence estimator attains 1.5-9.4 pp lower mean risk than three abstention-training methods at matched coverage.
fyg41v8ETo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matched-coverage risk decomposition into answering and distinguishing ability is a clear and useful evaluation protocol.
fyg41v8ETo.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains over TruthRL average only 1.49 pp, vary inconsistently across models without multi-seed variance, and lack validation-set threshold calibration.

FRp5VHW5K6.one_liner: Trains a perspective-video JEPA with 360-degree panoramic supervision to predict gravity-aligned spherical features out of view.
FRp5VHW5K6.problem: Standard video representations cover only the camera's narrow field of view, whereas panoramic prediction usually requires calibrated poses or pixel synthesis.
FRp5VHW5K6.method: SphereJEPA renders perspective crops from 360-degree videos so a context encoder processes perspective frames while an EMA target encoder processes the panorama, both writing onto gravity-aligned spherical tokens. Unlike standard JEPAs, the predictor is kept at inference to output full-sphere representations in one forward pass without camera parameters.
FRp5VHW5K6.key_idea: Supervises a perspective-video JEPA with unposed 360-degree panoramas on gravity-aligned spherical tokens and retains the predictor at inference for out-of-view features.
FRp5VHW5K6.evidence: Evaluated on scene/orientation identification, prediction-observation agreement, and TAPVid360 point tracking using a 113M-parameter model.
FRp5VHW5K6.claimed_gains: Roughly halves the TAPVid360 mean angular error of every method not trained on the benchmark without using point labels.
FRp5VHW5K6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the problem of learning 360-degree spatial awareness from narrow perspective video using unposed panoramas as free supervision.
FRp5VHW5K6.main_concern: Reviewers argue no downstream task directly validates out-of-view prediction (TAPVid360 relies on visible-region rotation estimation) and ablations do not isolate the out-of-view loss.

L8AfKK2RHl.one_liner: Governs long-horizon autonomous research using an intent-grounded research loop and sealed execution receipts.
L8AfKK2RHl.problem: Decomposing autonomous research into persistent planners and transient executors creates handoff boundaries where execution fidelity degrades and unsupported evidence corrupts scientific state.
L8AfKK2RHl.method: RIGOR pairs an Intent-Grounded Research Loop (IGRL) to govern evidence-to-state updates and termination with Scientific Execution Governance (SEG) to bind experiment briefs, implementations, executions, and sealed evidence receipts.
L8AfKK2RHl.key_idea: Enforces research intent integrity via role-separated planning and execution bound by experiment briefs, mechanical checks, and sealed evidence receipts.
L8AfKK2RHl.evidence: Evaluated through execution-level and long-horizon autonomous research trajectory comparisons against architectural baselines.
L8AfKK2RHl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that intent drift and evidence integrity in autonomous research agents are important problems and find the role separation intuitive.
L8AfKK2RHl.main_concern: Reviewers note heavy acronym density, incomplete isolation of SEG vs. IGRL contributions, high model-call overhead, and discrepancies in the supplied enforcement code.

FehxpIK9Ui.one_liner: Solves inverse problems via projected gradient descent on the explicit hypersphere latent space of a sphere encoder.
FehxpIK9Ui.problem: Latent-space inverse solvers with GAN, VAE, or flow priors rely on implicit valid-code sets and competing regularization penalties to prevent latent drift.
FehxpIK9Ui.method: Walk the Sphere (WTS) performs projected gradient descent on the explicit hyperspherical latent manifold of a sphere encoder using normalization, and WTS+Loop periodically re-encodes the decoded iterate.
FehxpIK9Ui.key_idea: Uses projected gradient descent on a sphere encoder's explicit hypersphere latent space with periodic iterate re-encoding (WTS+Loop) to solve inverse problems.
FehxpIK9Ui.evidence: Evaluated across ImageNet-256, FFHQ-256 restoration tasks, and three InverseBench scientific problems against five budget-matched diffusion solvers.
FehxpIK9Ui.claimed_gains: Ranks first (outright or tied) in 13 of 18 settings against five diffusion solvers, using 300 gradient steps and ~2 seconds per image on FFHQ-256.
FehxpIK9Ui.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree WTS is a simple, fast latent-space inverse solver that achieves competitive quantitative results against diffusion baselines.
FehxpIK9Ui.main_concern: Reviewers note limited task and resolution coverage (e.g., ImageNet tasks beyond super-resolution, higher resolutions), unclear novelty over PULSE and sphere encoders, and no guarantee that hypersphere projection stays on the data manifold.

IwsNfVbGIT.one_liner: Defines a Product-Spherical Shape Dissimilarity measure with intrinsic pre-shape extraction and Procrustes alignment for trajectories.
IwsNfVbGIT.problem: Euclidean scaling and translation quotienting used in classical shape analysis are undefined for trajectories embedded on spheres or product spheres.
IwsNfVbGIT.method: The authors propose the Product-Spherical Shape Dissimilarity (PSSD) measure, algorithms for intrinsic spherical pre-shape extraction and rotation alignment, and a uniformly convergent smoothing estimator for discrete observations.
IwsNfVbGIT.key_idea: Constructs intrinsic product-spherical pre-shapes via spherical scaling and reference-based translation, then aligns rotations to compute a dissimilarity metric.
IwsNfVbGIT.evidence: Theoretical invariance/identifiability and uniform-convergence proofs, plus classification experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets.
IwsNfVbGIT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper presents a well-defined, mathematically grounded geometric framework for comparing non-Euclidean trajectories on product spheres.
IwsNfVbGIT.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient empirical justification for product-sphere representations and invariances on real-world data, unclear novelty over prior spherical shape work, and missing manifold-based baselines.

7ryXeRv81o.one_liner: Uses solved change-point tasks as in-context demonstrations for a pretrained Transformer to adaptively localize new change points.
7ryXeRv81o.problem: Different change mechanisms typically require hand-crafted change-point detectors tailored to each specific type of structural shift.
7ryXeRv81o.method: In-Context Change-Point Localization (ICCP) prompts a pretrained Transformer with previously solved change-point sequences to localize change points in new sequences without parameter updates, analyzed theoretically via Bayesian approximation and finite-sample error bounds.
7ryXeRv81o.key_idea: Adapts a pretrained Transformer to new change-point mechanisms purely through in-context demonstrations of solved tasks, framed as Bayesian mechanism identification.
7ryXeRv81o.evidence: Finite-sample localization bounds and relative consistency proofs, plus synthetic Gaussian simulations across change mechanisms.
7ryXeRv81o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear problem formulation connecting in-context learning to Bayesian change-point mechanism identification.
7ryXeRv81o.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the exclusive reliance on synthetic Gaussian data (no public real-world benchmarks), missing classical/deep change-point baselines, and small localization gains from context.

AtkEsqBxfY.one_liner: Builds a cue-fact bipartite cognitive map traversed by Personalized PageRank and a schema layer for append-only agent memory.
AtkEsqBxfY.problem: Graph-based LLM agent memories struggle to achieve both semantic explicitness and broad implicit relational coverage while supporting updates without corrupting stored facts.
AtkEsqBxfY.method: CorMem organizes append-only facts in a cue-fact bipartite cognitive map where shared cues induce latent multi-hop relations traversed by query-conditioned Personalized PageRank (PPR). A separate hierarchical schema layer forms semantic gists to apply updates, corrections, and forgetting constraints at answer time without rewriting raw facts.
AtkEsqBxfY.key_idea: Inducing latent relations via shared-cue paths in a bipartite cue-fact graph traversed by Personalized PageRank alongside a non-destructive schema layer.
AtkEsqBxfY.evidence: Experiments on LoCoMo and PersonaMem-v2 across three LLM backbones compared against HippoRAG 2 with bootstrap confidence intervals.
AtkEsqBxfY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CorMem is clearly written and improves gold-session retrieval over HippoRAG 2 across tested backbones.
AtkEsqBxfY.main_concern: Reviewers note modest conceptual novelty over prior graph memory systems like AriGraph, confounded structural ablations, and small answer-quality gains despite higher retrieval recall.

EEaBcmi2xF.one_liner: Mitigates VLM continual-learning forgetting by gating drifting pretrained foundation skills and co-evolving them with verifier-guided supervision.
EEaBcmi2xF.problem: Continual post-training of vision-language models causes catastrophic forgetting not only of past tasks but also of reusable pretrained foundation capabilities.
EEaBcmi2xF.method: SCALE treats a pretrained VLM as a repertoire of foundation skills while adapting to downstream tasks via SFT. It uses drift-aware gates and a dynamically allocated maintenance budget to select drifting foundation skills and co-evolve them using verifier-guided behavioral supervision without constraining current-task updates.
EEaBcmi2xF.key_idea: Allocating a dynamic maintenance budget via drift-aware gates to co-evolve pretrained foundation skills alongside downstream SFT.
EEaBcmi2xF.evidence: Evaluated on continual VLM benchmarks under SS and PS settings on one VLM backbone, with generation-policy and budget analyses.
EEaBcmi2xF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting continual-learning preservation toward reusable pretrained foundation capabilities is a meaningful and well-explained perspective.
EEaBcmi2xF.main_concern: Reviewers find key components (drift-aware selection, budget allocation, gradient projection) insufficiently ablated, and question whether selected task categories with near-zero initial scores truly represent pretrained foundation skills.

iLriQtxnAA.one_liner: Unifies small molecules, peptides, proteins, DNA, and RNA into one atom-level autoregressive Transformer via reversible graph DFS and BPE.
iLriQtxnAA.problem: Existing molecular foundation models rely on modality-specific encoders for chemical versus biological molecules, and unified atom-level scaling laws remain underexplored.
iLriQtxnAA.method: MolToken maps small molecules, peptides, proteins, DNA, and RNA into an atom-level graph space, serializes them with strictly reversible Frequency Dual Depth First Search (FDDFS), compresses sequences via BPE into a shared vocabulary, and pre-trains a single autoregressive Transformer.
iLriQtxnAA.key_idea: Applies strictly reversible Frequency Dual Depth First Search serialization and BPE compression to tokenize five chemical and biological domains into one atom-level vocabulary.
iLriQtxnAA.evidence: Joint versus single-domain pre-training scaling-law experiments across model and data scales plus out-of-sample compute extrapolation and downstream evaluations.
iLriQtxnAA.claimed_gains: BPE reduces the total length of FDDFS sequences by a factor of approximately 71.8.
iLriQtxnAA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean, strictly reversible atom-level tokenization that compresses macromolecular sequences into tractable lengths across five domains.
iLriQtxnAA.main_concern: Reviewers argue the cross-domain comparison relies on unnormalized per-BPE-token NLL (producing near-tautological out-of-support losses), that joint training does not improve in-domain protein/DNA loss, and that scaling fits and downstream results are weak.

fUkvZl6Lfp.one_liner: Formulates contract-conditioned feedback admission for self-improving agents and adapts a span-level eligibility model with human supervision.
fUkvZl6Lfp.problem: Self-improving LLM agents often persist feedback based on local task success alone, which fails to verify whether evidence supports reuse under target persistence contracts.
fUkvZl6Lfp.method: The authors define target-conditioned update eligibility, evaluate a contract-conditioned Span-PRM against construction labels, human judgments, and counterfactual audits—exposing a fixed-contract ranking shortcut—and introduce human-supervised Span-PRM-H for feedback admission and 7B agent fine-tuning data selection.
fUkvZl6Lfp.key_idea: Conditions feedback admission on explicit persistence and reuse contracts and adapts a span-level eligibility model with human supervision to filter agent training data.
fUkvZl6Lfp.evidence: Controlled contract interventions, human-majority comparisons (120 pairs), retrospective Challenge evaluation (300 items), and 7B agent fine-tuning across 80 held-out tasks and three seeds.
fUkvZl6Lfp.claimed_gains: Span-PRM-H retains 70/78 eligible Challenge items with 4/222 ineligible admissions (+24.4 pp retention over contract-specific calibration), and its 7B fine-tuning selection reaches 42.917% success (+10.833 pp over matched random and +8.750 pp over Success-only).
fUkvZl6Lfp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that target-conditioned update eligibility is a timely and meaningful framing for long-term memory management in self-improving agents.
fUkvZl6Lfp.main_concern: Reviewers highlight that the base Span-PRM fails completely on fresh human evaluations and counterfactual audits, and question the practical takeaways and online-memory benefits over Write-All.

FIBl1ZH31K.one_liner: Disentangles expert identity, layer quotas, coverage, and local rank in routing-guided DoRA adaptation of MoE models under parameter budgets.
FIBl1ZH31K.problem: Budgeted low-rank adaptation of MoE models conflates expert selection, per-layer capacity quotas, coverage, and local rank, obscuring what drives accuracy gains.
FIBl1ZH31K.method: Using Native Router-Guided Layer-Expert Capacity Allocation (NRG) with reference-answer-free routing profiles and static DoRA adapters, the authors run budget-matched, fixed-rank, random-subset, and uniform-layer-quota controls to separate capacity allocation from expert identity.
FIBl1ZH31K.key_idea: Separates budget-matched coverage-rank trade-offs from fixed-rank expert identity and uniform-layer-quota controls when evaluating routing-guided MoE DoRA adaptation.
FIBl1ZH31K.evidence: Empirical study on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base across low-data VCR and NLVR2 settings with grouped intervals and exclusion probes.
FIBl1ZH31K.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, selected rank-32 adapters exceed budget-matched all-expert adapters by 0.83–0.90 pp across three VCR and NLVR2 settings, while on VCR Train50 selected rank-7 falls 0.90 points below all-expert rank-7 and raising rank on selected experts yields +1.77 points.
FIBl1ZH31K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the careful experimental decomposition of coverage, local rank, layer quotas, and expert identity as well as transparent reporting of limitations.
FIBl1ZH31K.main_concern: Reviewers point to unresolved execution discrepancies between historical and newly trained runs, narrow evaluation (one backbone, two small datasets), and inconclusive controls.

tw9ZH6HHxO.one_liner: Estimates per-task RL learnability from a short probe run and two endpoint evaluations to weight LLM post-training tasks.
tw9ZH6HHxO.problem: RL post-training task selectors rely on snapshot solvability (pass rate), ignoring that equally solvable tasks differ in how positively they respond to continued training.
tw9ZH6HHxO.method: The paper defines regime-conditional task learnability and proposes TrajVal, which runs a short probe and two endpoint evaluations to estimate per-task reward gain. TrajVal serves either as a standalone static sampling prior or as a multiplicative prior for online schedulers.
tw9ZH6HHxO.key_idea: Approximates per-task RL learnability from short-horizon probe reward gains to statically or multiplicatively weight training tasks.
tw9ZH6HHxO.evidence: Reward-trajectory analyses and experiments on mathematical and logical reasoning benchmarks across multiple model scales and online schedulers (BOTS, GRESO).
tw9ZH6HHxO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find distinguishing task learnability from snapshot solvability intuitive and appreciate the plug-in evaluation across domains and schedulers.
tw9ZH6HHxO.main_concern: Reviewers note that efficiency metrics omit substantial probe-training and scoring costs, gains in Table 1 are marginal, and the heuristic formulation feels somewhat circular with limited baseline comparisons.

bNIp76Vdqd.one_liner: Point cloud Transformer combining dual-branch Bilateral Context Attention with modernized spatial proximity, raw-point embedding, and pooling.
bNIp76Vdqd.problem: Existing point cloud Transformers using standard Softmax attention struggle to synergistically capture local geometric structures and semantic context.
bNIp76Vdqd.method: LoCoFormer introduces Bilateral Context Attention (BCA), which uses separate geometric and semantic context branches with bilateral fusion to modulate attention weights and inject geometric priors. It also modernizes spatial proximity serialization, sparse-convolution raw-point embedding, and partition-based pooling.
bNIp76Vdqd.key_idea: Pairs dual-branch geometric-semantic Bilateral Context Attention with serialized spatial proximity, sparse-convolution embedding, and partition pooling.
bNIp76Vdqd.evidence: Evaluated on ModelNet40 shape classification and indoor segmentation benchmarks (S3DIS, ScanNet v2, ScanNet200 per reviews) with component ablations.
bNIp76Vdqd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note consistent empirical improvements over selected baselines on indoor point-cloud benchmarks and clear component ablations.
bNIp76Vdqd.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty (reusing PTv2/PTv3 serialization, pooling, and sparse embeddings), underspecified tensor dimensions in BCA equations, missing recent baselines, and no outdoor-scene tests.

bpOmYif9u7.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM agent memory poisoning across persistence, downstream execution consequences, and selective repair over 310 cases.
bpOmYif9u7.problem: Existing agent memory security evaluations rarely trace a single malicious memory through persistence, downstream action execution, and selective benign-preserving repair across diverse backends.
bpOmYif9u7.method: MemSecBench evaluates 310 task-grounded cases across 48 contexts under a controlled Write-Execute-Forget protocol spanning a 24-configuration matrix (two harnesses, four memory backends, three LLMs). Adjudication combines deterministic write checks, checkpoint-specific judge models, and programmatic gates across seven lifecycle checkpoints.
bpOmYif9u7.key_idea: Tracks agent memory poisoning across a unified Write-Execute-Forget lifecycle using deterministic checks and checkpoint judges across 24 harness-memory-LLM configurations.
bpOmYif9u7.evidence: Evaluates 310 cases from 48 contexts across code/science, daily life, and office workflows over 24 system configurations, with human validation of judge checkpoints.
bpOmYif9u7.claimed_gains: Averaged across 24 configurations, malicious-memory persistence rate is 84.2% and full Write-Execute success rate is 50.3%.
bpOmYif9u7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the lifecycle framing linking memory persistence to verified downstream consequences and benign-preserving repair across backends is timely and well-structured.
bpOmYif9u7.main_concern: Reviewers highlight brittle LLM-judge reliability at the repair checkpoint (24 of 64 human-labeled repair failures misclassified as successes, 79.06% balanced accuracy) and limited scientific novelty.

MFUekSylcy.one_liner: Reformulates GUI visual grounding as box-supervised pixel-level executable-region mask prediction with deterministic click extraction.
MFUekSylcy.problem: Single-point coordinate supervision ignores spatially extended valid click areas, while patch-based scoring is constrained to coarse visual-token grids on dense GUI controls.
MFUekSylcy.method: Seg2Click trains a multimodal segmentation head with bounding-box supervision to predict a sub-token pixel-level executable-region mask in a single forward pass without verifiers or zoom-in passes. A deterministic rule then extracts the final click coordinate from the predicted mask.
MFUekSylcy.key_idea: Predicts sub-token pixel-level executable action masks from bounding-box supervision in one pass and deterministically converts the mask to a click point.
MFUekSylcy.evidence: Evaluated across five backbone configurations from two model families on ScreenSpot, ScreenSpot-v2, and ScreenSpot-Pro with matched-backbone comparisons.
MFUekSylcy.claimed_gains: Seg2Click-9B achieves 92.06% on ScreenSpot, 94.10% on ScreenSpot-v2, and 55.22% on ScreenSpot-Pro, outperforming coordinate generation and patch-based grounding on matched backbones.
MFUekSylcy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree predicting sub-token action masks in a single pass is a clean, practical representation for dense GUI controls with solid controlled grounding results.
MFUekSylcy.main_concern: Reviewers note moderate architectural novelty over MLLMSeg/PixelLM, reliance on static box-hit accuracy without interactive GUI agent evaluation, and rectangular boxes poorly approximating irregular controls.

iJrmHpl2M2.one_liner: Adaptively gates world-action-model rollout depth using a latent risk evaluator trained with a counterfactual driving dataset.
iJrmHpl2M2.problem: World Action Models allocate a fixed imagination rollout horizon to every driving scene regardless of scene risk or planning benefit.
iJrmHpl2M2.method: RISE adds a Latent Evaluator that estimates prefix risk and expected planning gain from continued imagination, paired with a Rollout Gate that makes sequential Roll/Stop decisions against compute cost. To supervise diverse hazard outcomes, the authors build CounterDrive, an expert-verified counterfactual driving dataset.
iJrmHpl2M2.key_idea: Makes sequential Roll/Stop imagination decisions by weighing latent-evaluated risk and expected planning benefit against rollout compute, trained with counterfactual hazard clips.
iJrmHpl2M2.evidence: Evaluated on NAVSIM (v1 and v2) and nuScenes, plus plug-in transfer across WAM architectures (including DAWN) and ablations.
iJrmHpl2M2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree adaptive imagination depth is a practical problem and that RISE improves planning metrics while reducing latency over fixed-depth rollouts.
iJrmHpl2M2.main_concern: Reviewers note modest single-seed gains without matched-compute learned horizon baselines, planner-specific training coupling, and limited documentation of CounterDrive's split hygiene and synthetic-risk validity.

jHr6Oay80d.one_liner: Synthesizes four-level preference rankings via modality-guided decoding and optimizes omni-modal LLMs with hierarchical margins and token reweighting.
jHr6Oay80d.problem: Binary preference optimization for omni-modal LLMs overlooks intermediate cross-modal hallucination states, yielding sparse supervision for complex audio-visual conflicts.
jHr6Oay80d.method: H-MPO uses an annotation-free Modality-Guided Decoding pipeline to synthesize four-level preference rankings of decreasing modality faithfulness from the model itself. It then optimizes the hierarchy using asymmetric margin constraints alongside token-level reweighting for modality-sensitive tokens.
jHr6Oay80d.key_idea: Generates annotation-free four-tier preference rankings via modality-guided logit decoding and trains with asymmetric hierarchical margins and modality-sensitive token weights.
jHr6Oay80d.evidence: Evaluated on cross-modal hallucination benchmarks and general audio-visual perception and reasoning tasks across two model sizes.
jHr6Oay80d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the annotation-free modality-guided data pipeline is practical and that H-MPO reduces cross-modal hallucinations without harming general perception.
jHr6Oay80d.main_concern: Reviewers note the four-level preference ordering is unvalidated by humans or judges (and the loss does not enforce r3 > r4), token reweighting may confound content-word POS bias, and training queries lack joint audio-video coverage.

k9S1Xlc5Az.one_liner: Trains lightweight receiver-conditioned gates to dynamically blend next-token predictions from frozen donor LLMs at decoding time.
k9S1Xlc5Az.problem: Adapting LLMs to new reasoning or alignment capabilities typically requires costly post-training or parameter-efficient fine-tuning of task-specific weights.
k9S1Xlc5Az.method: Mixture of Outputs (MoO) keeps both the receiver LLM and one or more specialized donor LLMs frozen, training only a lightweight gating module that maps the receiver's hidden state at each decoding step to independent donor contribution weights for next-token prediction.
k9S1Xlc5Az.key_idea: Uses a trained lightweight gate conditioned on the frozen receiver's hidden state to weight frozen donor next-token logits at every decoding step.
k9S1Xlc5Az.evidence: Evaluated across eight reasoning benchmarks (Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Qwen Base) and alignment transfer on Qwen and Llama, including multi-donor fusion over three gate-training seeds.
k9S1Xlc5Az.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-Math-7B, single-donor MoO raises 8-benchmark reasoning average from 48.36% to 56.82%, reduces attack success rate from 0.44 to 0.02 (Qwen) and 1.00 to 0.17 (Llama), and multi-donor fusion adds 2.01 and 1.92 points over best single-donor on Qwen Base and Qwen Math.
k9S1Xlc5Az.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree MoO provides a clean, lightweight compositional mechanism for reusing frozen donor models without modifying base weights.
k9S1Xlc5Az.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing reproducibility details (gate-training datasets, cross-vocabulary projection, safety scoring) and missing decoding-fusion baselines on reasoning tasks.

e77Ol7d9h2.one_liner: Masks redundant RL actions online via distributional equivalence hypothesis testing integrating aleatoric return spread and ensemble epistemic uncertainty.
e77Ol7d9h2.problem: Action redundancy inflates RL exploration spaces, yet transition-based equivalence is too strict and mean-based equivalence ignores risk and finite-sample estimation uncertainty.
e77Ol7d9h2.method: Distributional Action Equivalence Testing (DAET) formulates equivalence as statistical hypothesis testing over return distributions incorporating both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. DAET-Mask operationalizes this online by pairing a distributional RL backbone with Deep Ensembles to gate out statistically equivalent redundant actions.
e77Ol7d9h2.key_idea: Combines distributional RL return quantiles with Deep Ensemble epistemic uncertainty to statistically test and mask redundant actions online.
e77Ol7d9h2.evidence: Theoretical preservation analysis plus experiments on diagnostic GridWorld environments (10 seeds) and a 100-warehouse industrial RMFS setting (per abstract and reviews).
e77Ol7d9h2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree casting action equivalence as a distributional, uncertainty-aware statistical test is well-motivated and clearly distinguishes aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty.
e77Ol7d9h2.main_concern: Reviewers note mismatches between theoretical probability transfer and implemented renormalization, discrepancies between the described PPO method and released RMFS code, narrow empirical scope, and uncalibrated ensemble uncertainty.

a56QlXMxEk.one_liner: Infers cold-start GUI user preferences by comparing sparse interaction history against context-matched population alternatives.
a56QlXMxEk.problem: Sparse GUI interaction histories confound transferable user preferences with task, interface, or temporary context constraints.
a56QlXMxEk.method: SAIL compares each historical user action against plausible population alternatives in the same context, aggregates the resulting deviations into a compact probabilistic user state, and applies query-conditioned residual corrections to population predictions.
a56QlXMxEk.key_idea: Extracts transferable user tendencies by aggregating deviations between historical actions and context-matched population alternatives into a probabilistic residual user state.
a56QlXMxEk.evidence: Evaluated on FingerTip 20K (including held-out users and matched-budget controls), Persona2Web, and controlled adverse-history tests.
a56QlXMxEk.claimed_gains: On FingerTip 20K, SAIL improves User Macro Sim1 by 7.48 points over prior history baselines, retains a 1.61-point gain under strict matched controls, and reaches 43.25% GUI execution success.
a56QlXMxEk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree interpreting sparse user history relative to population context is a valuable perspective with sound closed-form posterior derivations and useful controls.
a56QlXMxEk.main_concern: Reviewers report that the self-fitting support loss causes precision saturation making 'what to personalize' inert, gains over matched controls are small (1–2 points), and notation/baseline specifications are unclear.

XqVrdVt1C1.one_liner: Benchmarks multimodal table-to-report generation across 386 tasks using MCTS-curated references and dual text-and-visualization judge models.
XqVrdVt1C1.problem: Existing table-to-report benchmarks focus on single modalities, simplistic fluency metrics, or omit chart fidelity, numerical grounding, and analytical novelty.
XqVrdVt1C1.method: MM-ReportBench comprises 386 tasks over 185 real-world tables paired with expert-curated reference reports built via MCTS generation and human QC. A dual-judge framework pairs a Text Judge (completeness, numerical fact-checking, novelty) with a Visualization Judge (fidelity, expressiveness, aesthetics, correctness) plus cross-modal consistency checks.
XqVrdVt1C1.key_idea: Combines MCTS-and-human curated table-to-report references with separate text and visualization judges that verify numerical grounding, novelty, and cross-modal consistency.
XqVrdVt1C1.evidence: Evaluates 20 models across 386 tasks from 185 real-world tables spanning six domains.
XqVrdVt1C1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree multimodal report generation from complex tables is a practically relevant, demanding task and appreciate the broad 20-model evaluation.
XqVrdVt1C1.main_concern: Reviewers note reliance on an outdated single judge (GPT-4o) without adversarial reward-hacking validation, insufficient differentiation from prior benchmarks (e.g., InsightBench, DataNarrative), and unclear metric definitions.

uzxKdWz75q.one_liner: Performs training-free one-shot federated learning by transferring shared cross-class covariance structure with text-anchored classification.
uzxKdWz75q.problem: Statistics-based one-shot federated learning estimates per-class covariances independently and shrinks scarce classes toward isotropic targets, discarding covariance structure shared across classes under a frozen encoder.
uzxKdWz75q.method: TACO aggregates per-class sufficient statistics from a frozen pre-trained encoder in a single round without local training, achieving partition invariance. It regularizes scarce class covariances via Structural Covariance Transfer (SCT) using shared cross-class covariance patterns, combined with text-space fusion and test-time augmentation (per abstract and reviews).
uzxKdWz75q.key_idea: Regularizes scarce per-class covariances in training-free one-shot federated learning by shrinking toward a shared cross-class covariance target rather than an isotropic matrix.
uzxKdWz75q.evidence: Evaluated across multiple datasets (including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet), pre-trained encoders, rotation tests, and ablations (per abstract and reviews).
uzxKdWz75q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree TACO is clearly written, partition-invariant, and that cross-class structural covariance transfer improves over standard isotropic shrinkage.
uzxKdWz75q.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over classical covariance shrinkage, note small gains from text fusion (with large gains driven by CTTA not applied to baselines), and point out balanced-class benchmarks do not test adaptive weighting.

B7FdBkvp00.one_liner: Benchmarks adaptive multi-agent social strategies in deterministic executable environments and evaluates trace-grounded decision-analysis reports.
B7FdBkvp00.problem: LLM social-simulation benchmarks focus on role-play realism rather than testing whether agents employ adaptive social strategies or whether simulation traces improve decision analysis.
B7FdBkvp00.method: The authors build an executable benchmark spanning social-media and commercial-negotiation environments with private goals, visibility constraints, and deterministic transitions, scoring agents via rule-based outcomes and five LLM-as-a-Judge dimensions. They also study a workflow converting simulation traces into conditional decision reports with triggers, alternatives, trade-offs, and exit conditions.
B7FdBkvp00.key_idea: Combines deterministic-transition social environments with a simulation-to-decision workflow that distills execution traces into structured conditional decision reports.
B7FdBkvp00.evidence: Evaluates LLMs across social-media and commercial-negotiation environments with rule-based metrics, LLM judges, post-hoc strategy analysis, and report-generation ablations.
B7FdBkvp00.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the deterministic executable environments with explicit private goals and visibility rules enable auditable evaluation and well-controlled report ablations.
B7FdBkvp00.main_concern: Reviewers note that simulation-grounded reports do not consistently beat structured scenario-only reports, benchmark metrics do not directly measure strategy, and human judge validation is small and statistically weak.

xNJG1AxqZF.one_liner: Decomposes multi-agent backdoors into benign tool-poisoned primitives assembled at runtime through cross-agent collaboration.
xNJG1AxqZF.problem: Single-agent backdoor threat models overlook collaborative multi-agent systems where role-specific tool access and cross-agent orchestration create distributed attack surfaces.
xNJG1AxqZF.method: The authors design a distributed backdoor attack that splits malicious behavior into independently benign, tool-poisoned primitives and assembles them at collaboration time through the integration and orchestration layer. They also build a multi-role collaborative task benchmark and sandbox to evaluate the threat.
xNJG1AxqZF.key_idea: Splits a backdoor into benign tool-poisoned primitives across roles and dynamically assembles the payload at runtime via cross-agent orchestration.
xNJG1AxqZF.evidence: Evaluated across five LLMs and three multi-agent benchmarks (including MultiAgentBench and a new multi-role sandbox benchmark, per abstract and reviews).
xNJG1AxqZF.claimed_gains: Achieves an attack success rate exceeding 95% while broadly preserving task accuracy.
xNJG1AxqZF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper highlights an important security risk in multi-agent tool and runtime orchestration beyond model weights.
xNJG1AxqZF.main_concern: Reviewers argue the threat model is overly strong (assuming full tool/runtime control and hand-crafted trigger instructions), novelty over prior distributed backdoors like DemonAgent is unclear, and defenses are barely discussed.

74LmPcsNc0.one_liner: Decouples EEG diagnosis from anatomy by fusing a fixed scalp spectral expert with a deformed source-space dynamics model.
74LmPcsNc0.problem: Sensor-space EEG models preserve diagnostic accuracy without anatomical interpretability, while source-space models provide anatomy at the cost of predictive signal.
74LmPcsNc0.method: DMD-EEG keeps a fixed scalp spectral expert for diagnosis and models a separate source-space disease representation as a low-rank, sparse, iterative deformation of a healthy neural-dynamics prior over a 46-ROI x 5-frequency x 4-lag coordinate system. The two branches combine only at a fixed decision level.
74LmPcsNc0.key_idea: Architecturally decouples a scalp spectral diagnostic expert from a source-space low-rank iterative deformation of a healthy ROI-frequency-lag dynamics prior, fusing only at the decision level.
74LmPcsNc0.evidence: Evaluated on major depressive disorder (MDD), first-episode psychosis (FEP), and Parkinson's disease (PD) with subject-level holdout, occlusion, and transfer analyses.
74LmPcsNc0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating diagnostic accuracy from an explicit anatomical-spectral source representation is well-motivated and evaluated with careful subject-level controls.
74LmPcsNc0.main_concern: Reviewers note that high per-fold variance on small cohorts obscures performance gaps, simple decision-level fusion rarely improves over the stronger single expert, and methodological novelty is limited.

rlj9KWzi9l.one_liner: Converts 1-bit worker momentum sign votes into adaptive distributed SGD step magnitudes scaled by coordinate-wise vote margin.
rlj9KWzi9l.problem: One-bit momentum-sign optimizers cut distributed communication overhead but discard gradient magnitudes, degrading optimization quality compared to full-precision AdamW.
rlj9KWzi9l.method: AdasignSGD transmits one sign bit per coordinate per worker, uses the majority sign for update direction, and uses the worker vote margin via a lookup table to scale per-coordinate step magnitudes, taking larger steps where workers strongly agree.
rlj9KWzi9l.key_idea: Sets distributed update direction from majority 1-bit worker momentum signs and scales per-coordinate step magnitudes by the worker vote agreement margin.
rlj9KWzi9l.evidence: C4 language-model pretraining across 13 model and budget settings (60M to 1B parameters) plus systems timing benchmarks on 32 H200 and 128 P100 GPUs.
rlj9KWzi9l.claimed_gains: Matches AdamW perplexity at 1B while achieving a 1.46x complete-step speedup over fused AdamW on 32 H200 GPUs, 14.1% of FP32 dense-DDP traffic at 128 workers, and a 4.39x speedup on 128 P100 GPUs for a 350M model.
rlj9KWzi9l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree recovering adaptive step magnitudes from 1-bit vote margins is an elegant idea supported by a broad model-budget grid and concrete communication implementation.
rlj9KWzi9l.main_concern: Reviewers point out that quality and speed benchmarks use mismatched batch/precision/worker configurations (lacking unified time-to-target runs) and that the favorable 1B result uses a shorter token-per-parameter budget.

LFDHAs1nb4.one_liner: Adapts the NLP Autointerpretability Score to vision SAEs and tests its correlation with human judgments and LRH proxy metrics.
LFDHAs1nb4.problem: Vision sparse autoencoders are commonly evaluated by proxy metrics like sparsity or dictionary coherence without verifying whether they align with human concept perception.
LFDHAs1nb4.method: The authors adapt the Autointerpretability Score (AIS) to vision SAEs using a patch-captioning pipeline, validate it via a dedicated user study, and benchmark it against standard Linear Representation Hypothesis proxies across SAE families, vision encoders, and datasets.
LFDHAs1nb4.key_idea: Adapts Autointerpretability Score to vision via patch-level captioning and correlates it against human judgments and standard sparsity/coherence SAE metrics.
LFDHAs1nb4.evidence: User study plus benchmarking across 3 SAE families, 3 vision backbones, and 3 datasets comparing AIS against sparsity, coherence, and OOD metrics.
LFDHAs1nb4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree benchmarking vision SAE interpretability proxies against a human-validated behavioral metric is timely and reveals striking disagreements between standard metrics and AIS.
LFDHAs1nb4.main_concern: Reviewers point out that evaluated SAEs are barely sparse (up to 50% active latents), the 4x4 captioning grid and positive-only 5-exemplar AIS pipeline lack sensitivity ablations, and patch activations mix global attention context.

MBNSuXmq2n.one_liner: Diagnoses embodied-adaptation spatial localization loss in MoE VLMs as reversible re-aiming and recovers it via joint task-format supervision.
MBNSuXmq2n.problem: Supervised fine-tuning of sparse MoE VLMs for embodied reasoning severely degrades spatial localization even while preserving general vision-language capabilities.
MBNSuXmq2n.method: Through prompt rephrasing and trajectory-update subtraction/addition interventions, the authors show localization loss reflects reversible re-aiming rather than erasure. They propose Joint Spatial Re-Aiming (JSR), applying joint supervision over affected spatial tasks and their required output formats.
MBNSuXmq2n.key_idea: Restores adaptation-degraded spatial localization in MoE VLMs via small-budget supervised fine-tuning jointly covering affected spatial tasks and required response formats.
MBNSuXmq2n.evidence: Diagnostic interventions and JSR repair experiments on two MoE VLM backbones (including Qwen3.5) with task- and format-subset ablations.
MBNSuXmq2n.claimed_gains: Restores spatial localization performance with only 384 examples and 32 training steps (as stated in the TL;DR).
MBNSuXmq2n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that documenting spatial localization degradation during embodied fine-tuning and demonstrating its low-budget recoverability is practically useful.
MBNSuXmq2n.main_concern: Reviewers view JSR as standard SFT over a task-format mixture with limited novelty over prior spurious-forgetting work, note a missing pre-adaptation control, and find no mechanistic explanation for why localization specifically degrades.

nsi6beQLbn.one_liner: Combines conformal latent-reward uncertainty sets with pessimistic preference optimization for finite-sample DPO guarantees.
nsi6beQLbn.problem: Direct Preference Optimization overfits to noisy or limited preference datasets when treating all observed preference labels as equally reliable.
nsi6beQLbn.method: LatentCP-DPO constructs finite-sample marginal-coverage uncertainty sets for latent relative rewards from conformal prediction sets on Bradley-Terry pairwise or Plackett-Luce ranking feedback. It then learns a policy by maximizing the worst-case expected preference log-likelihood over these uncertainty sets using unlabeled prompt-response samples.
nsi6beQLbn.key_idea: Maximizes worst-case preference log-likelihood over conformal uncertainty sets of latent relative rewards using an independent unlabeled prompt-response set.
nsi6beQLbn.evidence: Finite-sample policy suboptimality upper bounds and a matching BT lower bound, plus empirical PL ranking experiments on Nectar (per abstract and reviews).
nsi6beQLbn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree combining conformal prediction with pessimistic DPO is a statistically grounded approach with a thorough finite-sample theoretical analysis.
nsi6beQLbn.main_concern: Reviewers note that pairwise accuracy barely improves over standard DPO, experiments cover only one dataset (PL setting, no BT validation) without component ablations, and guarantees assume correctly specified preference models.

Mu84EVClyD.one_liner: Controlled UPMAS harness varies irreducible evidence uncertainty to measure uncertainty loss across multi-agent LLM hand-offs.
Mu84EVClyD.problem: In multi-agent LLM systems, the agent observing uncertain evidence often differs from the acting agent, causing uncertainty to disappear across hand-offs.
Mu84EVClyD.method: The authors design a controlled experimental framework implemented in the UPMAS dataset where only the irreducible uncertainty of one piece of external evidence varies while everything else stays fixed. They trace numerical uncertainty quantification metrics and message content across agent hand-offs to causally attribute behavioral changes to upstream uncertainty.
Mu84EVClyD.key_idea: Hold all task variables fixed while varying only irreducible evidence uncertainty across controlled multi-agent hand-offs to isolate upstream uncertainty loss.
Mu84EVClyD.evidence: Evaluated across three open-weight models on the UPMAS dataset using uncertainty quantification metrics and message-level content analysis.
Mu84EVClyD.claimed_gains: Agents omit uncertainty information three times as often after the first hand-off as before (37% against 11%), while uncertainty metrics barely react and fade within a few steps.
Mu84EVClyD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled experimental design that isolates irreducible external uncertainty and clearly frames vanishing uncertainty in multi-agent systems.
Mu84EVClyD.main_concern: The paper only diagnoses the failure in homogeneous single-model harnesses without proposing a mitigation, and reviewers question whether the metrics and indirect path-level measurements capture uncertainty at the final action.

v8AxgqLYIt.one_liner: Refines a three-level hierarchical video memory via scale-aligned multi-agent localization and targeted multimodal observations.
v8AxgqLYIt.problem: Long-video understanding struggles because query-driven exploration suffers localization errors while query-independent memory construction misses question-specific fine details.
v8AxgqLYIt.method: VideoTapestry is a training-free framework that assigns specialized agents to three preconstructed hierarchical memory levels (global narrative, event structure, relational evidence) to revisit query-relevant video regions, enrich layer-wise memories with targeted observations, and assemble a composite query-adaptive memory.
v8AxgqLYIt.key_idea: Assigns scale-aligned agents to coarse-to-fine levels of a preconstructed hierarchical video memory to iteratively localize and enrich query-relevant branches with targeted observations.
v8AxgqLYIt.evidence: Evaluated on long-video understanding benchmarks against direct GPT-5.5 inference and prior frontier-backbone agentic methods, with component ablations.
v8AxgqLYIt.claimed_gains: Achieves absolute accuracy gains of 17.2%, 14.9%, and 9.8% (and an additional truncated benchmark) over direct GPT-5.5 inference.
v8AxgqLYIt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the coarse-to-fine scale-aligned multi-agent refinement over hierarchical video memory intuitive, clearly written, and well-motivated.
v8AxgqLYIt.main_concern: Reviewers criticize unfair baseline comparisons (different frontier backbones across methods and giving VideoTapestry hierarchical memory/ASR unavailable to the 50-frame Direct baseline), limited novelty over MemDreamer, and unreported token/latency costs.

452EEuwsUb.one_liner: Controlled event-definition comparisons and Definition-Contrastive Scoring (DeCoS) diagnose and reduce definition blindness in open-world video anomaly detection.
452EEuwsUb.problem: Existing open-world video anomaly detection protocols obscure definition blindness, where detectors assign nearly unchanged scores across different user definitions and still highlight excluded anomalies.
452EEuwsUb.method: The authors introduce a controlled evaluation protocol testing anomaly discrimination, detection under varying definitions, and multi-event selection, alongside Definition-Contrastive Scoring (DeCoS). DeCoS subtracts or reduces anomaly evidence shared across competing definitions to isolate definition-specific scores.
452EEuwsUb.key_idea: Contrasts anomaly evidence across competing definitions to suppress shared generic-anomaly scores and enforce definition following.
452EEuwsUb.evidence: Evaluates VAD systems and general vision-language models on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD with semantic, ablation, and multi-event analyses.
452EEuwsUb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing definition blindness versus generic anomaly detection is an important problem and that the three-dataset multi-model evaluation is thorough.
452EEuwsUb.main_concern: Reviewers question the clarity of presentation, the independent value of the proposed metrics over existing statistics, and the assumption that anomaly categories are mutually exclusive.
